audit.strategy: Audit U1 as a concrete algorithm (what energy, computed at which pyramid level, parametrised how, optimised from what initialisation) rather than as an aspiration, then test each design choice against the five failure modes using PHerc0268 numbers: level 0 8.64 um (1 mm = 116 vox), level 2 34.56 um (1 mm = 29 vox), level 3 69.1 um (1 mm = 14.5 vox, 4.3 GB), level 4 138 um (1 mm = 7.2 vox, 0.54 GB); winding pitch 0.3-0.6 mm = 4-9 vox at L3, only 2-4 vox at L4; sheet thickness 100-200 um = 1.5-3 vox at L3; scroll height 128 mm, field 105 mm. Keep the owner's intent (one global coordinate origin, radial search direction, winding numbers, bridging of damaged sections from undamaged ones, energy derived from the layered structure) and replace only the parts that fail: raw-intensity concentricity energy, C2-everywhere smoothness, point-per-slice certainty inside the crushed zone, hand-set or transferred stiffness, and silent interpolation. The replacement must run on 4 CPU / 15 GB / 1 GB disk + 11 GB /dev/shm with level 3 streamed slab-by-slab from S3, and every output must carry a per-z confidence and a per-z pass/fail from metrics that need no ground truth. Also cross-checked the existing fl4.py axis: it is a level-4 silhouette centroid (not level 3 as the project facts state; only the outer-radius ray uses level 3), which measures the outer envelope centre, not the winding centre, and has never been tested.
audit.summary_of_method_as_specified: U1 fits one axis curve c(z) = (x(z), y(z)) over the full 128 mm height as a cubic B-spline (a 'deformable tube' if a core radius is also fitted), minimising E = E_internal + E_external. E_internal penalises first and second derivatives of the control polygon (tension alpha, rigidity beta), so the curve is globally smooth (C2 everywhere). E_external is derived from the surrounding layered structure, in practice one of: concentric-ring/Hough evidence on CT intensity, a gradient-vector-flow field pulling toward the centre of curvature of the sheets, or a structure-tensor 'normals point at me' term. Optimisation is gradient descent (or dynamic programming) from an initialisation, which in this project would be the 19-point level-4 mask-centroid axis in tools/fl4/fl4.py. In the crushed middle of PHerc0268 the external term is weak or multi-modal, so the curve there is determined by E_internal, i.e. it interpolates smoothly between the 'clean' top and bottom segments ('bridging'). The output is a single point per z with no confidence, used downstream as the origin for radial rays, seed placement (r/R bands 0.15-0.35 in cmd_seeds_inner) and absolute winding-number assignment.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: C2 smoothness plus a weak/absent external term in the crushed zone turns 'bridging' into straight-line interpolation between the clean ends. A lateral displacement of the true winding centre inside the damaged zone (core slumped sideways, kinked at a fracture plane, or sheared between top and bottom) is removed by the prior, and the error is silent because the output carries no confidence.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Suppose the crushed zone spans z = 40-90 mm (L3 slices ~580-1300) and the innermost windings are displaced 4 mm from the chord between the clean ends. 4 mm = 7-13 winding pitches. Seeds placed at r = 0.15-0.35 R from the bridged axis land 7-13 windings off, absolute winding numbers are wrong by that amount for the whole middle third, and near the core the radial direction from the false axis is up to 90 degrees off the true sheet normal, so vc_grow_seg_from_seed is pushed tangentially into the neighbouring sheet. If the ends are twisted relative to each other, the interpolated middle is additionally rotated: no single straight-ish tube is correct anywhere between.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Point-per-slice topology. The spline asserts that at every z there is exactly one centre. A crushed core is flattened into an ellipse/slab or split into two or more lobes, each with its own centre of curvature; the external energy then has several minima and the snake either picks one lobe (a radial from it is tangential to the other lobe) or averages into a point that is the centre of nothing.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A core flattened to a 12 x 3 mm ellipse at L3 (174 x 43 vox): rays from the ellipse centroid along the long axis run almost parallel to the sheets for 5 mm and cross 0-2 sheets where the short-axis rays cross 10-20. Winding counting from that point is undefined, yet the pipeline reports an axis with full confidence and cmd_seeds_inner places seeds on it.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Non-convex energy, capture range limited to roughly one integration scale around the initialisation. Initialised from the level-4 silhouette centroid, the snake converges to the nearest local minimum, which for an off-centre core is not the winding centre.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: If the core sits 8 mm (58 L4 vox, 116 L3 vox) from the silhouette centroid, a GVF/structure-tensor force with 0.5-1 mm capture range never reaches it; the result is the centroid axis with a cosmetic wobble, i.e. exactly the untested fl4.py axis in a more convincing wrapper.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Tension/rigidity coefficients (alpha, beta) are a material model for the roll's axis. If set by hand or tuned on another object (PHerc0257, an intact roll; En-Gedi parchment, which is stiffer and rolls regularly; organiser umbilici of other scrolls), they encode the wrong mechanics. Carbonised papyrus fails brittly: the axis has kinks (C0) at fracture planes and jumps at delaminations, which a C2 B-spline can only represent by a long bend with overshoot.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A 15-degree kink of the core over 2 mm at a fracture plane, smoothed with a 10 mm bend, misplaces the axis by ~1.3 mm (2-4 pitches) over 10 mm of z on both sides of the kink, pushing seed bands onto the wrong winding in a region that is otherwise clean and would have unrolled correctly.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: The level at which E_external is computed decides whether the 'layered structure' exists in the data at all. A 3-D GVF or Hough field over the full level-3 volume (4.3 G voxels x 3 float32 components = 51 GB) does not fit in 15 GB, so a full-volume snake as specified is only feasible at level 4, where the winding pitch is 2-4 voxels (at or below Nyquist) and sheets are 1 voxel or less: structure-tensor coherence collapses, the ring energy is noise, and the snake sees only the silhouette. Level 0 (2.2 TB) is out of the question.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Running the snake at L4 (928 x 760 x 760) returns an axis that tracks the mask centroid within a voxel everywhere, including the crushed zone, and a smooth low energy is reported as 'convergence'. At L3 the layering is visible (pitch 4-9 vox) but only if the volume is streamed in slabs with a 2-D/2.5-D energy; this is not what U1 specifies, and localisation is still limited to ~70 um until a local level-2 refinement is added for seed sites.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Scanner-ring decoy. CT ring artefacts are concentric about the reconstruction rotation centre, which is a perfectly straight, perfectly vertical line, i.e. the global minimiser of E_internal. Any concentricity or ring-Hough energy on raw intensity has a clean minimum there, and with a straightness prior it is preferred over the real, wobbly scroll axis.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: The reconstruction centre is near the field centre (x = y ~ 6072 at L0, ~759 at L3). If the scroll was mounted 5-10 mm off that point, U1 reports a straight axis 5-10 mm (10-30 windings) from the real one, with the lowest energy of any candidate, and nothing in the method can tell. The 'masked' volume adds a second decoy: the hard mask edge is the strongest gradient in the image and a GVF field is dominated by it, pulling the snake toward the silhouette centroid.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Local attractors: mineral inclusions (saturated uint8 blobs with very strong gradients), radial cracks (strong gradients whose normals are tangential), insect/dust debris and residual air pockets. A gradient-driven external term weights each voxel by its gradient magnitude, so a few bright artefacts near the current estimate outweigh thousands of low-contrast sheet voxels.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A 0.5 mm mineral grain 2 mm from the true core at z = 60 mm: its gradient energy exceeds the summed sheet-edge energy of the inner 5 windings at L3 (sheet contrast ~20-40 grey levels, grain edge ~200), so the snake bends toward the grain over a few mm of z and the local winding numbers shift by 3-4.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: The 'bridge from clean ends' rule is itself a memorised macro shape: it assumes damage is interior and both ends are clean, which is true of the scrolls with organiser umbilici and may be false here. Any learned initialiser or energy tuned on those organiser umbilici additionally memorises 'axis ~ silhouette centroid +- 2 mm, nearly straight'.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: If PHerc0268's crushed core reaches one end of the roll, the method extrapolates from a single clean end over 60+ mm with no warning; a centre regressor trained on PHerc0332/1667-style umbilici returns the centroid-like answer with high confidence exactly where the local physics (slumped core) contradicts it. The 'synthetic carbonised papyrus replicas' in the data plan would reinforce this unless their collapse modes are deliberately varied and unlike each other.

audit.hardened_alternative:
Name: evidence-weighted, piecewise-smooth axis with explicit confidence and explicit breaks (keeps U1's global curve, layered-structure energy and bridging; removes silent interpolation, intensity-ring decoys, C2-everywhere and transferred stiffness). All numbers are for PHerc0268.

Stage 0, decoy and artefact conditioning (level 3, streamed): read L3 (1855 x 1519 x 1519 uint8, 4.3 GB) in 16-slice slabs (1.1 mm, 37 MB each, 116 slabs) straight from the zarr; keep nothing on the 1 GB disk, scratch in /dev/shm. Per slab: erode the CT mask by 15 L3 vox (1 mm) so the mask edge never votes; mask intensities above the per-slab p99.5 dilated by 3 vox (mineral debris); subtract the angular mean about the reconstruction centre in polar coordinates (polar high-pass) so scanner rings carry no orientation signal.

Stage 1, layer-normal evidence (the 'layered structure' energy made robust): on the slab mean image (or each slice, tensors averaged), 2-D structure tensor with derivative sigma_d = 1.2 L3 vox (~80 um, half a sheet) and integration sigma_i = 5 L3 vox (~0.35 mm, about one pitch). Keep pixels with coherence >= 0.3. Each kept pixel p with unit normal n_p defines the line p + t n_p that must pass through the centre of local concentricity. This is a layer-level version of the U2 inversion at the scale where it actually works (fibres are invisible at 69 um; layers are not).

Stage 2, per-slab centre and multi-centre diagnostic: the centre c minimising the sum of w_p * dist(c, line_p)^2 is a 2 x 2 closed-form least squares; make it robust with Tukey-biweight IRLS (c = 0.5 mm = 7 L3 vox, 6 iterations). Then recompute the same estimate independently in 36 azimuth sectors x 3 radial bands (0.25-0.5 R, 0.5-0.85 R, plus the innermost 0.1-0.25 R) around the provisional centre. Slab outputs: robust centre, sector-centre MAD spread, angular coverage = fraction of sectors whose own centre is within 0.5 mm of the global one, number of clusters among the 108 sector centres (mean-shift, bandwidth 1 mm), median point-to-line residual. Confidence = coverage x (1 - clipped residual/0.5 mm). Slabs with >= 2 clusters each holding >= 25% of sectors are flagged multi-centre and their cluster centres are exported as mini-umbilici seeds for U3.

Stage 3, piecewise-smooth global curve: cubic B-spline x(z), y(z) with knots every 2 mm (29 L3 slices, ~64 knots), weighted least squares with slab weights = confidence, second-difference penalty lambda chosen by leave-one-slab-out cross-validation (never hand-set, never transferred from another scroll), Huber loss on residuals (IRLS). Break points: binary-segmentation/PELT change-point detection on the slab-centre sequence; a jump >= 1 mm sustained for >= 3 slabs with confidence >= 0.6 on both sides inserts a knot of multiplicity 3 at that z (C0, a true kink), never a smoothed bend. Crushed-zone rule: a run of >= 5 slabs with confidence < 0.3 is not fitted; the curve there is reported as the pair of one-sided extrapolations from the adjacent clean segments plus an envelope (their disagreement plus the slab spread), labelled 'bridged, confidence 0'. If the two extrapolations disagree by more than one pitch (0.5 mm) at the zone midpoint, the bridge is 'ambiguous' and downstream must not assign absolute winding numbers across it: winding numbers are then defined per segment, with U3 mini-umbilici inside the zone.

Stage 4, seed-site refinement (resolution gap): at every seed z used by cmd_seeds / cmd_seeds_inner, repeat Stages 1-2 in a 10 x 10 mm x 3-slice window at level 2 (290 x 290 px, a few chunks) to localise the centre to < 0.1 mm; also run it in 3 radial bands and refuse the seed if the bands disagree by > 0.3 mm.

Output: per L3 slice (x, y, confidence, coverage, residual_mm, n_centres, segment_id, flag in {clean, kink, multi-centre, bridged, ambiguous}) plus the knot list, break-point list, lambda and the validation table below. Downstream code must read the flag; the old umbilicus_xy(cps, z) interpolation is replaced by this table. Relation to the rest of the master model: Stage 1-2 is U2 done with layer normals at a feasible scale; Stage 2's cluster centres are U3's mini-umbilici; U1's global curve survives only where the evidence supports it.

validation_metrics.name: Sector coverage (M1)
validation_metrics.definition: Per slab, the fraction of 36 azimuth x 3 radial-band sectors whose independently estimated centre lies within 0.5 mm (one winding pitch) of the slab's global robust centre.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: >= 0.75 for every slab labelled 'clean'; any slab with coverage < 0.5 must carry a non-clean flag (label/evidence consistency is itself checked).
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Internal consistency only: the sector estimates are computed from disjoint pixel sets of the same slab at level 3; agreement among them is a property of a true centre of concentric layers, disagreement is a property of a false or non-unique one. No external reference needed.

validation_metrics.name: Normal-line residual (M2)
validation_metrics.definition: Median perpendicular distance, in mm, from the fitted axis point to the normal lines of all coherent (coherence >= 0.3) layer pixels in the slab.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: <= 0.35 mm (5 L3 vox) in 'clean' segments; reported as a curve along z, with the crushed zone expected to fail (that failure is the deliverable, not hidden).
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Computed from the structure-tensor normals at level 3 and the fitted curve; it measures how well the axis explains the observed sheet orientations, which is the physical definition of the umbilicus.

validation_metrics.name: Inner/outer band concentricity (M3)
validation_metrics.definition: Distance between the centre estimated from radial band 0.25-0.5 R and from 0.5-0.85 R, per slab.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: <= 0.3 mm in clean segments; a sustained larger offset flags a displaced core (physical, must be labelled, not averaged away).
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Two independent estimates from disjoint radial zones of the same slice; agreement is required for the roll to have a single centre at that z.

validation_metrics.name: Split-half reproducibility (M4)
validation_metrics.definition: Per slab, distance between the centre estimated from even slices and from odd slices (8 + 8 of 16).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: median <= 0.15 mm, p95 <= 0.4 mm over clean segments.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Standard split-half estimate of the statistical error of the centre; needs only the data.

validation_metrics.name: Azimuthal winding-count balance (M5)
validation_metrics.definition: At ~50 z-stations, cast 16 rays from the axis point to the eroded mask edge in a level-2 window and count sheet crossings (peaks of CT intensity and, independently, hit runs of the organiser surface-probability volume m7); metric = (max - min count)/mean count across azimuths and the absolute max-min difference.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: ratio <= 0.10 and max-min <= 2 windings in clean segments. Run the same test on the existing 19-point centroid axis: the new axis must be at least as balanced at every station, and it adjudicates between the two.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: A true centre sees the same number of windings in every direction; an offset d produces an imbalance of about 2d/pitch counts. Uses only the CT and an organiser product that is independent of the axis.

validation_metrics.name: Organiser normal-grid agreement (M6)
validation_metrics.definition: Median angle between the xy-projection of the organiser normal grid vectors and the radial direction to the fitted axis, sampled over the grid.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: <= 15 degrees in clean segments; regions > 30 degrees must be flagged non-radial and handed to U3.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: The organiser normals were produced by an independent method; agreement with the axis is a cross-method check, disagreement localises either a bad axis or genuinely non-concentric geometry, and M1-M3 distinguish the two.

validation_metrics.name: Decoy and artefact immunity (M7)
validation_metrics.definition: (a) Distance of the fitted axis from the reconstruction rotation centre along z; (b) axis shift when the polar high-pass is disabled; (c) axis shift after injecting synthetic concentric rings about a random off-centre point at the ring-artefact amplitude measured in air; (d) axis shift after injecting 20 synthetic saturated 0.5 mm blobs per slab at random positions within 3 mm of the axis.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: (a) FAIL if within 0.3 mm of the rotation centre for > 10 mm of z while the mask centroid is > 2 mm away; (b), (c), (d) shift <= 0.1 mm in clean segments.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Perturbation tests on the real volume: the correct axis must be invariant to artefacts we add ourselves, and the only thing that should be sensitive to scanner rings is a decoy-captured method.

validation_metrics.name: Smoothing sensitivity and break-point audit (M8)
validation_metrics.definition: Axis change under lambda/3 and 3 x lambda relative to the cross-validated lambda; and, for each inserted C0 knot, the sector-centre jump across it.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: <= 0.2 mm change in clean segments; every C0 knot must coincide with a sector-centre jump >= 1 mm with coverage >= 0.6 on both sides; zero knots allowed elsewhere; the list is delivered for human audit.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Sensitivity analysis of the fit and consistency between the break points and the per-slab evidence; both are internal to the method.

validation_metrics.name: Procedural phantom unit test (M9)
validation_metrics.definition: A self-generated 400^3 phantom at 69 um: spiral sheet with pitch 0.45 mm, thickness 0.15 mm, air gaps, a known curved/kinked axis, a crushed zone with two lobes, debris blobs, scanner rings about an off-centre point, noise matched to the PHerc0268 L3 histogram. Error of the recovered axis vs the known one, and the confidence assigned inside the two-lobe zone.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: <= 0.15 mm error in undamaged zones, kink localised within 1 mm, confidence <= 0.3 everywhere in the two-lobe zone (no false confidence). Explicitly a code-path test, not evidence of performance on the real scroll.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: The phantom's axis is known by construction; it is synthetic and must be reported as such, never substituted for M1-M8 on the real data.

audit.compute_estimate: Level 3 streamed from S3 in 116 slabs of 16 slices (37 MB each, 4.3 GB total): network-bound, roughly 10-40 min at 2-8 MB/s effective through the zarr chunk reader; nothing written to the 1 GB disk, scratch in /dev/shm (< 1 GB used, cleared per slab). Per slab: three Gaussian filters at 1519^2 and the structure tensor (~0.3 s), IRLS centre (6 iterations over ~1 M voters, ~0.5 s), 108 sector estimates (~0.5 s), polar high-pass (~0.3 s): ~2 s per slab, ~4 min total on 4 CPUs; peak RAM ~1 GB. Spline fit with cross-validated lambda and change-point detection: ~64 knots x 2 coords, seconds. Level-2 refinement and M5 ray tests at ~50 stations: each window touches 4-9 level-2 chunks (~10-20 MB), ~1 GB of reads total, ~5 min. Perturbation tests M7 (b)-(d) double the slab pass (~8 min). Phantom M9: 400^3 generation and processing, ~5 min. Total wall time about 1-1.5 h per full run, dominated by the download; can be split across the 7 sibling containers by z-range (each gets ~17 slabs, ~0.6 GB) with the spline fit done once on the merged slab table. Contrast: the method as specified (3-D GVF/Hough field over level 3) needs ~51 GB and is infeasible; at level 4 it fits (~6.5 GB) but is under-resolved.
audit.what_to_reject_outright: (1) A single globally C2 B-spline/snake whose output inside the crushed zone is presented as the umbilicus and used for absolute winding numbers or seed placement there; any 'bridge' delivered without a confidence value and an envelope, and any absolute winding numbering across a bridge whose two one-sided extrapolations disagree by more than one pitch. (2) Any external energy built from raw-intensity concentricity (ring Hough, GVF on the masked CT) that has not passed the scanner-rotation-centre decoy test and the mask-edge erosion, because its global minimum is the reconstruction axis. (3) Computing the layered-structure energy only at level 4 (138 um; pitch 2-4 voxels, aliased) or claiming a full-volume 3-D field at level 3 on this hardware (51 GB). (4) Tension/rigidity or any prior tuned on En-Gedi or other parchment (owner's toxic-data rule), on other scrolls' organiser umbilici, or on synthetic replicas with a single collapse style, and any learned centre regressor trained on a small library of umbilici (macro-shape memorisation). (5) Treating the existing fl4.py 19-point level-4 silhouette-centroid axis as validated or as the final initialisation without the M5 winding-balance test; it measures the outer envelope, not the winding centre, and the project facts mis-state its level. (6) Point-per-slice certainty where the sector analysis shows two or more centres: those z-ranges must be handed to U3 mini-umbilici, not averaged. (7) The 'tube radius' as a fitted quantity in collapsed-core regions, where no cavity exists.

refuted_claims.claim: Stage 2: Tukey-biweight IRLS (c = 0.5 mm = 7 L3 vox) on point-to-normal-line distance gives a robust centre, and the 0.35 mm residual (M2) / 0.5 mm sector agreement (M1) thresholds define 'clean' slabs.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Normals concur at a point only for circles. For nested similar ellipses of aspect a/b the normals envelope the evolute (astroid with cusps at rho*(a^2-b^2)/a on the major axis and rho*(a^2-b^2)/b on the minor axis); at 45 deg a normal misses the centre by rho*(a^2-b^2)/(sqrt2*sqrt(a^2+b^2)). PHerc0268's own silhouette at z-fraction 0.5 (logs/fl4/seeds_inner_PHerc0268.json outer radii: diameters 7670-9900 L0 vox = 66-86 mm by azimuth) has aspect ~1.29, so layer normals at rho = 20 mm miss the centre by ~5.5 mm, at rho = 5 mm by ~1.4 mm; a crushed core is more eccentric still. Even the scan tilt alone (fl4 centroid drifts 11 mm in y over the middle 70 mm, ~9 deg) makes z-sections elliptical with caustic 0.25-0.4 mm at rho 20-30 mm, comparable to c. Consequences, all fatal: (i) with c smaller than the caustic the biweight zeroes the layer lines and converges onto the evolute, up to (a^2-b^2)/a * rho = 15 mm from the centre, i.e. it is captured by a geometric decoy exactly like the snake it replaces; (ii) M2 residuals are 1-10 mm so confidence = coverage*(1 - residual/0.5 mm) = 0 for the whole roll and the entire scroll is labelled 'bridged' (the method delivers nothing); (iii) sector centres split into two clusters (flat-side normals near the far minor-axis cusp, end normals near the major-axis cusps), so an intact eccentric roll is exported to U3 as two mini-umbilici. The circular M9 phantom (R <= 13 mm) cannot detect this.
refuted_claims.fix: Replace point concurrency with a concentric-conic normal-field model n(p) proportional to Q(p - c): the constraint n x Q(p-c) = 0 is linear in (Q, Qc), 5 parameters, closed-form LS per slab and per radial band (aspect varies with radius in a crushed roll); robustify on the ANGULAR residual (angle between n and Q(p-c)) with a coarse-to-fine schedule 30 -> 10 -> 5 deg, never on a 0.5 mm distance; report c, Q (aspect, orientation), median angular residual; derive confidence from angular residual and band agreement on c. Validate first on 2-D phantoms of aspect 1.0, 1.3, 2.0 at rho up to 40 mm.

refuted_claims.claim: 36 azimuth x 3 radial-band sector centres with 'coverage' = fraction within 0.5 mm of the global centre, pass >= 0.75; mean-shift at 1 mm bandwidth declares multi-centre slabs.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Within a 10 deg sector the normal lines are nearly parallel; the intersection is conditioned as sigma_perp / sin(10 deg) ~ 5.8 sigma_perp along the mean normal. With realistic lateral error 0.1-0.2 mm (sheet waviness, mm-scale buckles, plus the spiral's own constant P/(2 pi) = 0.05-0.1 mm normal offset) the sector centre's radial error is 0.6-1.2 mm > 0.5 mm, so a perfect circular roll fails M1, and the 108 elongated error ellipses cluster spuriously along radial directions, producing false 'multi-centre' flags that hand clean slabs to U3.
refuted_claims.fix: Score each sector only on the component of its centre offset perpendicular to the sector's mean normal (the well-conditioned direction), or use sectors >= 45 deg; declare multi-centre only from a clustering that uses each sector estimate's covariance; or simply test sectors by their angular residual under the global (c, Q) model.

refuted_claims.claim: Stage 1 may run on the 16-slice slab-mean image.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The roll is tilted or bent relative to scan z (fl4 centroid: +11 mm in y over the middle 70 mm, 45 mm over the full height; never measured by the proposal). Across a 1.1 mm slab the layers shift laterally by 1.1 mm * tan(theta) = 0.17 mm (9 deg) to 0.49 mm (24 deg) = 2.5-7 L3 voxels = 0.5-1.6 winding pitches; the slab mean's layering contrast drops to ~35% or to zero and the structure tensor sees mush.
refuted_claims.fix: Per-slice tensors only (1855 slices x ~0.3 s, ~3 min on 4 cores), summed per slab; also fit the axis direction and check each slab's measured aspect against 1/cos(theta), a free tilt diagnostic.

refuted_claims.claim: M5 (16 rays from the axis to the mask edge at ~50 stations) touches 4-9 level-2 chunks (~10-20 MB) per station, ~1 GB and ~5 min total.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Rays to the mask edge are 33-45 mm = 950-1300 L2 px, so the window is the whole 3037^2 slice. Verified .zarray: chunks [128,128,128], compressor null (2,097,152 B each). One station costs a 24 x 24 chunk band = 1.21 GB; 50 stations over 128 mm hit all 29 bands = 35 GB for the CT and ~35 GB again for m7: 5-20 h at 2-8 MB/s, not 5 min (the 18-32 MB figure is right only for the 10 mm Stage-4 windows, 9-16 chunks). The pass bar 'max-min <= 2 windings' is also unreachable: counting 60-130 crossings along a 40 mm uint8 profile at L3 with fused layers, cracks and debris has per-ray counting noise far above +-1.
refuted_claims.fix: Run M5 at level 3 from the tmpfs copy (CT 4.5 GB cached; m7 L3 streamed band by band and discarded); measure the counting noise floor as the count difference between two rays 1 deg apart and pass only if the azimuthal imbalance never exceeds 2x that floor; keep level 2 for the 10 mm seed windows only.

refuted_claims.claim: Read level 3 in 16-slice slabs of 37 MB straight from the zarr; download 4.3 GB once.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Chunks are 128 slices deep, so a 16-slice slab is not addressable; a chunk-LRU reader like tools/fl4/fl4.py's Zarr class (64-chunk cache) against a 144-chunk band thrashes and downloads every band 8 times (36 GB). The padded L3 volume is 15 x 12 x 12 chunks = 4.53 GB. The M7(b)-(d) perturbation passes and M8 reruns each need the data again.
refuted_claims.fix: Read band by band (15 bands x 302 MB), split into slabs in RAM, and keep the whole 4.53 GB L3 in /dev/shm (11 GB free) so all later passes cost no download; 7 siblings take 2-3 bands each (0.6-0.9 GB).

refuted_claims.claim: Stage 0 polar high-pass about the reconstruction centre removes the ring decoy at no cost; M7(a) (axis within 0.3 mm of the rotation centre while the mask centroid is > 2 mm away) tests it.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: (i) Ring amplitude at L3 has never been measured on this volume; 8^3 averaging attenuates rings narrower than ~0.5 mm by 4-8x, and the 'masked' volume has no air outside the mask (fill 0) to measure it in. (ii) The angular-mean subtraction deletes the scroll's own layering within about one pitch of the rotation centre and attenuates it out to the axis offset delta; the fl4 centroid sits 0.3-3 mm from the field centre (6072, 6072) over the middle third, i.e. the core region. (iii) M7(a)'s precondition (mask centroid > 2 mm from the rotation centre) fails over most of the roll, so the test is inconclusive on PHerc0268; M7(b) passing cannot distinguish 'immune' from 'no rings'.
refuted_claims.fix: Measure ring amplitude first in air pockets inside the eroded mask; apply the high-pass only if it exceeds the L3 sheet contrast, and only at rotation radii > delta + 1 mm; make M7(c) (injected off-centre rings at the measured amplitude) the decisive decoy test.

refuted_claims.claim: Absolute winding numbers may be assigned across a bridge whose two one-sided axis extrapolations agree within one pitch (0.5 mm).
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Agreement of two extrapolated axis positions says nothing about the sheets between them. Winding-number continuity across a crushed zone needs the sheets themselves to be traceable through it (no fused, torn or folded layers), and inside a crushed cross-section a straight ray from even the correct centre crosses folded sheets more than once. Axis agreement is necessary, not sufficient; the rule reinstates silent interpolation one level up.
refuted_claims.fix: Winding numbers are a property of the sheet graph: count sheet crossings along integral curves of the normal field (organiser normal grids or the structure tensor) per segment; carry a number across a bridge only when a traced sheet closes the count on both sides.

refuted_claims.claim: The pixel-weighted slab robust centre is the umbilicus; inner/outer band disagreement (M3) is only a flag.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Voters scale with rho, so the global estimate tracks the outer windings. After delamination (outer group sagged 2 mm) or with an ash-filled core the reported 'umbilicus' is the outer envelope's centre, the same quantity the silhouette centroid already measures, while the core is unobserved; seeds_inner at r/R 0.15-0.35 are then placed from a point that no inner winding is concentric with.
refuted_claims.fix: Weight votes by 1/rho (equal weight per winding); report the innermost coherent band's (c, Q) as the umbilicus and the outer band's separately; label 'core unobserved at L3' when the inner band has no coherent pixels and refuse seeds_inner there.

refuted_claims.claim: Level 3 (69 um) is where the layered structure exists, so the resolution gap is closed (with L2 at seed sites).
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Closed only where air gaps >= 1 L3 voxel exist. In compressed or fused zones the only layer evidence is the propagation-phase-contrast fringe, width sqrt(lambda*d) = sqrt(1.07e-11 m x 1.2 m) ~ 3.6 um, i.e. one L0 voxel, which 8^3 averaging erases (and L2's 4^3 averaging mostly erases). So confidence is 0 in the crushed zone by construction of the processing scale, not by measurement; the owner's requirement (an axis where the roll is damaged) is foreclosed before any evidence is looked at.
refuted_claims.fix: Add a targeted level-1 (17 um) pass over low-confidence slabs in 20 mm windows (1160^2 x 8 slices = 11 MB per station, a few hundred MB total) and a second evidence channel: the structure tensor of the organiser m7 surface-probability volume at L2/L3, produced by a model that did see the fringes.

refuted_claims.claim: M4 split-half (even vs odd slices of 16) measures the statistical error of the centre; pass median <= 0.15 mm.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Adjacent L3 slices 69 um apart contain the same sheets, cracks and debris; the halves are not independent and measure pixel noise only, so the bar passes trivially and detects no systematic error.
refuted_claims.fix: Split by opposite azimuth halves and by first vs last 4 slices of the band; report both.

refuted_claims.claim: The crushed zone is interior and is bridged from the clean top and bottom.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The recorded level-4 mask area (logs/fl4/axis_PHerc0268.json) falls from ~250k to 32-60k L4 pixels over the top ~30 mm and bottom ~25 mm, the centroid jumps 20 mm between neighbouring 6 mm samples near the ends, and the last axis point (z = 14096: x = 10761, y = 1374) is off the scroll entirely. Whether the ends are broken, flared or oblique sections of a tilted roll (a 75 mm cylinder tilted 20 deg has a 27 mm partial-section zone), they are the least constrained part, not 'clean'; the narrative is probably inverted for this scroll.
refuted_claims.fix: Drop the assumption; let per-slab confidence decide which segments are clean; drop the z = 14096 point from any initialiser; expect extrapolation outward from the middle; note that fl4.py's centroid really is level 4 (ct4, x16) and only the outer-radius ray is level 3, as the proposal states.

refuted_claims.claim: C0 knots inserted on jumps >= 1 mm sustained for >= 3 slabs handle fracture planes.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: A kink (slope change) is not a jump; the rule never fires for it, so the proposal's own 15-deg-over-2-mm scenario is still smoothed by the spline and misplaces the axis by ~1.3 mm over 10 mm of z.
refuted_claims.fix: Run the change-point detector on first differences as well and insert double knots (C1 breaks) where a sustained slope change with confidence >= 0.6 on both sides is found; audit them like the C0 knots.

refuted_claims.claim: The 400^3 circular-spiral phantom (M9) is a sufficient code-path test.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: 27.6 mm cube, R <= 13 mm, circular layers, no tilt: the caustic size scales with rho and eccentricity, so the test is blind to the Stage-2 failure, the sector ill-conditioning and the slab-mean smear.
refuted_claims.fix: Use 2-D slice phantoms 1200^2 x 64 at 69 um (92 MB) with aspect 1.0, 1.3 and 2.0, tilt 10-20 deg, a D-shaped core, cracks and debris; require the recovered centre within 0.15 mm at every aspect.

verdict.surviving_core: What survives both lenses, restated precisely: (1) Evidence: per-slice (never slab-mean) 2-D structure-tensor layer normals at level 3 (sigma_d ~1.2 vox, sigma_i ~5 vox, coherence gate), with the mask eroded 1 mm and saturated blobs (> p99.5, dilated) masked, computed band by band from the 128^3 uncompressed chunks with the 4.53 GB L3 volume cached once in /dev/shm; ~3-10 min of CPU per pass, < 2 GB RAM, nothing on the 1 GB disk. (2) Per-slab geometry: a concentric-conic normal-field fit n(p) ~ Q(p - c), linear least squares in (Q, Qc), robustified on angular residual with a coarse-to-fine schedule, solved per radial band with 1/rho weighting; outputs c, Q (aspect, orientation), median angular residual, band disagreement, sector consistency scored in the well-conditioned direction, and split-azimuth reproducibility. The umbilicus at a z is the innermost coherent band's c; the outer band's c is reported separately; 'core unobserved' is an explicit state. (3) Global curve: cubic B-spline x(z), y(z) with 2 mm knots, confidence weights, Huber loss, lambda by cross-validation, change-point knots for both jumps (C0) and slope breaks (C1), and explicit no-fit zones reported as one-sided extrapolations plus an envelope at confidence 0; never a silent interpolation. (4) Output contract: a per-slice table (x, y, Q, confidence, residual, n_centres, segment_id, flag) that downstream must read, replacing umbilicus_xy(); the fl4 level-4 silhouette centroid is demoted to a search-window initialiser with its off-scroll last point dropped. (5) Validation that needs no ground truth and is actually informative: injected off-centre rings and injected blobs (M7c, M7d), lambda sensitivity and knot audit (M8), organiser normal-grid agreement measured against the (c, Q) normal field rather than the ray, an azimuthal winding-balance test run at level 3 against a measured counting-noise floor and applied equally to the old centroid axis, eccentric and tilted 2-D phantoms. (6) Role in the master model: the axis supplies the global origin and a topological reference per segment; the radial search direction is the local normal field Q(p - c) or the organiser normal grid, not the straight ray to the axis; absolute winding numbers come from sheet tracing along that field, per segment, and cross a damaged zone only when a traced sheet closes the count on both sides. Compute for all of this on 4 CPU / 15 GB / 11 GB tmpfs: one 4.5 GB download (plus m7 L3 streamed, plus ~1-1.6 GB of level-2 seed windows, plus a few hundred MB of level-1 windows for fused zones), roughly 1-2 h wall time, splittable over the 7 siblings by chunk band.
verdict.missing_validation: (1) No test on eccentric or tilted geometry: the only phantom is a circular spiral of R <= 13 mm, so the central estimator (normal concurrency with a 0.5 mm biweight) is never exercised against the aspect ~1.29 silhouette this scroll actually has or against the 9-24 deg centroid drift; add 2-D phantoms at aspect 1.0/1.3/2.0 and tilt 10-20 deg before any run on the scroll. (2) The scan tilt / bending of PHerc0268 is never measured; the proposal works in z-slices and never checks per-slab aspect against 1/cos(theta) or fits the axis direction. (3) Ring-artefact amplitude at level 3 is assumed, not measured, and the masked volume has no outside-air region to measure it in; M7(a) is inconclusive here because the mask centroid is within 0.3-3 mm of the field centre over the middle third. (4) No audit of whether the organiser mask hugs the scroll or is a loose hull (changes what the 1 mm erosion removes and whether container walls vote). (5) No check that the organiser m7 pyramid at L2/L3 still carries layer information (what its downsampling does to a one-voxel surface), although M5 and the suggested second evidence channel depend on it. (6) No downstream, end-to-end check: a seed placed from the new axis should grow a sheet (vc_grow_seg_from_seed) that stays on one winding over >= 20 mm, and a closed loop traced at fixed winding number around the axis with the normal grid should close; the winding count between axis and outer surface along a fixed azimuth should vary smoothly with z, with any jump localised to a declared break or bridge. (7) No evidence either way on whether the crushed zone is interior; the mask-area profile suggests the ends, not the middle, are the least constrained, and the bridging narrative is untested. (8) Counting noise for M5 is not measured, so its 2-winding bar is unfounded. (9) Split-half M4 as defined is not independent and validates nothing. (10) The L3-only evidence model is never checked against a level-1 window in a compressed zone to see whether fused layers carry any signal at 17 um that 69 um discards.

audit.strategy: Keep the owner's intent (invert a dense orientation field to locate the global axis, so that the axis can be found even where the physical core is destroyed) but change the physical carrier and the inversion. The carrier cannot be papyrus fibres: recto fibres are tangent to the winding and verso fibres are parallel to the axis, so neither family 'projects back' to the axis, and fibres are only marginally resolved at 8.64 um and absent at 34.56/69 um. The carrier that actually encodes the radial direction is the sheet layering, whose normal is the first eigenvector of a 3-D structure tensor at level 3 (69 um, pitch = 4-9 voxels) with a level-2 (34.56 um) crop inside the core. The inversion is not a Hough mode of normal lines (which peaks on the evolute of non-circular sections) nor a plain least-squares focal point (biased by buckles, cracks, ash, rings and the mask edge), but a per-slab, azimuth-balanced, curvature-gated, IRLS-Cauchy weighted concurrency fit of in-plane normal lines, solved in the plane perpendicular to a per-slab axis direction obtained from the null vector of the normal covariance, and checked by a Poincare-index test that localises the singularity of the orientation field to the innermost coherent winding (the 'core envelope'). U2 then delivers, per 4.4 mm slab: centre c(z), its covariance, axis direction t(z), core-envelope radius r_core(z), conditioning, and shear/indeterminate flags with explicit C0 break-points. These are the data term for the U1 tube; the rejected high-curvature local centres are handed to U3 rather than being averaged into the global axis. Every stage has a measurable self-consistency or phantom metric; nothing is learned, so no parchment or macro-shape memorisation can enter.
audit.summary_of_method_as_specified: U2 as written: compute a dense 3-D tensor field of papyrus fibre orientation across the whole PHerc0268 volume, then 'project backwards' the fibre curves to their shared origin, taking that focal point as the umbilicus; claimed to work even where the physical core is destroyed because the outer, intact fibre field still points at the lost centre. Implicit assumptions: (a) fibres are resolved at the processing scale; (b) fibre directions (or their curvature) are radially informative; (c) the back-projected lines of the field are concurrent at one point per height; (d) that point is well defined and continuous in z through the crushed middle; (e) the computation over the full volume is affordable on CPU.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Non-concurrency of normal lines in non-circular sections. Normal lines of a closed curve are concurrent only for a circle; for any flattened/elliptical/D-shaped winding they envelope the evolute, so a mode-seeking (Hough/accumulator/mean-shift) inversion peaks at the evolute cusps, and even the plain least-squares focal point is biased for asymmetric (D-shaped) sections toward the more curved side. No local geometric quantity of the sheets defines the centre of a non-circular spiral; only the topological singularity of the orientation field does.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: In the crushed middle third of PHerc0268 (roughly z = 40-85 mm of the 128 mm height), suppose a slab's windings are squashed to a 2:1 section with semi-axes a = 16 mm, b = 8 mm (to be read from the level-3 mask, not assumed). The normal-line accumulator then peaks at the astroid cusps at +/-(a^2-b^2)/a = +/-12 mm from the true centre along the long axis, i.e. two false umbilici 24 mm apart, each sitting ~30 windings off at 0.4 mm pitch; a mode estimator flips between them from slab to slab, the derived winding numbers jump by tens, and rays from the false centre cross the windings on the near side twice and the far side zero times.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Local centres of curvature of buckles, folds and delamination arcs are concurrency points in their own right (mini-umbilici). An unweighted or coherence-only weighted focal-point fit sums their offsets into the global estimate; the level-3 integration scale (rho = 3 voxels = 0.2 mm) does not average out buckles with radius above ~0.3 mm, which are exactly the structures a crushed core is made of.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A core slab containing a few dozen sharp buckles of radius 0.3-0.8 mm at R = 3-8 mm: each buckle's normals converge at its own centre; with uniform weights the fit lands inside the buckle cluster rather than at the axis, and the error is systematic (same sign over neighbouring slabs), so it survives z-smoothing in U1 and shifts the origin of the whole core by millimetres.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: One point per slab plus forced continuity through a sheared core. Where the upper and lower intact parts of the roll are laterally offset (shear) across a collapse zone, a single C2-continuous axis cuts the sheets obliquely in the transition; rays from it become tangent to sheets, giving double crossings and winding-number jumps of 2.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: If the per-slab fits above and below the crushed zone of PHerc0268 differ by, say, 4 mm laterally across a 10 mm collapse zone, a smooth bridge in U1 passes within one sheet thickness of several windings in the zone; the ray-crossing count N(az) along the bridge then differs by 2 between adjacent azimuths and the absolute winding number assigned to the top half is wrong by one or two relative to the bottom half, i.e. the exact drift/twist the umbilicus is supposed to prevent.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Fibre geometry misconception. Recto fibres run circumferentially (tangent to the winding) and verso fibres run along the roll axis. Back-projecting tangent lines gives lines that miss the axis by exactly R and envelope the winding curve itself; back-projecting axial lines gives a parallel bundle that never intersects the axis. The only fibre-derived quantity that carries axis information is the DIRECTION of the verso family (parallel to the axis), not its position. Radial information lives in the sheet normal, which is a layering property, not a fibre property.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A level-0 block at R = 15 mm with well-preserved recto fibres: projected fibre lines are tangent to the 15 mm circle; an accumulator over them peaks on the circle (the sheet itself), never at the centre; the verso family contributes parallel lines whose 'intersection' is numerically undefined (rank-deficient normal matrix), so the solver returns whatever regularisation or initialisation it was given, typically the mask centroid, which looks plausible and is unvalidated.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Negative transfer only enters if a learned orientation/normal estimator replaces the structure tensor (e.g. the organizer normal grids or an En-Gedi-trained model). Parchment has no bast-fibre lattice and different layering/collapse mechanics; its normal priors and the toxic-data rule both forbid it. The structure tensor itself is physics-free and does not transfer anything.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Using the organizer's normal grids (provenance and training data unknown, community code unaudited) as the primary normal field: in PHerc0268's ash core the model emits confident normals shaped by its training scrolls' collapse patterns; these are then 'inverted' into a confident but fictitious centre. They may be used only as an independent cross-check with an angular-agreement metric, never as input.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Scale/feasibility: fibres (tens of um) are at the Nyquist limit at 8.64 um and do not exist in the data at 34.56 or 69 um; at level 3 the structure tensor's second and third eigenvectors (the in-sheet directions, one of which would be 'the fibre direction') are noise. A whole-volume fibre-scale tensor at level 0 is 2.2e12 voxels (2.2 TB uint8; 53 TB for a 6-component float32 tensor).
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Level 0 of 20251110183117-8.640um-1.2m-116keV-masked.zarr: 14833 x 12145 x 12145. Nine separable Gaussian filters over 2.2e12 voxels is ~1e6 CPU-seconds (about 3 days on 4 cores, if memory allowed, which it does not), after a ~2 TB download onto 1 GB of free disk. And the result would still be the wrong carrier (see mode 2). At level 3 (1855 x 1519 x 1519) the layering is resolved (sheets 1.5-3 voxels thick, pitch 4-9 voxels) so only e1 (the sheet normal) is meaningful there.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Aliasing at level 4 near the core. At 138 um a 0.3 mm pitch is 2.2 voxels (Nyquist); the structure tensor of an aliased stripe pattern returns rotated or random normals exactly in the innermost windings where axis accuracy matters most. The existing fl4 centroid proxy at level 4 is mass-based and unaffected, but a level-4 normal field is unusable inside ~5 mm of the core.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Innermost intact windings of PHerc0268 at 0.3-0.4 mm pitch: level-4 normals there are wrong by tens of degrees, so lines from the shortest lever arms (which carry the least angular-lever error and would otherwise anchor the fit) are corrupted; the fit is then carried entirely by the outer windings, whose non-circularity bias (mode 1) is largest.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Mask-edge leakage. The '-masked' volume has a hard zero border; at level 3 that border is the strongest edge in the data, its normals are planar, coherent and concurrent on the mask shape's centre/evolute. Unless the nonzero mask is eroded by at least 3*sigma_g + 3*rho (about 12 voxels = 0.8 mm at level 3), the fit is pulled to the mask centroid.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: The leaked mask-edge term silently reproduces the fl4 CT-mask-centroid proxy (tools/fl4/fl4.py cmd_seeds, 'axis proxy (CT-mask centroid, level 4)'), so U2 and the old proxy 'agree' everywhere, including in the crushed zone where they should disagree; the agreement is then misread as validation.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Ring artefacts and beam-hardening cupping. Rings are concentric about the reconstruction rotation axis, z-stationary, perfectly planar, low-curvature and radius-consistent, so they pass every geometric gate and are exactly concurrent at the rotation centre, a perfect fake umbilicus. Cupping adds a smooth radial gradient over the whole mass whose normals point at the mass centre.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Reconstruction centre at about (759.5, 759.5) at level 3 (image centre). In the ash core where genuine layering contrast is weak, residual broad ring bands dominate the admissible normals and c(z) collapses onto the image centre for every core slab, yielding a suspiciously straight axis through the middle that is actually the scanner's rotation axis, offset from the scroll's own axis by whatever the sample's mounting offset was.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Ash / no-layering regions with an uncalibrated coherence gate. Where layering contrast is absent the tensor normals are noise-driven and uniformly distributed; a uniform bundle of lines through points p_i has its least-squares concurrency point at the centroid of the p_i, so an ungated fit returns the ash lump's centroid: a plausible-looking, meaningless number.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A compacted core slab of PHerc0268 where sheets are pressed together with no air gaps (the owner's R2 concern): at level 3 the trace and planarity of the tensor are at the noise floor; if the coherence threshold is copied from another scroll/beamline instead of being measured on PHerc0268's own air/ash null regions, the slab passes as 'determined' with a sub-millimetre covariance that is pure noise statistics.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Debris, inclusions and radial cracks. Sub-0.2 mm hairs/dust are averaged out at rho = 0.2 mm; 0.3-1 mm mineral inclusions have closed boundaries whose normals converge at the inclusion centre (local radius of curvature far below R); straight radial cracks have tangential normals whose lines miss the axis by R. Each is benign individually but a crack field covering a large sector inflates the robust scale estimate and tilts the fit.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A 90-degree sector of radial cracks in a crushed slab contributes ~25% of admissible lines with residual ~R; if the Cauchy scale is set by the global MAD without a cap, the scale grows to millimetres, the kernel stops rejecting them and the fit is pulled along the crack sector by a fraction of a millimetre to millimetres.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Hand-set priors (pitch band 0.3-0.6 mm fixing rho, the circular-winding assumption fixing the curvature-gate tolerance, isotropic bandwidths, initialisation from the mask centroid) encode a 'typical scroll'. Any learned per-slice centre regressor trained on the handful of scanned scrolls would memorise their macro collapse shapes outright.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: One-sided collapse in PHerc0268's middle puts the mask centroid several millimetres from the axis basin; a single-start IRLS from the centroid converges to a secondary (evolute/buckle) minimum and reports a tight covariance there. A learned regressor would instead output the average collapse geometry of its training scrolls. Both failures are detectable only by the multi-start basin test and the index test, which must be mandatory.

audit.hardened_alternative:
Hardened U2 = 'layering-normal concurrency + topological index', executed per 4.4 mm slab, with explicit uncertainty and break-points. All parameters below are defaults to be calibrated on PHerc0268 by the null test and phantom (metric list); no measured values are claimed.

H0 Scale and data. Primary scale: level 3 (69.1 um; 1855 x 1519 x 1519, 4.3 GB uint8): sheets 1.5-3 voxels, pitch 4-9 voxels, layering resolved, fibres absent. Secondary: level 2 (34.56 um) only as a crop around the core envelope. Level 4 is used for nothing but a coarse initial mask and the legacy centroid; level 0/1 are not processed volumetrically. Stream z-slabs of 64 slices with 8-slice halos (float32 slab ~0.74 GB; peak ~4-5 GB per worker; 2 workers in 15 GB); split the 29 slabs across the 7 sibling containers by z-range. Erode the nonzero mask by 12 voxels (0.8 mm) before any accumulation; apply the ring diagnostic (z-stationarity of the normal-angle field; distance of c(z) from the image centre) and an optional polar azimuthal-median ring filter about the reconstruction centre whose on/off effect on c(z) must be below 0.2 mm, otherwise the filter is disabled and the diagnostic alone is reported.

H1 Structure tensor (not a fibre tensor). Gaussian derivatives sigma_g = 1.0 voxel; J = G_rho * (grad I grad I^T) with rho = 3.0 voxels (0.21 mm: about one sheet plus gap, below one pitch, so a single winding's normal is measured and neighbouring windings only reinforce it). Block-average J to stride 2 (grid 928 x 760 x 760) before the analytic 3x3 symmetric eigendecomposition. Outputs per decimated voxel: unsigned normal n = e1 (3 x int8), planarity c_p = (l1-l2)/(l1+eps), line-likeness c_l = (l2-l3)/(l1+eps) (recorded only to prove it is noise at this scale), trace (contrast). Admissible voxels: eroded mask AND c_p >= c_p0 AND trace >= tr0, with c_p0 and tr0 = 99th percentile of the same quantities measured in PHerc0268's own air/ash null regions (not copied from any other scroll).

H2 Per-slab axis direction without fitting. T(z) = sum_i w_i n_i n_i^T over admissible voxels (w = c_p); t(z) = eigenvector of the smallest eigenvalue (all sheet normals are perpendicular to the roll axis even when crushed radially). Report tilt of t(z) to the scanner z and the ratio of the two smallest eigenvalues (cylindricity). If tilt > 3 degrees, halve the slab thickness (32 slices) and project normals onto the plane perpendicular to t(z) rather than onto xy.

H3 Robust planar concurrency fit (the correct inversion). For each admissible voxel, in-plane unit normal m_i (projection of n_i onto the plane perpendicular to t(z), renormalised) and tangent u_i perpendicular to m_i; the line is p_i + s m_i (unsigned, so no inward/outward disambiguation is needed). Residual d_i(c) = u_i . (c - p_i). Minimise sum_i w_i d_i^2 by IRLS: normal matrix A = sum_i w_i u_i u_i^T, c = A^-1 sum_i w_i u_i u_i^T p_i. Weights: w_i = c_p,i * b_sector(i) * g_curv,i * psi(d_i / s) / (sigma_theta^2 R_i^2 + sigma_0^2), where psi is the Cauchy kernel 1/(1+(d/s)^2) with s = 1.4826 * MAD(d) floored at 0.2 mm and capped at 1.5 mm; sigma_theta = angular noise of the normals measured on the phantom/null test (expected 2-4 degrees), sigma_0 = 0.15 mm, R_i = |c - p_i| (Gauss-Markov weighting of the angular lever arm, recomputed each iteration); b_sector normalises the total weight in each 10-degree azimuth sector about the current c so that a densely sampled curved side cannot outvote a sparse flat side (this is what keeps the LS point at the centre of symmetric non-circular sections instead of on their evolute); g_curv is the curvature-consistency gate: local curvature kappa_i from the in-plane orientation field (doubled-angle representation (cos 2theta, sin 2theta) smoothed at 3 voxels; kappa = |d theta / ds| along u_i); g = 0 when 1/kappa_i < 0.25 R_i (buckles, folds, inclusion boundaries: their centres go to U3), g = 1 otherwise; straight features (kappa ~ 0) are left to the Cauchy kernel. Initialise from (a) the c_p-weighted plain LS, (b) the legacy fl4 mask centroid, (c) eight points 5 mm off (a) at 45-degree spacing; iterate to |delta c| < 0.02 mm; all ten runs must agree (basin test). Report c(z), covariance = chi^2-scaled A^-1 inflated by a 50-draw azimuth-sector bootstrap, the conditioning ratio lambda_min/lambda_max of A (rank-1 A = parallel stack, 'lasagna', undetermined along the sheets), and the inlier fraction.

H4 Topological index and core envelope. From the slab's 2-D orientation field theta(x,y) (level 3 stride 2; level 2 inside the crop), compute the Poincare index of the director field on loops of radius 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16 mm about c(z): index = (sum of wrapped 2*theta increments around the loop)/(4 pi), valid only when >= 80% of loop samples are admissible. The smallest radius r_core(z) from which all admissible loops give index +1 is the innermost coherent winding: the axis is guaranteed inside it, and in indeterminate slabs the covariance of c(z) is replaced by a disc of radius r_core(z). If no loop up to 16 mm passes, the slab is flagged 'indeterminate'.

H5 Level-2 refinement. Crop level 2 around c(z) with half-width r_core(z) + 2 mm (typically a few hundred voxels square by 3709 slices, under 1 GB), sigma_g = 1.0, rho = 4 voxels (0.14 mm), repeat H3-H4; level-2 and level-3 centres must agree (metric).

H6 Break-point handling for U1. Deliverable per slab: {z, c, Sigma, t, r_core, cond(A), inlier fraction, basin flag, index flags}. Where consecutive determined slabs differ by more than 3 combined sigma and the index test fails between them (shear/collapse), U1 receives a C0 knot (position continuity only, free curvature) and the two sides are treated as separate rigid segments; where slabs are indeterminate, U1 bridges on the smoothness prior between the nearest determined slabs above and below, and the bridge length in mm plus the union of flanking r_core discs is reported as the axis uncertainty envelope. The radial search direction inside crushed zones is taken from the local normal field n (which U2 already produces), not from rays out of c(z); rays from c(z) are used for absolute winding-number assignment only in slabs where the ray-crossing metric passes.

H7 Optional, gated fibre use (direction only). Twelve 384^3 blocks of level 0 (3.3 mm cubes, ~57 MB each, ~0.7 GB total) on coherent sheets in the clean top and bottom; sigma_g = 1 voxel (8.64 um), rho = 4 voxels (35 um); within sheet voxels test line-likeness c_l >= 0.3 in >= 20% of voxels. If the gate fails, fibres are declared unresolved and the fibre route is closed with that number recorded. If it passes, the e3 directions must be bimodal (tangential recto, axial verso) and the axial mode must agree with t(z) from H2 within 5 degrees; this is a cross-check of the axis direction, never a position estimate.

H8 Independent cross-checks (data, not truth): organizer normal grids (audited line by line before any loading; their angular agreement with n is a reported metric), the m7 surface-probability volume (for the ray-crossing metric), and the legacy fl4 centroid (reported difference, with the warning that agreement in the crushed zone indicates mask-edge leakage rather than correctness).

validation_metrics.name: Null calibration of the coherence gate
validation_metrics.definition: Distribution of planarity c_p and trace in air/ash regions of PHerc0268 at level 3 (and level 2 crop); gate thresholds set at their 99th percentiles; fraction of in-mask voxels that pass.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Thresholds must come from PHerc0268 itself; admissible fraction in the clean top/bottom zones expected 20-60%; below 5% means sigma_g/rho are mismatched to the pitch and the run is invalid.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Air is identified as the zero-mask exterior ring just inside the erosion margin and large interior voids; ash as low-trace interior regions; statistics are empirical percentiles of the computed tensor, no labels needed.

validation_metrics.name: Concurrency conditioning ratio
validation_metrics.definition: lambda_min/lambda_max of the IRLS normal matrix A(z) = sum w u u^T at convergence (rank-1 means normals are parallel, e.g. a compacted stack).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: >= 0.3 in clean zones for a determined slab; < 0.1 forces the 'indeterminate' flag regardless of the reported covariance.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Direct eigenvalues of the 2x2 matrix accumulated during the fit.

validation_metrics.name: Robust residual, inlier fraction and uncertainty ellipse
validation_metrics.definition: At converged c(z): fraction of admissible lines with |d_i| < 1.0 mm; 95% uncertainty ellipse from chi^2-scaled A^-1 inflated by a 50-draw azimuth-sector bootstrap.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Clean zones: inlier fraction >= 0.5 and ellipse semi-major <= 0.5 mm; crushed zones: report only, semi-major <= r_core(z) by construction.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Residuals and bootstrap are internal to the fit; sector bootstrap resamples 10-degree azimuth sectors with replacement and refits.

validation_metrics.name: Multi-start basin agreement
validation_metrics.definition: Spread of converged c(z) over ten initialisations (weighted LS, legacy centroid, eight 5 mm offsets).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: All ten within 0.2 mm of each other; otherwise the slab is multimodal (evolute cusps/buckle cluster) and is flagged, never averaged.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Repeat the IRLS with different starts; compare end points.

validation_metrics.name: Poincare index and core envelope continuity
validation_metrics.definition: Director-field index on loops of 1.5-16 mm radius about c(z); r_core(z) = smallest radius from which all admissible loops give +1.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Clean zones: index +1 on every admissible loop with radius >= r_core and r_core continuous (|delta r_core| < 2 mm between adjacent slabs); any slab with no passing loop up to 16 mm is 'indeterminate'. Break-points allowed only where this metric or the basin test fails.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Sum of wrapped doubled-angle increments around each sampled loop of the computed orientation field; a purely topological property of the data.

validation_metrics.name: Ray-crossing consistency (m7 surface probability)
validation_metrics.definition: Along 72 rays from c(z) to the outer mask radius at level 2, count sheet crossings N(az) in the organizer surface-probability volume; detect double crossings (two crossings within 0.15 mm on one ray).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Clean zones: |N(az) - N(az+5 deg)| <= 1 for >= 95% of adjacent pairs and zero double crossings; a jump of 2 or a double crossing marks the centre as outside the innermost winding or the slab as sheared.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: A spiral about its true axis changes its crossing count by exactly one unit per revolution; the test uses only the m7 volume (treated as data) and the candidate axis.

validation_metrics.name: Axis-direction consistency
validation_metrics.definition: Angle between t(z) (null vector of the slab normal covariance) and the finite-difference direction of the c(z) track over +/-2 slabs.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: <= 3 degrees in clean zones (two independent estimators of the same tilt).
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Both quantities are computed from the data; agreement is internal consistency, not fit quality, so it cannot be tuned into passing.

validation_metrics.name: Scale and stride consistency
validation_metrics.definition: |c_L3(z) - c_L2(z)| inside the core crop; |c_stride2 - c_stride3| at level 3.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: <= 0.3 mm between levels; <= 0.1 mm between strides.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Run the identical pipeline at the two scales/strides and difference the outputs.

validation_metrics.name: z-smoothness residual of independent slab fits
validation_metrics.definition: Second difference |c(z+1) - 2 c(z) + c(z-1)| of per-slab centres (slabs are fitted independently, with no z coupling).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: <= 0.3 mm per 4.4 mm slab in clean zones; larger values permitted only at slabs already flagged by the basin or index tests (these become U1 C0 knots).
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Finite differences of the slab outputs; the absence of z-coupling in the fit makes smoothness a genuine test rather than a prior.

validation_metrics.name: Artefact leak tests (rings, cupping, mask edge)
validation_metrics.definition: (a) Correlation of the normal-angle field between z and z + 10 mm at the same (x,y) within the mask; (b) distance of c(z) from the reconstruction centre (image centre) versus the mask centroid; (c) change of c(z) when the polar ring filter is toggled; (d) change of c(z) when mask erosion is reduced from 12 to 4 voxels.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: (a) < 0.3 after processing (rings give ~1); (b) c(z) must not sit within 0.3 mm of the image centre over the core while the mask centroid is elsewhere; (c) <= 0.2 mm; (d) <= 0.2 mm (larger means mask-edge leakage).
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: All four are differential or statistical tests on the computed field and on re-runs with one preprocessing step toggled.

validation_metrics.name: Synthetic phantom bias (allowed synthetic data, no parchment)
validation_metrics.definition: In-silico Archimedean spiral sheet (thickness 0.15 mm, pitch 0.4 mm) rendered at 69 and 34.56 um with noise matched to the measured PHerc0268 level-3 noise std, in variants: circular; 2:1 elliptical squash; 40 random buckles of 0.3-0.8 mm radius; straight radial crack sector of 90 degrees; ring pattern centred 8 mm off-axis; 30% ash core with layering removed. Centre error of the identical pipeline against the known phantom axis.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Circular <= 0.15 mm; 2:1 ellipse <= 1.0 mm; buckles <= 0.5 mm; crack sector <= 0.3 mm; off-axis rings bias <= 0.3 mm; ash core: error <= reported r_core and slab correctly flagged indeterminate when no loop passes.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Ground truth exists only in the phantom, which is generated analytically; it measures the estimator's bias under each failure mode, nothing is trained on it.

validation_metrics.name: Cross-check against existing products (reported, not pass/fail)
validation_metrics.definition: Median angle between structure-tensor normals and the audited organizer normal grids in clean zones; |c_U2(z) - c_fl4centroid(z)| per slab.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Angle reported (expect <= 10 degrees in clean zones; larger triggers numeric inspection of both); centroid difference > 5 mm triggers inspection; near-zero difference everywhere including the crushed zone is itself a failure signal (mask-edge leakage, metric above).
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Both comparators are data products of unknown accuracy, so they are reported as differences, never used as truth.

audit.compute_estimate: Level-3 global structure tensor: 4.28e9 voxels, 9 separable Gaussian filters (sigma 1 derivatives, rho 3 smoothing) ~ 30-40 min single-threaded with scipy.ndimage, ~15-20 min with 2 parallel slab workers in 15 GB (peak ~4-5 GB each); analytic eigendecomposition at stride 2 (5.4e8 voxels) ~ 1-2 min; download/decompression of level 3 (4.3 GB raw, ~2-4 GB compressed) ~ 3-8 min through the proxy. Split by z-range over the 7 siblings with 8-slice halos: ~10-15 min each. Per-slab IRLS fits (29 slabs, ~1-7 M lines each, 10 starts, <= 20 iterations) < 5 min total; index tests seconds; bootstrap (50 draws x 29 slabs) ~ 10 min. Level-2 core crop (about 3709 x 450 x 450 = 7.5e8 voxels, 0.75 GB) ~ 10-15 min. Phantoms (400^3 volumes, 6 variants x 2 scales) ~ 15 min total. Optional level-0 fibre gate: 12 x 57 MB blocks, ~5 min. Storage: stride-2 normal field 5.4e8 x 7 B = 3.8 GB (or 1.1 GB at stride 3) in /dev/shm (11 GB free), per-slab JSON a few MB to the repo; the field is recomputable in under an hour so loss on restart is acceptable, but the JSON must be committed. Total wall time on one container ~1.5-2.5 h, under 1 h with siblings. Rejected level-0 whole-volume variant for comparison: 2.2e12 voxels, ~1e6 CPU-s (~3 days on 4 cores) plus ~2 TB download onto 1 GB of free disk.
audit.what_to_reject_outright: (1) Any whole-volume 'fibre-orientation tensor' at level 0 or 1: 2.2 TB / 273 GB of input, days of CPU, no disk, and the wrong carrier. (2) Using the second/third structure-tensor eigenvectors at level 2-4 as 'fibre direction': fibres are not in the data at those scales; those vectors are noise. (3) The geometric premise that fibre curves 'project backwards to a shared origin': recto fibres are tangential (miss the axis by R), verso fibres are axial (never intersect it); only sheet-layering normals carry radial information, and fibres can at most confirm the axis direction. (4) Hough/accumulator/mean-shift 'focal point' of normal lines as the centre: it finds the evolute cusps of any non-circular section, i.e. false umbilici millimetres off along the long axis of a crushed slab. (5) Unweighted or coherence-only least squares without the curvature gate, azimuth-sector balancing, Cauchy kernel with a capped scale, and mask erosion: biased by buckles, cracks, ash, rings and the mask edge. (6) Level-4 (138 um) normals anywhere near the core: 0.3 mm pitch is at Nyquist there. (7) A single C2-continuous point-axis forced through verified shear/indeterminate zones; U2 must emit C0 break-points and uncertainty discs instead. (8) Any learned per-slice centre regressor or any learned normal estimator trained on parchment (En-Gedi) or on the few available scrolls' collapse shapes: toxic-data rule and macro-shape memorisation; the organizer normal grids may serve only as an audited cross-check. (9) Reporting a centre for any slab that fails the basin test, the index test or the conditioning threshold; such slabs are 'indeterminate' by definition and are bridged by U1, not filled in by U2. (10) Treating agreement with the unvalidated fl4 mask-centroid proxy as validation.

refuted_claims.claim: Compute: 'stride-2 normal field 5.4e8 x 7 B = 3.8 GB in /dev/shm (11 GB free)' alongside '2 workers in 15 GB (peak ~4-5 GB each)'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: tmpfs is RAM, not extra storage: on this container `free` shows total 16.1 GB, 'shared' (tmpfs) already 3.4 GB (/dev/shm/umb 2.1 GB of level-4 arrays, /dev/shm/shards 1.3 GB), other resident jobs ~5.5 GB (build_data.py 3.6 GB RSS, train_master.py 1.2 GB, fetch_zarr.py 0.7 GB), available 6.5 GB. The plan's 2 x 5 GB + 3.8 GB = 13.8 GB cannot coexist with that; and with the correct 16-slice halo (see next item) a worker's peak is ~6.5 GB (float32 buffer 96 x 1519^2 x 4 B = 0.89 GB; input + 3 gradients + product + smoothed = 6 buffers = 5.3 GB, + 0.66 GB decimated accumulators + chunk-row cache). Disk is 1.2 GB free, so nothing can spill there.
refuted_claims.fix: One worker, or two workers with y-tiling (two 16-voxel-halo tiles: ~3.3 GB each). Do not keep the full field: keep per-slab admissible voters subsampled to <= 300k (29 x 300k x 16 B = 140 MB) plus a stride-3 int8 angle/coherence field only if the existing 2.1 GB level-4 arrays are released. Record `free -m` before launch and refuse to start below 8 GB available.

refuted_claims.claim: 'Stream z-slabs of 64 slices with 8-slice halos' is exact for sigma_g = 1.0 and rho = 3.0.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: scipy.ndimage truncates at 4 sigma: derivative radius 4 + smoothing radius 12 = 16 voxels of support. An 8-slice halo mirrors the slab edge into J_xz and J_yz for the outer 8-16 slices of every slab (sign-flipped under reflection, so they are attenuated), biasing the 3-D normal toward the xy-plane exactly where H2's t(z) is estimated. In-plane angles are unaffected, so it is not fatal, but the stated memory (0.74 GB per buffer) assumes the wrong halo; the chunk layout is 128 x 128 x 128 uncompressed, so 64-slice slabs with any halo also read two chunk rows each (2 x ~160 MB of stored chunks).
refuted_claims.fix: Halo 16 (or truncate = 3.0 with halo 12), slabs aligned to the 128-slice chunk rows (one chunk row + 16-slice halos from the neighbours), and state the buffer size as 96-160 slices x 1519^2 x 4 B.

refuted_claims.claim: 'Per-slab IRLS fits (29 slabs, ~1-7 M lines each, 10 starts, <= 20 iterations) < 5 min total; bootstrap (50 draws x 29 slabs) ~10 min.'
refuted_claims.why_wrong: At 1-7 M lines an IRLS iteration (residual, lever arm, Cauchy weight, atan2 for 10-degree sectors, bincount, three accumulations, ~25 passes over float64 arrays of 8-56 MB) costs 0.3-1 s in numpy. 10 starts x 20 iterations = 200 iterations = 1-3 min per slab, 30-90 min for 29 slabs; the bootstrap is 1000 iterations per slab = 5-15 min per slab, 2.5-7 h total; the level-2 pass doubles it. The budget is wrong by 10-30x unless the voters are subsampled, which the text never says.
refuted_claims.fix: Stratified subsampling to <= 300k voters per slab (per azimuth sector, as the sibling's tools/umb/st_axis.py already does with --max_voters 300000): ~15 ms per iteration, 4 s per slab for the starts, ~15 s for 50 bootstrap draws, ~10 min total. Compute the sector index once per start and refresh it only every 5 iterations (c moves < 0.5 mm).

refuted_claims.claim: 'Level-2 core crop (about 3709 x 450 x 450 = 7.5e8 voxels, 0.75 GB) ~10-15 min' with half-width r_core(z) + 2 mm.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: 450 voxels at 34.56 um assumes r_core ~ 5.8 mm. The proposal's own index test allows r_core up to 16 mm, giving a 1042-voxel crop = 4.0e9 voxels = 4 GB, the size of the whole level 3; and the session's level-4 exploration (/dev/shm/umb/explore_L4.json: mask area 230-266k voxels at 138 um) puts the section's equivalent radius at 37-40 mm, so a crushed slab whose innermost coherent winding is far out would ask for most of level 2 (34 GB raw, 32-128 chunk rows that cannot be held). Level 2 refinement also adds nothing where the inner windings are gone, which is exactly where r_core is large.
refuted_claims.fix: Run the level-2 refinement only for slabs with r_core <= 6 mm (crop <= 8 mm half-width, ~460 voxels), per-slab crops centred on c(z), streamed one 128-slice chunk row at a time; skip and say so elsewhere.

refuted_claims.claim: 'download/decompression of level 3 (4.3 GB raw, ~2-4 GB compressed) ~3-8 min through the proxy'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The volume's .zarray says compressor: null, so nothing is compressed; chunks are 2,097,152-byte blocks and only in-mask chunks are stored (z-rows 0, 7, 14 hold 41, 81, 89 of 144 possible), i.e. ~1.1-1.2k chunks = 2.3-2.5 GB. A single GET through the agent proxy measured 0.9-1.7 MB/s (2 MB in 1.2-2.3 s), so sequential fetch is 25-45 min; only the threaded fetcher (tools/umb/fetch_zarr.py reports ~70 req/s at 32 threads; its log shows a 41-chunk row in <= 7 s, ~12 MB/s) brings it to ~3-4 min. The 3-8 min figure is right by accident and the premise is wrong.
refuted_claims.fix: State: level 3 = ~2.4 GB of uncompressed 2 MB chunks, fetched with >= 32 threads at ~12 MB/s (~4 min), never to disk; level 2 only as crops; level 0 only the twelve 384^3 blocks (27 chunks each, 54 MB).

refuted_claims.claim: The ray-crossing metric 'along 72 rays from c(z) to the outer mask radius at level 2' in the m7 volume, and the lasagna/normal-grid cross-checks, cost nothing in the compute estimate.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: m7 level 2 is 3709 x 3037^2 in 192^3 zstd chunks (~1.2 MB compressed, 7 MB raw each): one z-chunk-row per slab is 256 chunks = 1.8 GB raw, 20 rows = 34 GB raw / ~6 GB compressed, ~10 min of proxy time and 1.8 GB RAM per slab that the plan never budgets. The lasagna nx/ny at level 3 are stored in 32^3 lz4 chunks: 133,632 requests per component, 30+ min per component even at 70 req/s. The normal grids are > 1000 files of 252 KB in xy alone, undocumented format.
refuted_claims.fix: Ray test on m7 level 3 (10 rows x 64 chunks = ~0.8 GB compressed; 0.15 mm = 2.2 voxels, still resolvable as a double crossing) and on the raw slab mean image as a second opinion; lasagna cross-check at level 4 only (nx, ny already in /dev/shm/umb); normal grids only after the generating code is audited.

refuted_claims.claim: 'Level-3 global structure tensor ... ~30-40 min single-threaded; ~15-20 min with 2 parallel slab workers'; 'Total wall time on one container ~1.5-2.5 h'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: 27 one-dimensional passes (3 gradients x 3 axes + 6 tensor components x 3 axes) over 4.28e9 voxels plus 25-50 % halo overhead = ~6e9 voxel-passes at scipy.ndimage's 50-100 M voxel-passes/s (single-threaded, slower on the strided axes) = 60-120 min single-threaded; the analytic eigendecomposition of 5.4e8 3x3 matrices is ~5-10 min, not 1-2. scipy does not multithread, so two memory-limited workers give 2x, not 4x. With the unsubsampled fits above the honest single-container total is 4-8 h; with subsampling ~1.5-3 h. The sibling's 2-D per-slice variant measured 11-15 s per 16-slice slab on the real volume (st_axis.log), ~30 min for all 116 slabs.
refuted_claims.fix: Quote 1.5-3 h for the 3-D variant with subsampled fits (under 1 h across siblings), or adopt the measured 2-D per-slice tensor for the in-plane angle (30 min) and compute the 3-D tensor only at stride 2 in the clean zones for t(z).

refuted_claims.claim: Phantom: '400^3 volumes ... circular; 2:1 elliptical squash' with bars 'circular <= 0.15 mm; 2:1 ellipse <= 1.0 mm; buckles <= 0.5 mm', computed at 69 and 34.56 um.
