refuted_claims.why_wrong: 400 voxels at 69 um is 27.6 mm, so the phantom roll has R <= 11.6 mm (tools/umb/phantom.py: R_out = 0.42 x 400) against the measured 37-40 mm section: ~25 windings instead of ~60-130, lever-arm weights and sector statistics at the wrong scale; at 34.56 um the cube is 13.8 mm and cannot hold any section. A '2:1 squash' is an affine map of a circle, so its normals satisfy the affine-squeeze model exactly: a fit that passes it has been validated against its own assumption (the sibling's 'crushed max 0.055 mm' is this circularity). Real crushing of carbonised papyrus is inextensional (perimeter-preserving folding and buckling), never affine, so the <= 1.0 mm bar says nothing about PHerc0268.
refuted_claims.fix: Phantoms at the real scale (>= 1200^2 section at level 3, 32-64 slices in z) with inextensional sections: closed curves of conserved arc length made from the circle by inserted folds of random radius 0.3-3 mm and a flat contact side; a two-block oblique shear phantom (plane at 30-60 degrees to z, 2-6 mm offset); report the estimator's bias and whether it flags, with no bar below the measured resolution of the loop test.

refuted_claims.claim: 'b_sector normalises the total weight in each 10-degree azimuth sector ... this is what keeps the LS point at the centre of symmetric non-circular sections instead of on their evolute.'
refuted_claims.why_wrong: For nested ellipses the normals at parameters +t and -t intersect on the long axis at x = (a^2-b^2)/a cos t, so every point between the centre and the evolute cusp is a concurrency point of some normal pair; with a Cauchy scale capped at 1.5 mm the IRLS objective has a continuum of local minima along the long axis and the inlier set at the true centre is four arcs of 4-7 degrees of parameter (~6 % of voters). Equal sector weights do not remove these minima; they only stop dense sectors outvoting sparse ones. What actually protects the output is the basin test flagging the slab (the sibling's end-cap slabs already show 2 clusters and conditioning 0.10-0.11), so the fit does not deliver a <= 1 mm centre for a 2:1 section, it refuses.
refuted_claims.fix: Keep sector balancing for sampling asymmetry only. For non-circular slabs define the centre as the area centroid of the region enclosed by the innermost closed streamline of the tangent field (any interior point of a convex innermost winding gives single ray crossings), or an explicit inextensional-section model; report the point-fit's local-minimum structure, not a 1 mm number.

refuted_claims.claim: 'w_i = ... / (sigma_theta^2 R_i^2 + sigma_0^2)' Gauss-Markov weighting of the angular lever arm, and the curvature gate, prevent the buckle cluster from shifting the global axis.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: With sigma_theta = 3 degrees and sigma_0 = 0.15 mm a voter at R = 2 mm gets weight 30 and one at R = 40 mm gets 0.23: the innermost 3 mm, which in a crushed slab is the chaotic material, outvotes the outer 30 mm by ~100x per voter, inverting the stated intent. Random or shard lines within 1.5 mm of c always have |d| < R < s, so they are permanent high-weight inliers. The dominant error is not angular noise but structural non-concurrency, which is not a function of R; and the curvature gate (kappa from the doubled-angle field smoothed at 0.41 mm, noise ~0.24 rad/mm) only resolves buckle radii of ~1-3 mm; 0.3-0.8 mm buckles are caught, if at all, by the coherence drop.
refuted_claims.fix: No lever-arm weighting (or floor R at r_core); exclude voters with R < r_core(z) and iterate fit -> r_core -> refit; report per-radial-band centres (as st_axis.py's 3 bands) and require inner/outer band concentricity within tolerance; send everything inside r_core to U3.

refuted_claims.claim: H2: 't(z) = eigenvector of the smallest eigenvalue ... all sheet normals are perpendicular to the roll axis even when crushed radially'; 'if tilt > 3 degrees' is the exception branch.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: True only for cylindrical buckling with fold lines parallel to the axis. Axial compression, telescoping and the oblique end crush produce folds with fold lines across the axis whose normals tilt toward z by up to 90 degrees, so the null vector of T(z) is undefined or biased and cylindricity is only 'reported', never gated. The session's level-4 track shows the centroid moving 10.8 mm in y over 70.8 mm of z (8.7 degrees) and the focal track 5.1 mm (4.1 degrees): the > 3 degree branch (32-slice slabs, oblique projection) is the default path for this scroll, not an exception, and the 2-D sibling code has no tilt handling at all.
refuted_claims.fix: Estimate t once per 10-20 mm from the clean zones (ratio of the two smallest eigenvalues >= 3 required), apply it as a global oblique slab geometry, gate slabs whose cylindricity fails as 'non-cylindrical' (U3), and validate t against the finite-difference direction of c(z) only over >= 20 mm baselines.

refuted_claims.claim: H4: Poincare index 'valid only when >= 80 % of loop samples are admissible'; loops of 1.5-16 mm; 'the smallest radius from which all admissible loops give index +1 is the innermost coherent winding: the axis is guaranteed inside it'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: (a) With 20 % gaps the wrapped doubled-angle increment between non-adjacent admissible samples can exceed pi, so the branch choice and the integer result are arbitrary. (b) The director field has half-integer defects at every fragment end, crack tip and fold core; a loop with one such defect inside and its partner outside returns +1/2 or +3/2, and two wrong branches can fake a +1. (c) 16 mm covers under half of the measured 37-40 mm section, so a slab whose only coherent windings are outside 16 mm is 'indeterminate' for no physical reason. (d) The far field fixes the enclosed charge at +1 for any loop in coherent material, so 'index +1 on all loops >= r_core' is trivially true; r_core measures where circles about the current c avoid defects, which depends on c being right and on circles being the wrong loop shape for non-circular sections.
refuted_claims.fix: Compute the index on the smoothed doubled-angle vector field with no gaps, demanding |v| > v_min on the whole loop; use closed streamlines of the tangent field as loops (they exist exactly where the section is a nested foliation), extend to the full mask radius, define r_core by the innermost closed streamline, and store the half-integer defects as U3 seeds.

refuted_claims.claim: H6: 'Where consecutive determined slabs differ by more than 3 combined sigma and the index test fails between them (shear/collapse), U1 receives a C0 knot.'
refuted_claims.why_wrong: That detects shear planes nearly perpendicular to z only. A collapse plane at 30-60 degrees to z, the usual case, puts both displaced blocks in the same slab for 10-20 mm of z with a changing fraction; the single IRLS centre drifts smoothly from one block's axis to the other's, passing within sheets of neither, with no 3-sigma jump and with index +1 (the loop encloses the charge of whichever block dominates). The output is a smooth, confident, wrong axis, the drift/twist the umbilicus is meant to prevent.
refuted_claims.fix: Per-slab multi-centre test independent of z: refit the residual set (voters with |d| > 1 mm, >= 10 % of voters) and accept a second centre when its conditioning >= 0.1 and inlier fraction >= 0.5 (st_axis.py already implements this); the z-range over which two centres coexist is the shear band, bounded by two C0 knots, with no single centre inside it.

refuted_claims.claim: 'Admissible voxels: ... c_p0 and tr0 = 99th percentile of the same quantities measured in PHerc0268's own air/ash null regions'; 'Air is identified as the zero-mask exterior ring just inside the erosion margin ... ash as low-trace interior regions.'
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The masked volume's exterior is exactly zero (fill_value 0; out-of-mask chunks are not even stored), so the 'air just inside the erosion margin' has no noise statistics at all, and 'ash = low trace' then 'tr0 = 99th percentile of ash trace' is circular: the threshold reproduces the definition.
refuted_claims.fix: Phase-randomised null of the same slab (same power spectrum, no structure; st_axis.py's phase_null) or a Monte Carlo on noise matched to the slice-difference spectrum of coherent regions; thresholds = 99th percentile of that null's coherence, contrast threshold from the real slab's own distribution with its effect reported.

refuted_claims.claim: 'Bridging crushed/ash sections from the clean top and bottom' and the clean-zone bars 'conditioning >= 0.3, inlier fraction >= 0.5, ellipse semi-major <= 0.5 mm'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The ends are not clean: the level-4 mask area ramps from 34k to 266k voxels over ~18 mm at each end (oblique end faces or a tilted roll), so the top and bottom ~18 mm are partial sections whose eroded mask edge is a cut face. The only two real level-3 slabs analysed so far (st_axis.log, z = 2.2-4.4 mm into the mask) give conditioning 0.10-0.11, 26-39 % of voters more than 1 mm off, two >= 25 % clusters, and an 11.2 mm jump between adjacent 1.1 mm slabs. The 0.3 / 0.5 thresholds have no measured basis on this scroll or on a phantom of its scale; if the middle third is crushed, the clean material may be two bands of ~20 mm.
refuted_claims.fix: Define the clean zone empirically: full-section slabs (mask area within 10 % of the volume median) with sector coverage >= 0.75; set the conditioning and inlier thresholds from the real-scale phantom and the clean-zone distribution, and report the clean fraction of z before any bar is quoted.

refuted_claims.claim: 'The carrier cannot be papyrus fibres: recto fibres are tangent to the winding and verso fibres are parallel to the axis, so neither family projects back to the axis' ('miss the axis by exactly R').
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The owner's 'shared origin of the curves' is the centre of curvature, not the tangent line; a circumferential recto fibre is a circle about the axis and its centre of curvature IS the axis, so the geometric refutation is wrong. The valid reasons to reject fibre inversion are resolution (fibres marginal at 8.64 um, absent at 34.56/69 um), cost (2.2e12 voxels, no disk), and redundancy: in-sheet fibre curvature equals the sheet's in-plane curvature d(theta)/ds, which the orientation field already provides, and in crushed zones it follows the buckles exactly as the sheet normals do.
refuted_claims.fix: Reject U2-fibre on resolution, cost and redundancy; keep H7 as a direction-only gate; drop the 'miss by R' argument from the audit so it cannot be refuted by the owner.

refuted_claims.claim: 'Nothing is learned, so no parchment or macro-shape memorisation can enter.'
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The estimator is physics-free, but two of its validation metrics are not: the ray-crossing test reads the organizers' m7 surface model and the cross-check reads the lasagna normals and normal grids, all learned products of unknown training data and provenance. A collapse-shape or parchment bias in m7 would pass through the 'validation' unseen, exactly the mode-2/5 contamination the sentence denies.
refuted_claims.fix: Run the ray-crossing test on the raw slab mean image as well as on m7 and report both; treat disagreement between them as a finding about m7; use the lasagna field only where its angular agreement with the raw-CT tensor is itself reported.

verdict.surviving_core: What survives both lenses, restated: (1) the physical carrier is the sheet layering, not fibres: at level 3 (69.1 um; 1855 x 1519 x 1519 uint8, 128^3 uncompressed chunks, ~2.4 GB actually stored) sheets are 1.5-3 voxels and the 0.3-0.6 mm pitch is 4-9 voxels, so a structure tensor (derivative sigma ~1-1.2 voxel, integration 3-5 voxels) measures the layering normal, and only its first eigenvector carries information; level 4 is at Nyquist for the pitch and is used for nothing but masks and cross-checks; level 0/1 are never processed volumetrically. (2) The inversion is a per-slab robust concurrency fit of in-plane normal lines (unsigned, linear residual d_i = u_i.(c - p_i), Cauchy/Tukey IRLS with a floored and capped scale, mask eroded ~0.8-1 mm, debris excluded, azimuth-sector balancing for sampling asymmetry only, NO lever-arm weighting, voters subsampled to <= 300k per slab, 9-10 starts for the basin test, split-half, conditioning ratio, inlier fraction, per-band concentricity) whose honest output in deformed sections is a flag plus a disc, never a point: the point is reported only where the basin, conditioning, coverage and ray-crossing tests pass, and those thresholds are set from a real-scale inextensional phantom, not declared. (3) A topological core envelope exists, but as the innermost closed streamline of the gap-free smoothed doubled-angle field (index computed only where |v| > v_min on the loop, half-integer defects recorded as U3 seeds), extended to the full ~40 mm section radius; the deliverable per slab is {z, c, Sigma or disc of radius r_core, tilt, conditioning, inlier fraction, multi-centre record with secondary centres, flags}. (4) Shear handling by per-slab multi-centre detection (residual refit), with C0 knots at both ends of the band where two centres coexist and no single centre inside it; indeterminate slabs are bridged by U1 with a declared envelope; the radial direction inside crushed zones comes from the local normal field, and absolute winding numbers are assigned only where the ray-crossing test passes, i.e. not across the crushed zone. (5) Axis tilt is a global, slowly varying quantity (measured 4-9 degrees on this scroll) estimated from the clean zones and applied as oblique slab geometry, with non-cylindrical slabs gated out. (6) Compute, corrected: level 3 streamed by 128-slice chunk rows with 16-slice halos at ~12 MB/s with >= 32 threads (~4 min), one worker or two y-tiled workers (~3.3-6.5 GB peak; tmpfs counts as RAM and 6.5 GB is available today), 3-D tensor 1-2 h single-threaded or the measured 2-D per-slice variant ~30 min (11-15 s per 16-slice slab), subsampled fits and bootstraps ~10 min, ray test on m7 level 3 (~0.8 GB compressed), lasagna cross-check at level 4 only, level-2 refinement only for slabs with r_core <= 6 mm; ~1.5-3 h on one container, under 1 h across the siblings; per-slab JSON committed, no field kept. (7) Nothing learned enters the estimator; learned products (m7, lasagna, normal grids) are cross-checks whose disagreement is reported, and the fibre route is a direction-only gate on twelve 384^3 level-0 blocks. A parallel implementation of (1)-(2) and part of (4) already exists in the repo (tools/umb/st_axis.py, axis_spline.py, phantom.py under DECL-UMB-1, with a real level-3 run started in logs/umb/PHerc0268); the genuinely new pieces of the hardened U2 are the gated 3-D tilt estimate, the streamline-based core envelope, the inner-radius exclusion, and the real-scale inextensional phantom, and those should be added to it rather than built twice.
verdict.missing_validation: Not validated anywhere in the proposal or the repo: (a) a phantom at the real scale (section radius 37-40 mm, 60-130 windings, >= 1200^2 at level 3) with inextensional (perimeter-conserving) folding and a flat contact side instead of an affine squash, plus a two-block oblique-shear phantom at 30-60 degrees to z, each reporting bias AND whether the slab is flagged; (b) the conditioning (0.3), inlier (0.5), basin (0.2 mm) and ellipse (0.5 mm) thresholds have no measured basis: the only two real level-3 slabs give conditioning 0.10-0.11, and the thresholds must come from the real-scale phantom and the clean-zone distribution; (c) the extent of the clean zone on PHerc0268 itself (the end caps are partial sections; the full-z run of st_axis.py has not been completed, only z = 0-80 of 1855); (d) the axis tilt (4-9 degrees from level-4 centroid and focal tracks) and whether the roll is cylindrical enough for a null-vector t(z) at all (cylindricity never gated); (e) the Poincare index with gaps and half-integer defects: no test shows the circular-loop index is correct on crushed material, and no streamline-closure test exists yet; (f) the null calibration: the proposed air/ash null is unobtainable from a zero-filled masked volume, and the phase-randomised null's 99th percentile (0.47-0.54 measured in the two slabs) has not been checked against a synthetic-noise null; (g) whether the reconstruction rotation centre coincides with the image centre (759.5, 759.5) of a masked, possibly cropped volume, on which the ring diagnostic and polar filter depend; (h) the independence of the validation from learned products: the ray-crossing test needs a raw-CT version alongside m7, and m7's own agreement with the raw layering has not been measured; (i) the memory plan has never been run: no `free -m` before/after a worker, no halo-16 buffer accounting, no confirmation that the sibling containers can be dispatched or that their proxies deliver ~12 MB/s; (j) the sibling's phantom claims (clean max 0.087 mm, crushed max 0.055 mm) are a seed-0 development run on an 11.6 mm affine phantom and are not evidence for PHerc0268; (k) the ordering fit -> r_core -> refit excluding R < r_core has no test showing it converges rather than oscillating in crushed slabs.

audit.strategy: Keep the owner's intent (local frames for sheared bundles so they unroll independently; umbilicus as the origin that sets the radial direction and winding numbers) but replace the two mechanisms named in U3 that cannot work on PHerc0268 - the 3-D thinning skeleton of inter-layer air gaps, and mean-shift clustering of local curvature centres - with a per-z-slab robust fit of a radial direction field to the sheet normals. The origin model is a point OR a slit (elliptic/confocal coordinates, c=0 reduces to a point) so that a flattened/crushed spiral is one origin, not several. 'Many centres' is a residual-driven hypothesis that must pass four gates (MDL gain, compact support, topological separation of its sheets from the primary bundle, z-persistence) before it is accepted. Centres are tracked across slabs into a graph with explicit break-points, which is what U1 then smooths (never across a break). Winding numbers are assigned per bundle by monotone ray/hyperbola casting from the bundle origin; cross-bundle offsets are integer edge labels that are either measured from a traceable sheet or reported as unknown - never invented. Everything runs on level 3 normals (69 um; the lowest level where the 0.3-0.6 mm pitch is 4-9 voxels) with candidate origins evaluated on the level-4 grid, streamed slab by slab from S3 so nothing exceeds ~6 GB RAM or 1 GB disk. Every stage has a hand-free, ground-truth-free metric with a pass threshold, plus a deterministic geometric phantom test (not training data) that checks the false-split rate on flattened spirals and the split recall on sheared ones. Mode-1 risk of the hardened version itself (the slit model forcing a shape) is bounded by the residual gates and by reporting the alignment distribution, not just the fit.
audit.summary_of_method_as_specified: U3 as written: (a) segment the inter-layer spaces (air gaps between windings) in 3-D, (b) compute their topological skeleton (thinning / medial axis), (c) from the skeleton and/or from the centres of curvature of the local sheet patches, build a cloud of candidate centre points, (d) cluster them (mean-shift) into a 'web' of local centres (mini-umbilici), one per fragment bundle, (e) link centres across z, (f) decide per region whether one or several centres apply, and (g) assign winding numbers per bundle relative to its own mini-umbilicus so sheared sections unroll independently. The implicit assumptions are: air gaps exist and are resolvable wherever a centre is needed; the medial axis of the gap space encodes 'centres'; a bundle is locally a circular spiral so its curvature centres pile up at one point; distinct clusters of curvature centres mean distinct physical bundles; and winding numbers from different bundles can be reconciled into one absolute index.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Evolute false-split. The centres of curvature of a non-circular closed curve do not pile up at a point; they lie on its evolute. For an ellipse with semi-axes a>b the evolute is an astroid with cusps at distance (a^2-b^2)/a along the long axis and (a^2-b^2)/b along the short axis - the second one is OUTSIDE the ellipse whenever a/b > sqrt(2). Mean-shift on curvature centres of a flattened spiral therefore returns 2-4 well-separated, z-persistent, high-density 'mini-umbilici' for a single continuous roll. Hough voting of normal lines has the same defect (line density peaks on the evolute). The one-vs-many rule then splits a single sheet into bundles exactly in proportion to how crushed it is - the straightjacket in reverse: a point-centre model is being forced onto a shape that has none, and the method 'explains' the misfit by inventing fragments.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: The crushed core region of PHerc0268 (inner ~10-20 mm, mid-height of the 128 mm scroll at level 3) has windings flattened to aspect ratio ~1.5-2.5. Curvature centres of a winding with a=12 mm, b=6 mm form cusps at 9 mm and 18 mm from the true centre - the second lies beyond the winding itself, in the next windings' territory. The pipeline would report two to four bundles with centres millimetres apart in every slab of the crushed zone, assign independent winding numbers to each, and the unroller would then cut one continuous sheet into 2-4 'fragments', each with the radial direction wrong by up to 90 degrees on the shoulders. Nothing in U3 as specified can detect this because the fake centres persist across z just like real ones.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: The topological skeleton of the inter-layer spaces is not a set of centres. The gap between two sheets is itself a sheet-like volume; its medial axis is a medial SURFACE (the mid-gap sheet), so thinning returns more sheets, not points. The 1-D 'web' only appears where the skeleton degenerates - at junctions created by holes and cracks (see mode 4) and at the core cavity. The umbilicus is a property of how the sheets wind (their normals / their topology), not of the gap skeleton, so U3 conflates two unrelated objects.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Running a 3-D thinning on the low-m7 (gap) space of a level-3 slab of PHerc0268 (32 x 1519 x 1519) yields a stack of ~60 medial surfaces nested like the windings, with branch junctions at every tear. Projected to xy they give no centre at all in the clean top and bottom (where there IS a clean cavity, the cavity is one blob whose centroid is just the mask-centroid proxy we already have); in the crushed core they give a dense tangle of junction points whose mean-shift modes are determined by tear positions, not by the roll geometry.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Material mismatch inside U3's own prior. The crushed core of a carbonised papyrus roll is not a spiral with gaps: the inner windings are collapsed onto each other, sheets are fused with no resolvable air layer, and the collapsed stack behaves like a flat slit (two 'foci'), while sharp buckles have radii of curvature of the order of the sheet thickness (0.1-0.5 mm). So (i) the gap-space skeleton vanishes exactly in the region U3 was proposed for, and (ii) the curvature centres of buckles are strong, compact, z-persistent clusters at radius ~0.2 mm from the fold that look like perfect mini-umbilici. A parchment-derived or 'circular arc' elasticity prior would make both worse, but even without learning, the circular-spiral assumption is the mismatch.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: In the crushed core at mid-height, a single buckled sheet with 5 folds of radius ~0.3 mm casts 5 tight curvature-centre clusters, each supported by hundreds of thousands of level-0-equivalent voxels and persisting over many mm of z (a fold runs along z). Mean-shift reports 5 bundles with 5 centres; each bundle is a 1 mm wide strip of one sheet; the per-bundle winding number is '1' everywhere; the global coordinate is destroyed inside the only region where the letters are expected (First Letters prize target is the crushed core).

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Scale mismatch for the quantities U3 needs. Curvature (second derivative of the sheet) must be estimated from a window much wider than the sheet thickness but much narrower than the radius; at level 4 (138 um) the pitch is 2-4 voxels and sheets are ~1 voxel, so neither gaps nor normals are reliable; at level 3 (69 um) normals are usable (pitch 4-9 voxels) but curvature of an outer winding (R=20-30 mm) over a 10-voxel window is a bend of ~1-2 degrees, below the structure-tensor noise floor, so outer-winding curvature centres scatter over tens of mm. At level 2 (35 um) the slab needed for the same physical window is 8x the memory (the full volume is 34 GB uint8; a 32-slice slab with float tensors is ~1.7 GB, feasible but the gap skeleton still sits at 1-3 voxels and is partial-volume dominated). Level 0/1 full-volume processing is impossible on 15 GB and is unnecessary for a macro quantity.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Level-3 curvature-centre cloud for an outer slab of PHerc0268: inner windings (R<5 mm) vote within ~0.5 mm of the axis, outer windings (R>15 mm, which hold most of the voxels) vote with radial error of +-10 mm or more, so the density-weighted mode is pulled by the outer windings' noise and the mean-shift bandwidth that works for the inner windings (0.5 mm) sees the outer votes as dozens of spurious modes. Using level 4 instead, normals from a 1-voxel-thick sheet with a 2-voxel gap are ~30 degrees noisy and the gap space is not segmentable at all.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Three contamination paths. (i) Thinning is unstable: every hole in a sheet joins two gap spaces, every crack joins radially, every debris grain splits a gap - each creates skeleton branches and junctions, so bundle boundaries follow artefacts. (ii) Any curved foreign surface (hair, insect cuticle, mineral shell fragment) votes a tight curvature-centre cluster. (iii) Two systematic fake centres with perfect z-persistence: the scanner ring artefacts (concentric about the reconstruction axis - every ring voxel votes for the rotation axis) and the boundary of the '-masked' volume (the mask edge is a smooth closed surface whose normals all point at the mask centroid, i.e. at the existing fl4 proxy). Without erosion and ring exclusion the method rediscovers the mask centroid with high confidence and calls it validated.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: In PHerc0268 level 3, the mask boundary alone contributes a closed ~105 mm circumference x 32 slices of coherent normal votes per slab - more coherent than any papyrus winding - and the ring artefacts, if present after masking, add a second coherent vote at the rotation axis. The top-ranked 'umbilicus' per slab is then the mask/rotation centre, which is offset from the true axis by whatever the scroll's off-centre position is (typically several mm, and varying with z if the scroll is tilted in the holder), and the result passes any z-smoothness check. Meanwhile, in the crushed zone, a few cracks running radially connect gap spaces so the gap-skeleton 'bundles' are split along crack lines, not along shear surfaces.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: U3 has no trained network, so it cannot memorise collapse shapes in the deep-learning sense, but the same effect enters through (a) hyperparameters (mean-shift bandwidth, cluster-count criterion, minimum support) tuned by hand on PHerc0257 / PHerc0490A and frozen, and (b) any temptation to add a learned 'bundle detector' or a prior on the number of bundles. A rule like 'crushed scrolls have N bundles' or a bandwidth that matches one scroll's winding pitch is macro-shape memorisation by hand.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A bandwidth of 0.5 mm chosen because it separates PHerc0257's inner windings becomes, on PHerc0268's crushed core where the local 'pitch' after collapse is ~0.15 mm (sheets fused), a rule that merges 3-4 real sheets into one bundle, or, with the opposite tuning, splits one buckled sheet into many. The fix is to derive scales from the slab itself (measured pitch from the radial crossing sequence) and to require the phantom tests to pass over a range of pitches and aspect ratios, not at one value.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Winding numbers are only defined relative to one origin along a continuous sheet. 'Per-bundle winding numbers' are local integers; turning them into absolute winding numbers (the owner's stated purpose for the umbilicus) requires an integer offset per pair of adjacent bundles, and that offset is measurable only where a sheet is physically traceable across the bundle boundary - which is precisely where the boundary was declared because the sheet is sheared or torn. This is a global integer-labelling (phase-unwrapping) problem with possibly inconsistent cycles, not a clustering output. If the pipeline silently assigns offsets (e.g. by radius ordering) it fabricates continuity.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Suppose the crushed core of PHerc0268 legitimately splits into bundle A (upper-left slab region, 40 windings) and bundle B (a splayed fan of 6 sheets with its own curvature). B's sheets 1-6 are some windings k..k+5 of A. If the shear surface between them is fully torn, k is unknowable from geometry alone; ordering B's sheets by distance from A's centre would give k wrong by the amount of slip (several windings). A rendered 'sheet 23' from A and 'sheet 23' from B would then be different physical sheets, which contaminates any later text join - the exact drift/twist the umbilicus was meant to prevent.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Connectivity across z is a multi-target tracking problem with births, deaths, merges and splits. A gap-skeleton or mean-shift centre has no identity across slabs, so a naive nearest-neighbour link swaps identities when two centres pass within a bandwidth of each other, and a centre that disappears for one slab (artefact, local fusion) is re-born as a 'new bundle', resetting its winding numbers.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: In PHerc0268 a real secondary bundle drifting 1 mm per 4.4 mm slab crosses the primary axis's xy position in the slab where the fan rejoins the main stack; nearest-neighbour linking swaps the two tracks, so above that z the main stack's windings are counted in the fan's frame. Separately, a single slab with a debris-induced skeleton tangle makes the main centre jump 3 mm, which breaks the track into two tracks with independent winding counts.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Slab thickness versus axis tilt. Any per-slab 2-D centre blurs by T*tan(theta) when the axis is tilted by theta across a slab of thickness T. This is minor for an upright scroll but a crushed, possibly bent core can tilt locally.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A 32-slice level-4 slab is 4.4 mm; at 10 degrees tilt the centre estimate is smeared by 0.8 mm, larger than the 0.45 mm pitch, enough to misassign the innermost winding index by one. Mitigation: after a first pass, re-slab perpendicular to the fitted local axis (or halve the slab) and re-fit; convergence in two iterations is itself a check.

audit.hardened_alternative:
DATA AND LEVELS. Stream from S3 per slab, no local copy of a full volume (1 GB disk, 11 GB tmpfs). Normals at level 3 (69 um; pitch 4-9 voxels, sheet 1.5-3 voxels) - either the organizer normal grids if their resolution and coverage pass a line-by-line audit (they are community/organizer code, treat as untrusted until read), or our own structure tensor on the m7 surface-probability volume (gradient sigma 1.5 vox, integration sigma 3.5 vox), computed in slabs of 32 level-3 slices (74 M voxels; float32 gradients + 6 tensor components ~2.7 GB peak), downsampled to level-4 geometry for the fit (a 928 x 760 x 760 grid). Sheet voxels = m7 > 0.5 AND structure-tensor coherence > 0.3 AND inside the CT mask eroded by 10 level-4 voxels (kills the mask-boundary decoy). Ring-artefact exclusion: evaluate the same alignment energy on the FOV-but-outside-mask region; any peak there marks the rotation axis, and voxels whose normal passes within 0.3 mm of that axis AND whose coherence is high only in the azimuthal direction (ring signature) are removed; fraction of votes removed is logged.

STAGE 1 - ONE ORIGIN PER SLAB, POINT-OR-SLIT MODEL. For a candidate origin O = (x, y, c, phi) with slit half-length c >= 0 and orientation phi, define the radial direction field d_O(v) as the outward normal of the confocal ellipse through v in elliptic coordinates (x = c cosh(mu) cos(nu), y = c sinh(mu) sin(nu); d = grad mu); c = 0 gives the ordinary point-radial field. Alignment energy per voxel: a(v) = |cos(n_v, d_O(v))| (sign of the normal is irrelevant). Robust slab energy E(O) = sum over sheet voxels of w_v * rho(a(v)), with w_v = m7 * coherence and rho a Tukey biweight on the angle arccos(a) with cutoff 30 degrees (voxels misaligned by more than 30 degrees contribute zero, so a sheared fan cannot drag the primary origin). Optimise: point model first - coarse grid of candidate (x, y) every 10 level-4 voxels (1.4 mm) over the eroded mask (~5000 candidates) using a stratified random subsample of 20k sheet voxels per slab; refine the best 5 maxima with Nelder-Mead on all sheet voxels of the slab; then refine (c, phi) locally with c in [0, 8 mm], phi over 12 angles, accepting c > 0 only if E improves by more than the MDL cost of 2 parameters AND the split-half (odd/even slices) estimates of c agree within 0.5 mm. Slab thickness 32 level-3 slices (2.2 mm); after the first pass, re-slab perpendicular to the smoothed local axis and repeat once.

STAGE 2 - ONE VERSUS MANY (RESIDUAL-DRIVEN, FOUR GATES). Residual set R = sheet voxels with a(v) < cos 30 degrees under the primary origin. Connected components of R in 3-D (within the slab, 26-connectivity after a 1-voxel opening at level 4) are candidate bundles. For each component with support >= 5e4 level-3 voxels (~16 mm^3), fit its own point-or-slit origin by the same energy. Accept the component as a bundle only if ALL of: (G1 MDL) its own-origin robust energy exceeds its energy under the primary origin by more than the parameter cost and its median alignment rises from < 0.6 to > 0.85; (G2 compactness) its support is one connected component spanning at least 2 windings radially (>= 2 crossings along the local radial direction) and at least 15 degrees of azimuth about its own origin - this rejects single-fold curvature clusters (mode 2) and hairs/debris (mode 4); (G3 topological separation) the m7 > 0.5 sheet volume of the component, eroded by one level-3 voxel, is NOT 3-D connected within the slab to the sheet volume of the primary support - i.e. there is a low-probability shear/tear surface between them (this is the one legitimate use of the inter-layer-space idea: a separating gap/crack must exist; a flattened but continuous spiral fails G3 and stays one bundle); (G4 persistence) the same component (tracked in Stage 3) exists in >= 3 consecutive slabs (>= 6.6 mm) with origin drift <= 1 mm per slab. Iterate: residuals of accepted bundles are re-examined for a third origin, maximum 6 origins per slab, every acceptance logged with its gate values. No clustering of curvature centres anywhere; mean-shift is dropped. The curvature-centre cloud may be computed as a DIAGNOSTIC only (its spread measures local aspect ratio) and never drives a decision.

STAGE 3 - CONNECTIVITY ACROSS Z. Multi-target tracking of origins across slabs: cost = origin distance (gate 1.5 mm per 2.2 mm slab, i.e. < 35 degrees tilt) + Jaccard distance of the supports' xy footprints (gate 0.5); solved by Hungarian assignment with birth/death; identity swaps are prevented by the footprint term, not by position alone. Each track is a bundle with a 3-D axis polyline. Smoothing per track: Huber-robust smoothing spline, knot spacing 5 mm, with explicit BREAK-POINTS inserted where (a) the raw origin jumps by more than 1 mm relative to the spline prediction, (b) the slit parameter c changes sign of its orientation or jumps > 2 mm, or (c) G3 separation of the support appears/disappears; the spline is fitted independently on each side of a break and never bridges it. The primary track (largest total support, expected to run top to bottom through the clean regions) is the input data term for U1; U1's global B-spline is allowed to bridge the crushed zone ONLY along the primary track and only where the primary track's own gates passed; secondary tracks keep their own local axes.

STAGE 4 - WINDING NUMBERS PER BUNDLE AND BETWEEN BUNDLES. Within a bundle: on each level-3 slice, cast 72 'rays' from the bundle origin (straight rays for c = 0, confocal hyperbolae for c > 0) through the bundle's support, record sheet crossings (m7 ridge maxima after 20 um smoothing, as in the existing RULES ray-crossing procedure), and assign crossing index k along each ray; link crossings between neighbouring rays by following the sheet tangent (normal perpendicular) over the 5-degree step; a consistent labelling around 360 degrees (closure sum zero) gives the winding number w = k; rays where the crossing count differs from both neighbours by > 1 are flagged non-star-shaped and excluded from the frame; z-propagation by the same tangent-following between slices. Between bundles: build the bundle adjacency graph (bundles whose supports touch); for each edge, attempt to trace a sheet across the boundary with the existing normal-grid patch grower (vc_grow_seg_from_seed with the local bundle axis as its radial reference) from 3 seeds on each side; if a traced patch connects crossing w_A in A to crossing w_B in B, the edge offset is w_B - w_A with its evidence recorded; if no trace succeeds the offset is UNKNOWN and the two bundles keep separate winding frames, reported as such in the output (frame id + local winding number). Cycle consistency of known offsets is checked (sum around every cycle must be zero); a violated cycle marks all its edges as disputed. Absolute winding numbers are only reported for the connected component of the adjacency graph that contains the primary track with all offsets known; everything else is 'local frame' - this is a deliberate refusal to fabricate.

SCALES DERIVED FROM DATA, NOT TUNED. Pitch is measured per slab from the median radial crossing spacing (expected 0.3-0.6 mm) and used to set the ray-crossing smoothing and the G2 '2 windings' threshold; the 30-degree robust cutoff and the slab thickness are fixed physically motivated constants and are varied in the phantom test to show insensitivity. No learned component, no En-Gedi / parchment, no other-scroll statistics anywhere in U3.

validation_metrics.name: Radial alignment score (per slab, per bundle)
validation_metrics.definition: Median over the bundle's sheet voxels of |cos(n_v, d_O(v))| under the bundle's fitted origin, plus the fraction of voxels with alignment below cos 30 degrees (the residual fraction). Same quantity as the repo's sheetcheck |cos| but over all sheet voxels, not a seed.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Median >= 0.90 and residual fraction <= 5% in the clean top and bottom of PHerc0268; median >= 0.80 and residual fraction <= 15% in the crushed core after the multi-origin model; and the multi-origin model must raise the crushed-core median by >= 0.10 over the single point-origin model, otherwise the extra origins are rejected.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Uses only the m7 surface probability and the structure-tensor normals of the volume itself; computed on all sheet voxels of each level-3 slab (streamed), reported as a per-slab table and a z-profile. Requires no segmentation, no labels, no human input.

validation_metrics.name: Star-shapedness / ray monotonicity
validation_metrics.definition: Fraction of the 72 rays (or confocal hyperbolae) per slice from the bundle origin on which the sheet-crossing count differs from both neighbouring rays by at most 1 and no sheet is crossed twice (no sign flip of n . d along one sheet). Also the 360-degree closure of the winding labelling (returns to the same index).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: >= 95% of rays monotone and closure exact on >= 95% of slices in the clean regions; >= 80% of rays monotone within each accepted bundle in the crushed core; closure failures are logged per slice and any slice with closure error > 1 marks the frame invalid there.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Ray casting on the m7 ridge maxima (20 um-smoothed) from the fitted origin, per level-3 slice; purely geometric, hand-free; a wrong origin (e.g. the mask centroid when the scroll is off-centre, or an evolute cusp) produces non-monotone rays on the shoulders and fails this test directly.

validation_metrics.name: Origin stability (split-half and bootstrap)
validation_metrics.definition: Distance between origins fitted on odd versus even slices of the same slab, and the 95% radius of the bootstrap distribution over 50 random 20k-voxel subsamples; same for the slit parameter c.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Split-half distance <= 0.15 mm (less than half the smallest expected pitch, so the innermost winding index cannot flip) and bootstrap 95% radius <= 0.2 mm; c agreement within 0.5 mm. Slabs failing this are flagged 'undetermined', not smoothed over.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Internal consistency of the estimator on the real data; no reference needed. Costs a few seconds per slab at level 4 candidate resolution.

validation_metrics.name: Agreement with independent hand-free estimators
validation_metrics.definition: Per-z distance between the primary-track origin and (a) the existing fl4 level-4 CT-mask centroid axis points, (b) the centre-of-curvature curve from organizer mesh normals (hercules.pipeline.centre.geometric_centre_curve applied to any organizer tifxyz segment of PHerc0268 that passes audit), (c) the same U3 fit run at level 4 normals instead of level 3.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: (a) within 1.5 mm in the clean top/bottom (the mask centroid is a coarse proxy, divergence in the crushed zone is expected and must be reported, not hidden); (b) within 0.5 mm (one pitch) wherever an audited segment exists; (c) level 3 vs level 4 within 0.3 mm in clean regions. Any disagreement beyond threshold is reported as a finding with the slab alignment scores of both candidates, never resolved by averaging.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: All three comparators are themselves derived from the volume or the organizer meshes without human axis annotation; agreement among methods with different failure modes is the evidence, disagreement localises a problem.

validation_metrics.name: Decoy rejection (mask boundary and scanner axis)
validation_metrics.definition: Alignment energy of the fitted origin computed (i) with and without the 10-voxel mask erosion and (ii) on FOV-outside-mask voxels only; the shift of the origin between (i) variants, and the ratio of the outside-mask peak to the in-scroll peak.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Origin shift between eroded and non-eroded runs <= 0.3 mm (if larger, the non-eroded fit was mask-driven and the eroded one is kept with a logged warning); outside-mask peak ratio <= 0.1 and fewer than 1% of accepted votes come from voxels flagged with the ring signature.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Both are properties of the data and the mask alone; the '-masked.zarr' mask is read from the volume itself (nonzero support).

validation_metrics.name: Geometric phantom suite (unit test, not training data)
validation_metrics.definition: Deterministic synthetic volumes at 69 um voxels: (P1) Archimedean spirals with pitch 0.3-0.6 mm, sheet thickness 100-200 um, aspect ratio 1.0-2.5, Gaussian noise, 5% random holes, 50 debris grains, 3 radial cracks - all ONE sheet; (P2) the same with a sheared fan of 6 sheets slipped by a known number of windings and separated by a tear surface; (P3) a slit-collapsed core (confocal ellipses around a 4 mm slit); (P4) added concentric ring artefacts and a hard mask edge. Known centres, bundles and offsets.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: P1: centre error <= 0.2 mm and false-split rate 0 over all aspect ratios up to 2.5 (the evolute test); P2: bundle recall >= 0.9, false bundles 0, recovered offset exact where the tear leaves a traceable bridge and reported 'unknown' where it does not; P3: c recovered within 0.5 mm; P4: centre shift from rings/mask <= 0.2 mm. Also insensitivity: results unchanged within thresholds for the 30-degree cutoff varied 20-40 degrees and slab thickness 16-64 slices.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: The phantoms are generated by a parametric script with known parameters; this is a test of the algorithm's geometry, involves no real-scroll or parchment data and trains nothing, so it does not touch the toxic-data rule. Each phantom is 32 x 1024 x 1024 level-3 voxels (~34 MB), seconds to generate and fit.

validation_metrics.name: Winding-number consistency across z and across bundles
validation_metrics.definition: Within a bundle: per-slice winding count versus radial crossing count on each monotone ray, and the slice-to-slice change of the winding label of a tangent-tracked sheet. Across bundles: fraction of adjacency edges with a measured offset, and cycle-closure residual of the known offsets.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Winding count equals crossing count +-1 on >= 90% of monotone rays; tracked sheet label changes by 0 between adjacent slices on >= 99% of slices (a change of 1 is a logged possible tear, > 1 invalidates the track there); all cycles of known offsets close to 0, any violated cycle marks its edges disputed; the report must state the number of bundles whose frame is local-only - a value of zero in the crushed core is suspicious and triggers review, not celebration.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Purely from the ray-cast crossings and the patch-grower traces on the volume; offsets are only ever measured, never inferred from radius ordering.

audit.compute_estimate: PHerc0268 at level 3: 1855 slices -> 58 slabs of 32 slices (2.2 mm), each 32 x 1519 x 1519 = 74 M voxels uint8 streamed from S3 (CT level 3 ~4.3 GB and m7 level 3 of similar size, read once, ~2-5 min each at 50-100 MB/s, no disk copy; chunks held in /dev/shm per slab only). Structure tensor per slab: 9 separable Gaussian filters over 74 M float32 voxels ~20-30 s on 4 cores, peak RAM ~2.7 GB; 58 slabs -> ~25 min. If the organizer normal grids pass audit, this step is replaced by a read. Origin fit: 5000 candidates x 20k subsampled voxels = 1e8 cosine evaluations per slab (< 1 s numpy), Nelder-Mead refinement on all ~5-10 M sheet voxels of the slab ~50 evaluations -> ~10-20 s; slit (c, phi) refinement 72 combinations x 20k ~ 2 s; residual components + secondary fits ~ same again; bootstrap 50 x 20k ~ 5 s. Per slab ~1 min, 58 slabs ~1 h, second pass after re-slabbing ~1 h. Tracking and splines: negligible. Ray casting winding numbers: 72 rays x 1855 slices x ~500 samples = 67 M samples, < 5 min. Phantom suite: 4 phantoms x ~10 parameter settings x 34 MB, ~10 min total. Cross-bundle offset tracing with vc_grow_seg_from_seed: 6 seeds per edge, expected < 20 edges, this is the only heavy step (~5-15 min per seed on 4 CPUs by earlier runs) -> 1-3 h, parallelisable over the 7 sibling containers. Total: ~3-4 CPU-hours on one container for U3 proper plus 1-3 h of patch growing, peak RAM ~3-6 GB, disk < 200 MB of outputs (origin tables, tracks, gate logs, phantom results). Level 0/1/2 full-volume processing is not needed and is excluded.
audit.what_to_reject_outright: (1) The 3-D topological skeleton / thinning of the inter-layer air-gap space as a centre finder: it yields medial surfaces, not centres; it vanishes in the fused crushed core of PHerc0268, the one region it was meant for; it is unstable under holes, cracks and debris (every artefact becomes a junction); and the gaps are 1-3 voxels at level 3 and sub-voxel at level 4. Keep only the reduced idea 'a separating low-probability surface must exist between two bundles' as gate G3. (2) Mean-shift or any density clustering of local curvature centres (or of normal-line Hough votes) as the one-vs-many decision: curvature centres of any flattened winding lie on its evolute (astroid cusps, some outside the winding), so a crushed spiral is guaranteed to be split into 2-4 fake bundles; curvature is also unmeasurable for R > ~5 mm at level 3. Curvature-centre clouds may be logged as a diagnostic only. (3) Voting on raw CT edges or normals without mask erosion and ring-artefact exclusion: the masked volume's boundary and the reconstruction axis are the two most coherent 'centres' in the data, and the current fl4 proxy is literally the first of these. (4) Any learned bundle detector, prior on the number of bundles, or hyperparameter frozen from PHerc0257/0490A; any use of En-Gedi or other parchment anywhere in U3 (not even 'reference only' for setting scales). (5) Any reporting of absolute winding numbers across bundles whose connecting sheet was not actually traced - offsets inferred from radius ordering or 'nearest winding' are fabrication and must be refused; the output format must carry a frame id and the gate values that admitted each bundle. (6) Processing at level 0, 1 or full level 2 for the axis: infeasible on 15 GB / 1 GB disk and unnecessary for a macro quantity; the axis is estimated at level 3/4 and only the cross-bundle sheet traces touch finer levels through the existing patch grower.

refuted_claims.claim: The point-or-slit (confocal ellipse) origin model makes 'a flattened/crushed spiral one origin, not several' and bounds the mode-1 risk.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Confocal ellipses share a constant focal distance c^2 = a^2 - b^2, so their aspect ratio changes with radius (inner windings very flat, outer nearly round). A crushed roll whose windings keep a roughly constant aspect ratio (affine squeeze, the model the existing DECL-UMB-1 run already accepted on PHerc0268 slab z=48) has c growing linearly with a: for s = b/a = 0.6, c runs from ~0.8 a_in to ~0.8 a_out (4 mm to >20 mm across 40 windings), outside the proposal's c <= 8 mm box. Worked numbers for a = 20 mm, b = 12 mm with c fitted at 8 mm: at the 45-degree and 30-degree shoulders the true layer normal is 21 degrees off the confocal field, and 25-28 degrees off the point field. That is right at the 30-degree Tukey cutoff, so every shoulder of every squeezed winding lands in the residual set R, in a connected wedge spanning many windings and >15 degrees of azimuth, with its own excellent point origin near the evolute cusp, persistent in z. It passes G1 (if G1 were consistent, see below), G2 and G4. The evolute false split that the audit correctly attributed to mean-shift is reproduced by the residual gate. Also the stadium (racetrack) shape of a stack collapsed between two flat faces has parallel normals along the flat runs: they have no finite concurrency point at all; near the ends of the flat runs the confocal field is 30+ degrees off.
refuted_claims.fix: Model set per slab = {point, affine squeeze M(v-c) = R diag(1,s^2) R^T (constant aspect), slit/confocal}, chosen by a calibrated criterion (median-residual improvement >= 30 % AND split-half agreement, as DECL-UMB-1 does), never by an uncalibrated 'MDL cost'. Report the per-voxel misalignment distribution under the accepted model; the 'many origins' hypothesis may only be examined for residual components whose misalignment exceeds the accepted model's own shoulder residual by a margin measured on the slab, and the phantom suite must include constant-aspect spirals (s from 1.0 down to 0.4) and stadium cores with the required outcome ONE origin.

refuted_claims.claim: Gate G3 (m7 > 0.5 sheet volume eroded by one level-3 voxel is not 3-D connected to the primary support) separates torn bundles from a flattened-but-continuous spiral, so the continuous spiral 'fails G3 and stays one bundle'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: At level 3 a papyrus sheet is 1.5-3 voxels thick (100-200 um / 69 um). A 3x3x3 erosion removes one voxel from each face, i.e. two voxels of thickness, so every sheet thinner than ~3 voxels vanishes and every component becomes 'not connected' to the primary support regardless of tears. Conversely a fused stack (m7 > 0.5 is a solid blob) survives erosion and stays connected even across a real shear interface, because there is no resolvable gap. G3 therefore decides on partial volume, not on physics: it passes vacuously for thin continuous sheets (false splits) and fails for exactly the fused-core shears it was meant to admit. It is the one gate standing between the shoulder components of claim 1 and acceptance.
refuted_claims.fix: Drop erosion-connectivity as a tear test. Replace with a crossing-field test: along rays/hyperbolae crossing the candidate boundary, a tear or fault shows as a discontinuity of the sheet-crossing labelling (a phase residue when integrated around a small loop straddling the boundary), computed on the un-eroded m7 ridge/CT layering; continuity of the labelling across the boundary means one bundle. Test on a phantom at 1.5-voxel sheet thickness with antialiased rendering.

refuted_claims.claim: Translational shear is handled: residual-driven components give sheared sections their own frame so they unroll independently.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The residual is normal misalignment. A block of windings displaced by a fault without rotation keeps its normals parallel to the host; at R = 10 mm a 1 mm offset changes the radial direction by atan(0.1) = 6 degrees, far inside the 30-degree cutoff, so no residual, no component, no local frame, while the winding correspondence across the fault is off by offset/pitch = 2-3 windings. Interlayer slip (windings sliding over each other, the dominant shear in collapsed rolls) likewise leaves normals continuous. Stage 4 then sees a crossing-count jump at the fault azimuth, flags those rays 'non-star-shaped' and excludes them, or the tangent-following link crosses the fault and the 360-degree closure fails and the slice frame is marked invalid. So the method detects only rotational shear; the owner's stated case (sheared sections) is mostly reported as 'frame invalid', never as a bundle with its own frame.
refuted_claims.fix: Add a second bundle-detection channel independent of normals: residues of the crossing-label field (2-D phase-unwrapping residues per slice, tracked in z). A fault that terminates inside the volume has a measurable Burgers-like count (crossings around a closed loop enclosing the fault tip) which gives the inter-bundle offset WITHOUT tracing through the fault; a fault that spans the whole volume keeps its offset UNKNOWN, as the proposal already requires.

refuted_claims.claim: Winding numbers per bundle: 'a consistent labelling around 360 degrees (closure sum zero) gives the winding number w = k'; bar 'winding count equals crossing count +-1 on >= 90 % of monotone rays'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: For a spiral, following one sheet by its tangent through 360 degrees arrives one crossing further out on the starting ray: the closure of a sheet-identity labelling is +1 per turn (or +N for N sheets wound together), never 0. Closure 0 is satisfied only by the crossing-index labelling k, which is trivially closed when counts match and is simply 'count of crossings from the origin': that is the correct winding index only if the innermost sheet is the same physical sheet at every azimuth. In an ash-filled or torn core the innermost surviving winding at azimuth A is winding 5 and at azimuth B winding 9, so k is wrong by several windings and the +-1 bar hides it. Delamination (one winding splitting into recto and verso plies, each ~50-100 um, sub-voxel at 69 um, which the m7 net may mark as two surfaces) adds +1 crossings over a sector; the +-1 tolerance again accepts an off-by-one label.
refuted_claims.fix: Define the winding number as the unwrapped azimuth/2pi along a tangent-tracked sheet from one reference crossing; the closure test is closure == +1 (one sheet) and the measured closure integer is itself reported (closure 2 means two sheets wound together, closure 0 means a closed tube, i.e. not a roll). Detect ply pairs (two crossings closer than half the local measured pitch with no intervening gap) and count them as one winding. Where the core is ash or fused, report the index only outward of the last continuous winding, and state that inner indices are undetermined at this level.

refuted_claims.claim: Decoy rejection: evaluate the alignment energy on the 'FOV-but-outside-mask region' to locate the scanner rotation axis; bar 'outside-mask peak ratio <= 0.1'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The volume is 20251110183117-8.640um-1.2m-116keV-masked.zarr: voxels outside the mask are zero (the existing run records whole slabs as status 'no mask', mask_area_vox 0). There is no outside-mask signal to evaluate; the ring-axis detector and its bar cannot be computed as written. Ring artefacts inside the mask survive untouched. The existing slab z=32 record shows the fitted centre 0.53 mm from the image centre while the mask centroid is 8.6 mm away: either the tip is genuinely on the rotation axis or the decoy is live; the proposal's test could not tell.
refuted_claims.fix: Use the method already in tools/umb/st_axis.py: per-slice polar high-pass about the reconstruction (image) centre before the structure tensor, plus the DECL-UMB-1 M7 bar (axis must not sit within 0.3 mm of the image centre over > 10 mm of z while the mask centroid is > 2 mm away; normal-angle field not z-stationary). Report the fraction of energy removed by the high-pass per slab.

refuted_claims.claim: 'No learned component ... anywhere in U3' while sheet voxels, voter weights, the G3 tear test and the Stage-4 crossings are all taken from the m7 surface-probability volume.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: m7 (…surface-m7-L0-th0.2.zarr) is the organizers' neural surface prediction, trained on labels from other scrolls, produced at level 0 and (by its name) thresholded at 0.2 before storage; it cannot be audited line by line and it carries exactly the mode-5 and mode-2 risks the owner excluded: it was trained to find sheets separated by gaps and is least reliable in the fused crushed core and around debris, where the owner wants the mini-umbilici. Four load-bearing roles on one unaudited learned product is a back door. Also, after averaging to level 3 a 100 um sheet in a 69 um voxel peaks at a probability of ~0.5-0.7, so 'm7 > 0.5' preferentially keeps thick/fused stacks and drops thin clean sheets, the opposite of the intended voter set, and whether the pyramid levels were built by averaging or nearest-neighbour is unverified.
refuted_claims.fix: Primary voters from the CT layering itself (structure tensor on the polar-high-passed CT, with data-derived coherence/contrast thresholds from a phase-randomised null, as DECL-UMB-1 does); m7 only as a cross-check comparator, with its level-3 histogram inspected before any threshold is fixed. State this as the resolution of the contradiction with the 'no learned component' sentence.

refuted_claims.claim: The alignment bars (median >= 0.90, residual <= 5 % clean; >= 0.80, <= 15 % crushed core) validate the origin and the crushed-core model.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: They are computed only over admitted voters (m7 > 0.5 AND coherence > 0.3). With integration sigma 3.5 voxels (0.24 mm, ±2 sigma = 1 mm) the fused core, where the collapsed 'pitch' is ~0.15 mm and buckles have 0.3 mm radius, has coherence below 0.3 and is excluded, so the bars are measured on a self-selected inlier set and pass by construction where the method knows nothing. The real run already shows admissible voter fractions of 0.10-0.31 of the mask area and one slab rejected for 'too few admissible voters' — none of which the proposed bars would surface.
refuted_claims.fix: Add a coverage bar per slab and per radial band: fraction of mask area that votes, fraction of 72 rays with >= 1 crossing in each 5 mm radial band; any zone with voter coverage below a declared fraction gets 'no winding numbers delivered here', and the crushed-core alignment bar is reported together with its coverage, never alone.

refuted_claims.claim: The crushed core's winding numbers are a macro quantity: 'Level 0/1/2 full-volume processing is ... unnecessary for a macro quantity'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The origin is a macro quantity; the winding INDEX inside the fused core is not. Where sheets are fused with no air gap, the only remaining periodicity is the sheet-to-sheet density modulation (recto/verso fibre layers and the interface) at the 100-200 um period, which is 1.5-3 voxels at level 3 (unresolvable after the 0.24 mm integration window) and 11-23 voxels at 8.64 um. Level 3 cannot count windings through a fused stack, and that is precisely the First Letters target region.
refuted_claims.fix: Keep the axis at level 3/4, but count windings in the fused core on level-0/1 ROIs along the fitted axis: the core is ~10-20 mm across, so a 1 mm z-slab at 8.64 um is ~116 x 2300 x 2300 = 0.6 GB uint8, feasible per ROI on 15 GB; radial density profiles from the fitted origin, periodicity measured by autocorrelation, counted outward to the first gap-resolved winding where the level-3 index takes over.

refuted_claims.claim: Compute: structure tensor per 32-slice level-3 slab = 74 M voxels, 9 Gaussian filters, ~20-30 s on 4 cores, 2.7 GB peak; 58 slabs in ~25 min; second (oblique re-slab) pass ~1 h.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: (i) Halo: with sigma_d 1.5 and sigma_i 3.5 the slab needs ~15 slices of context each side to avoid edge normals, so 62 slices = 143 M voxels are processed per slab; 3 gradients + 6 tensor components in float32 = 5.2 GB, plus ndimage's per-call output buffers and the float input = ~6.5 GB, plus cached zarr chunk rows (level-3 chunk row is 128 x 1519 x 1519 = 295 MB; CT and m7, two rows each at boundaries = 1.2 GB) = ~7.5 GB peak, not 2.7. (ii) scipy.ndimage Gaussian filters are single-threaded; 9 three-axis filters on 143 M float32 voxels is ~2-3 min per slab, and two slabs in parallel already exceed 15 GB, so the stage is ~2-3 h, not 25 min. (iii) A batched eigendecomposition of 143 M symmetric 3x3 tensors (np.linalg.eigh) needs ~5 GB input + 5 GB eigenvectors unless chunked; the proposal does not say. (iv) The oblique second pass is not another 1 h: a tilted 2.2 mm slab spanning the 105 mm field touches 2.2 + 105 tan(theta) mm of z (at 5 degrees, 11.4 mm = 165 slices per volume), so pass 2 re-reads each chunk row ~3-5 times (25-45 GB of S3 traffic) and adds a trilinear resampling of ~2 x 143 M voxels per slab. (v) /dev/shm is RAM: anything parked there is subtracted from the same 15 GB the arrays use; the '~6 GB RAM' and '11 GB tmpfs' are one budget. (vi) The 50-100 MB/s S3 rate is unverified behind the agent proxy; the existing run's log shows ~15-25 s per 295 MB chunk row including processing of near-empty slabs.
refuted_claims.fix: All of this stays feasible but must be budgeted honestly: ~4-6 CPU-hours for U3 proper, ~7.5 GB peak, chunked eigendecomposition. Better: the energy uses only xy normal components, so compute a 2-D per-slice structure tensor accumulated over the slab (the DECL-UMB-1 design, cv2/ndimage on 2.3 M-pixel slices, ~10x cheaper, 0.5 GB) and handle tilt by the split-half/first-vs-last-half check already recorded (half_first_last_mm) instead of an oblique re-slab; re-slab only the slabs whose first/last-half centres differ by more than the pitch.

refuted_claims.claim: Cross-bundle offsets are measured with 'vc_grow_seg_from_seed with the local bundle axis as its radial reference', 6 seeds per edge, '~5-15 min per seed on 4 CPUs by earlier runs', 1-3 h total.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The grower as invoked in tools/fl4/run.sh takes a surface volume (-v), a seed and a params JSON {mode, step_size, generations, min_area_cm, voxelsize, thread_limit, cache_size, cache_root, use_cuda, tgt_overlap_count, search_effort}; there is no axis or radial-reference input, so the quoted capability is asserted, not verified. Its disk cache is 3 GB (cache_size 3e9 at $W/vc_cache), which cannot exist on the orchestrator's 1 GB free disk; and the run script allows 3 h per seed, while no per-seed wall time is recorded anywhere in this checkout, so '5-15 min' is unsupported. Physically, the grower follows the m7 surface prediction, and a tear/shear boundary is by definition where that prediction is discontinuous, so the trace will return UNKNOWN on nearly every edge: honest, but it means the owner's absolute winding numbers across bundles are essentially never delivered by this mechanism.
refuted_claims.fix: Run any grower work on the sibling containers only (cache on their /work), record per-seed wall time before quoting it, and do not describe a radial-reference option until VC3D's source for this build has been read. Prefer the dislocation-loop count (offset from crossing counts around a loop enclosing a terminating fault tip, computable from ray crossings alone) for every fault that ends inside the volume; keep UNKNOWN for through-going faults.

refuted_claims.claim: Gate G1 accepts a bundle only if 'its median alignment rises from < 0.6 to > 0.85'; secondary origins are accepted 'if E improves by more than the MDL cost of 2 parameters'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The residual set is defined by a(v) < cos 30 deg = 0.866. A sheared fan rotated by 30-53 degrees has median alignment 0.6-0.866 under the primary origin: it is in R but can never satisfy '< 0.6', so G1 admits only bundles rotated by more than 53 degrees and rejects every moderately sheared fan (the common case). Separately, the Tukey energy is not a log-likelihood, so 'the MDL cost of 2 parameters' has no units and no value; the point-vs-slit decision as written is unspecified.
refuted_claims.fix: One consistent threshold (the 30-degree residual cutoff) for membership and for the G1 'before' state; accept extra parameters on a calibrated improvement (relative median-residual reduction and split-half agreement, with the thresholds themselves exercised in the phantom suite).

refuted_claims.claim: The '20 um smoothing' ray-crossing procedure 'as in the existing RULES ray-crossing procedure' is applied to level-3 slices.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: RULES.md 1959 defines that smoothing for intensity peaks at the volume's native resolution; at level 3 (69.12 um) 20 um is 0.29 voxel, a no-op, and the only peaks available are 1.5-3-voxel sheets at 4-9-voxel pitch, where a one-voxel error is a quarter pitch. The existing run's ray_crossings on the slab mean image returned 0 crossings on the tip slabs. The 5-degree tangent-following step is 2.6 mm (38 voxels) at R = 30 mm and 0.44 mm at R = 5 mm, larger than a 0.3 mm buckle radius, so the link lands on a neighbouring sheet in the crushed zone. This is a resolution-gap (mode 3) transplant.
refuted_claims.fix: Set the peak-detection scale and the link step from the pitch measured on the slab (step <= pitch/2 along the sheet, curvature-limited), run crossing detection on the polar-high-passed CT slices (not the slab mean), and record crossing counts per ray per band as a coverage statistic.

refuted_claims.claim: The phantom suite (32 x 1024 x 1024 per phantom) tests false-split rate, bundle recall, offsets and insensitivity, in ~10 min.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: A 32-slice phantom is one slab: G4 (persistence over >= 3 slabs), Stage-3 tracking, identity swaps, break-points and z-propagation of winding labels are never exercised, so 'bundle recall >= 0.9' cannot be measured at all. The suite also lacks the cases that break the hardened method: constant-aspect (affine) spirals and stadium cores at s = 0.4-0.7, a translational fault, a delaminated sector, a mineral-filled crack running along z (passes G2/G3/G4 and gives a false bundle along every such crack), sheets rendered with partial volume at 1.5 voxels. Each phantom must pass through the full pipeline (~2 min each), so 40 runs are ~80 min, not 10.
refuted_claims.fix: Phantoms of >= 192 slices (0.2 GB each, still trivial), with the added cases and the required outcomes stated (ONE origin for continuous squeezed spirals; frame-with-offset for terminating faults; UNKNOWN for through-going faults; no bundle along a debris-filled crack); run time budgeted at ~1.5 h.

refuted_claims.claim: Slit orientation changes are break-points: 'the slit parameter c changes sign of its orientation or jumps > 2 mm' inserts a break.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Wherever the accepted model has c near 0 (all clean regions) the orientation phi is undefined noise, so this rule inserts breaks throughout the clean zone or forces the smoother to run broken everywhere; it also double-counts the point/slit decision as a geometric discontinuity.
refuted_claims.fix: Condition orientation-based breaks on c exceeding its split-half uncertainty by a margin, and accept a break only if the broken fit lowers the leave-one-slab-out cross-validation error (DECL-UMB-1 rule).

refuted_claims.claim: Comparator (b): geometric_centre_curve on 'any organizer tifxyz segment of PHerc0268 that passes audit'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: No organizer tifxyz segments of PHerc0268 appear in this checkout's catalogues (the fl4 queue segments are our own grown patches), and geometric_centre_curve is itself a least-squares intersection of normal lines whose docstring restricts it to roughly circular windings — the evolute defect the audit rejects for the core. As written the comparator is empty, and where it could run it shares the failure mode it is supposed to check.
refuted_claims.fix: Use our own kept patches (logs/fl4, fl7 seeds) as the mesh comparator in the clean zone only, labelled as such, and add the existing DECL-UMB-1 st_axis.py output as the primary independent comparator: two implementations of the same idea must agree within the split-half noise in the clean zone before either is declared.

verdict.surviving_core: What survives both lenses: (1) The axis is a property of how the LAYERING normals wind, estimated per z-slab at level 3 (69 um, pitch 4-9 voxels) from the CT itself after polar high-pass about the image centre and >= 1 mm mask erosion, with voters admitted by data-derived coherence/contrast thresholds (phase-randomised null), and the slab origin found by a Tukey-robust concurrency/alignment fit with multi-start, split-half and first-vs-last-half checks. A 2-D per-slice structure tensor accumulated over the slab is sufficient and ~10x cheaper than the 3-D tensor. (2) A per-slab model set {point, affine squeeze (constant aspect), slit}, chosen by calibrated improvement plus split-half agreement, with the full misalignment distribution reported. (3) Secondary origins are a residual-driven hypothesis gated by compactness and z-persistence, but tears are tested on the crossing-label field (phase residues / loop counts), never by erosion connectivity, and translational faults are detected from crossing discontinuities, not from normals. (4) Origins are tracked across slabs by assignment with a footprint term, smoothed piecewise with explicit, CV-validated breaks, never across a break; the primary track is the only data term U1 may bridge. (5) Winding numbers are defined along tangent-tracked sheets with spiral closure == +1 (the closure integer reported), delivered only in radial bands with measured voter and crossing coverage; cross-bundle offsets are integers measured either by a traced bridge or by a loop count around a terminating fault, otherwise UNKNOWN; absolute numbers only for the connected component of the primary track with all offsets known. (6) m7 and the organizers' lasagna normals are cross-checks only; no learned product is load-bearing. (7) The fused crushed core receives an origin from this stage but NOT a winding index: that is a level-0/1 ROI task (radial density periodicity at 8.64 um along the fitted axis, ~0.6 GB per 1 mm slab), declared as a separate stage. (8) Compute: feasible on one 4-CPU/15 GB container at ~4-6 CPU-hours and ~7.5 GB peak for the 3-D variant, or ~1 h and <1 GB for the 2-D variant; grower work only on sibling containers with disk; phantoms >= 192 slices including constant-aspect, stadium, fault, delamination and debris-crack cases, ~1.5 h.
verdict.missing_validation: (a) Coverage bars: per slab and per 5 mm radial band, the fraction of mask area that votes and the fraction of rays with >= 1 crossing; without them every alignment/residual bar is measured on a self-selected inlier set (the real run shows 10-31 % admissible voters and a slab rejected for too few). (b) A single-origin requirement test on continuous constant-aspect (affine) spirals and stadium cores at s = 0.4-0.7 and on PHerc0268's own crushed slabs: the residual fraction under the accepted model must be reported against the number of secondary origins proposed, and a continuous phantom must yield exactly one origin. (c) A G3 replacement test: show on a 1.5-voxel-thick continuous phantom sheet that the tear test does NOT separate it (the erosion version will). (d) Translational-fault, delamination and debris-filled-crack phantoms with the required outcomes stated, and phantoms >= 192 slices so G4, tracking, identity swaps and break-points are actually exercised. (e) A spiral-closure test (closure integer == +1 per bundle, value reported) replacing 'closure sum zero', plus a ply-pair detector check. (f) A decoy test that runs on masked data: polar-high-pass energy removed per slab, image-centre proximity vs mask-centroid distance over z (DECL-UMB-1 M7), applied to the slab z=32 case where the fitted centre sits 0.53 mm from the image centre. (g) A level-3 m7 histogram check before any 'm7 > 0.5' threshold, and a statement of the pyramid downsampling method. (h) Agreement of this implementation with the already-declared tools/umb/st_axis.py run within split-half noise in the clean zone (two implementations, one declared method). (i) Measured, not quoted, per-seed grower wall time and a demonstration that the grower accepts any radial reference at all before the cross-bundle step is declared. (j) A fused-core winding count validation at level 0/1 (periodicity of radial density profiles vs. the level-3 index at the first gap-resolved winding), since no level-3 bar can validate winding numbers where there are no resolvable gaps.

audit.strategy: Reject R1 as specified (a dense, globally regularised 'fluid' flow field integrated along z, with learned 'deep voxel' features) and keep only the owner's underlying intent: carry sheets across z by data-driven inter-slice correspondence instead of a brute-force neural mesh. The hardened form is a sheet-conditioned, normal-only, per-slice re-anchored z-tracker with explicit break/split/merge events and no cross-gap smoothing, run on streamed level-2 slabs (34.56 um) with a level-3 macro prior and level-1 verification crops, consuming the U-pipeline umbilicus for winding numbers. It is a component that hands off to the normal-grid patch grower (R3) wherever sheets leave the z-tracking regime (folds whose normal has |n_z| > 0.7, ash, no coherent ridge); it does not replace the grower. Everything is classical, auditable numpy/scipy; no learned flow net until a self-supervised one trained on PHerc0268 itself beats the classical tracker on the metrics below.
audit.summary_of_method_as_specified: R1 treats the CT volume as a video whose frames are x-y slices (or thick z-slabs, 'deep voxels') and the papyrus sheet cross-sections as a continuum advected by a dense displacement field u(x,y,z): a 2-D/3-D optical-flow estimate between slice z and z+1 (brightness constancy plus a smoothness or fluid-like regulariser, possibly learned by a deep network on 3-D patches), integrated along z so that a contour segmented at one slice is propagated through the whole 14833-slice (level 0) or 3709-slice (level 2) stack to form a surface. 'Sheet warp as a fluid state' means a single smooth velocity field over the whole cross-section replaces explicit mesh fitting/growing; the surface is the streamline of each contour point. On PHerc0268 that would mean a dense 2-3 component field over 2.2e12 voxels at level 0 (or 3.4e10 at level 2) and a global energy spanning air gaps, cracks, fragments and the crushed core.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Optical flow is a global smooth field: brightness constancy plus a smoothness/fluid regulariser whose kernel (5-15 px in any practical solver; at level 2 that is 0.17-0.5 mm, i.e. half to one winding pitch) averages displacement across air gaps, shear planes and fragment boundaries. Topology changes in the slice (a sheet folding over so its contour closes to a point and vanishes, delamination creating two ridges from one, two sheets coming into contact) cannot be represented by advection at all. Tangential motion along a smooth ribbon is unobservable (aperture problem), so the regulariser invents it. Integrating the field along z without re-anchoring to the image accumulates bias: 0.05 vox/slice of systematic bias over 3709 level-2 slices is 185 vox = 6.4 mm, i.e. 10-20 windings of drift, which is exactly the drift/twist the owner's umbilicus directive is meant to prevent.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: In the crushed core of PHerc0268 (inner third of the radius, where even the level-4 mask-centroid axis of tools/fl4/fl4.py is unvalidated) a bundle of ~10 windings is compacted with no air gaps and sheared along a plane inclined to z. A smoothness window of 15 vox at level 2 (0.5 mm) straddles the shear plane; the estimated displacement is the mean of the two sides, so a contour tracked across it lands in the neighbouring sheet and carries a wrong winding number for every remaining slice (up to 3709); no local signal reveals the hop. Where an outer sheet buckles into a fold whose crease axis lies in x-y, the slice contour shrinks to a point over ~20 slices and the flow must destroy or create matter, which the fluid model cannot; the tracker either stalls or jumps to the nearest ridge. Over the clean outer windings the pure z-integration drifts by mm-scale amounts long before reaching the core.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: 'Fluid' is the wrong constitutive model. A fluid has no shape memory, permits arbitrary in-plane stretch and shear, and (if incompressibility/divergence penalties are used) resists convergence of neighbouring layers. Papyrus is a thin, nearly inextensible-in-plane shell that bends freely, creases sharply, delaminates and breaks; sheet spacing is NOT conserved along z in a collapse (0.4 mm pitch at the clean top compresses to sheet-thickness contact in the core). A learned 'deep voxel' flow model inherits the mechanics of its training set: natural-video flow datasets (rigid objects with occlusion), parchment (one thick continuous sheet with no air gaps, forbidden by the toxic-data rule) or lab-made carbonised replicas (fresh papyrus rolled and charred, not 2000 years of compaction and the 79 AD pyroclastic loading).
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Between z ~ 1000 and 2500 at level 2 the inner windings of PHerc0268 converge from 9-17 vox spacing to ~3-5 vox (sheet thickness).
