A smooth or divergence-penalised flow prior resists that convergence and spreads tracked contours into the gaps or onto neighbours. A weakly regularised flow lets contours slide tangentially by 10-20% of arc-length per 100 slices (physically impossible for the fibre direction), which appears in the unrolled strip as band-to-band stretching of the fibre texture and ink. Any flow network fine-tuned on En-Gedi would carry a 'no air gap, uniform spacing' prior that is exactly wrong for the crushed core; this is already prohibited by the owner's toxic-data rule.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Flow solvers are coarse-to-fine pyramids. At the coarse OME levels (3-5, 69-276 um) the sheet thickness (100-200 um) and air gap are sub-voxel, so the coarse estimate is the motion of the macro envelope; it is then propagated to fine levels whose search/refinement range is +-1-2 vox. If the coarse estimate places a sheet one pitch off (4-9 vox at level 3, 9-17 at level 2) the fine level cannot correct it: systematic off-by-one-winding errors. At level 0 (8.64 um) brightness constancy is violated at the voxel scale by scanner noise and by the fibre texture itself (recto fibres run along the contour and give no normal-direction signal; verso fibres along z appear as stationary dots), so the data term is noise-dominated unless pre-smoothed with sigma >= 2-3 vox, which is already level 2. A learned model trained at one um/voxel and applied at another sees different patch statistics (sheet = 1 vox at level 3 vs 12-23 vox at level 0).
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Where the core bundle of PHerc0268 shifts by several pitches over ~100 slices (visible at level 3 as envelope motion), a pyramidal flow initialised at level 4 (138 um, 0.54 GB volume) locks the fine-level estimate onto whichever sheet lies nearest the envelope-predicted position; every tracked contour in that region silently acquires a +-1 winding offset. At level 0 the full volume is 2.2e12 voxels, so no dense flow is computable at the deployment resolution anyway; the method would necessarily be run at a scale where layering is at the Nyquist limit (level 3: sheet 1.5-3 vox, gap ~1 vox).

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Optical flow is driven by the strongest image gradients. Bright mineral inclusions (5-10x the sheet contrast), hairs, dust, cracks, ring artefacts (concentric, constant in z, i.e. zero-flow anchors) and the hard edge of the '-masked' volume boundary dominate the data term; the regulariser then propagates their displacement (or their zero displacement) into the surrounding sheets within a kernel width. A tilted inclusion moving 1-2 vox/slice in x-y drags neighbouring contours across their air gaps; a crack opening along z behaves as a 'source' and pulls sheets apart; the mask boundary pins the outer windings. In a periodic stack the matching cost has minima every pitch, so any disturbance larger than half a pitch resolves to an arbitrary neighbour (layer hop).
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: PHerc0268's 116 keV masked volume has ring artefacts about the rotation axis and, in the crushed core, embedded grains of several hundred um. A 300 um grain (9 vox at level 2) lodged between two windings and inclined 30 degrees to z moves ~0.6 vox/slice; its gradient dominates a 15-vox window, so the two adjacent contours are dragged ~0.5 mm over 100 slices, i.e. one full pitch: both hop a winding in opposite senses and the error is invisible locally. At the mask boundary the outermost sheet's contour lags the true sheet by the regularised amount and the outer winding number is wrong from the start.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: If the 'deep voxel' features are learned on the few scrolls with organizer segmentations plus synthetic replicas, the network learns that windings drift coherently with the macro collapse envelope of those volumes, and inherits the layer-hop errors of the organizer meshes used as targets. In ambiguous regions it then predicts the memorised envelope-coherent motion rather than following local evidence: hallucinated continuity across sheared fragments. The 'ESRF/Diamond unreleased raw volumes' and MAE pretraining are unavailable/unverifiable and add unaudited community code paths.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A flow net trained on PHerc0332/1667/Scroll-1-style collapse (ovalised but continuous windings) applied to PHerc0268's crushed core, where fragments move independently, outputs the training scrolls' smooth coherent displacement in exactly the regions where the data term is weakest (ash, contact bundles); the resulting surface is a plausible-looking fabrication, and because the net has no 'no data' output it never flags the region. If the training targets were organizer meshes, their own hops are reproduced as confident predictions.

audit.hardened_alternative:
Sheet-conditioned normal z-tracker (SNZ), classical and auditable, keeping the owner's goal of carrying sheets across z by inter-slice correspondence without a neural mesh.

Scales and data. Working scale = level 2 (34.56 um; sheet 3-6 vox, pitch 9-17 vox; 3709 x 3037 x 3037 uint8), streamed from the OME-zarr in z-slabs of 64 slices (590 MB) into /dev/shm; never materialised whole (34 GB). Level 3 (69 um, 4.3 GB, fits in /dev/shm) is used ONLY for a macro prior and a 3-D structure tensor, never to track sheets (layering is at Nyquist there). Level 1 (17.28 um) is read only as bounded 128^3 verification crops (2 MB each) at flagged events. Level 0 is never processed densely. Input from the U-pipeline: the umbilicus curve per z (U1) and, in the core, U3 local centres; the m7 surface-probability volume is used as a second, audited data term for re-anchoring, never alone.

Step 0, macro prior (level 3): per slice pair, ZNCC block matching with 32x32 blocks (2.2 mm), stride 16, search +-4 vox; keep blocks with peak >= 0.7 and peak-ratio (best/second) >= 1.2; 3x3-block median filter; cap |p| <= 3 vox. This is the bundle's envelope motion and is used only to centre the per-point search window. Also a 3-D structure tensor (sigma_d 1 vox, sigma_i 2 vox) giving |n_z|; regions with |n_z| > 0.7 (sheet turning perpendicular to z) are marked 'not z-trackable' and handed to the normal-grid patch grower (R3).

Step 1, sheet field (level 2, per slice): 2-D structure tensor with Gaussian derivative sigma_d = 1.0 vox (35 um) and integration sigma_i = 2.5 vox (86 um), i.e. the integration window is smaller than half the smallest pitch (4.5 vox), so it never spans two sheets; outputs in-slice normal n and coherence c in [0,1]. Ridge detection along n (Hessian eigenvalue at sigma 1.5 vox) gives sheet centrelines as polylines sampled every 2 vox (70 um). Local pitch at each point = spacing of adjacent ridges along n (expected 9-17 vox).

Step 2, seeding: in the clean top and bottom z-bands (chosen as the slices whose coherent-ridge fraction c > 0.6 covers >= 80% of the mask), every ridge polyline becomes a segment with an id; winding number w = ridge-crossing count along the ray from the umbilicus to the point (independent per slice, stored with the point).

Step 3, per-slice step z -> z+1, normal component only (the aperture problem is embraced: tangential position is re-parametrised by arc-length each slice and is set by azimuth about the umbilicus at unrolling time, as unroll_ring.py already does): prediction = position + macro prior p; sample the level-2 intensity (and the m7 probability) along n at +-6 vox (0.2 mm) around the prediction in slice z+1 and ZNCC-match the +-4 vox profile from slice z; displacement d = argmax with parabolic sub-voxel refinement. Accept only if ZNCC peak >= 0.6, peak ratio >= 1.3 and |d| <= 0.4 x local pitch (search window < half pitch, so the periodic-stack aliasing that causes layer hops is structurally excluded rather than regularised away). Along each segment the accepted d are smoothed with a robust 1-D second-difference penalty (Huber loss, delta = 1 vox, 5-point window): creases stay sharp, outliers from grains/hairs are down-weighted (points > 3 MAD from the segment median are rejected). Rejected points are interpolated only if both neighbours within 3 points are accepted; otherwise they are 'lost'. Then re-anchor: snap each point to the ridge maximum in slice z+1 within +-1.5 vox along n. Re-anchoring every slice makes the method a ridge tracker with a flow predictor, so integration bias cannot accumulate (drift is bounded by the per-slice snap, not by the sum of flow errors). No smoothing is ever applied across z beyond one step and none across different segments.

Step 4, events instead of regularisation: a segment is cut where >= 3 consecutive points are lost or where c < 0.5 (ash/amorphous: declare 'no data', do not interpolate). Split (delamination) is declared when two ridges appear within the former profile over >= 3 consecutive slices; children inherit w with an 'uncertain' flag. Contact/merge is declared when two segments stay within 1 vox for >= 3 slices; both ids are kept and flagged (never fused). A thickness change > 50% in one step or a |d| > 0.4 pitch is a break, not a move. Lost segments are re-seeded with new ids at the next slice; two ids are linked across a gap only when a level-1 128^3 crop shows a continuous 3-D ridge path with coherence > 0.6 along the whole path; otherwise they stay separate. Nothing is bridged by interpolation.

Step 5, bidirectional: run top-down and bottom-up as independent passes; in overlaps they must agree (metric below); disagreements are flagged, never averaged.

Step 6, output: per-slice polylines with id, w, confidence, event flags, assembled per segment into tifxyz-style grids (u = arc-length about the umbilicus from the azimuth cut, v = z) so vc_render_tifxyz, unroll_ring.py and the ink models consume them unchanged. In the crushed core, w and azimuth are computed against the U3 local centre of the point's fragment bundle, so sheared bundles unroll independently.

Dependencies and parallelism: 7 siblings each take a z-band of ~530 level-2 slices with 32-slice overlap, both directions; the orchestrator merges on the overlap-agreement metric. No GPU, no training, no community code; scipy.ndimage, numpy and zarr/fsspec reads only.

validation_metrics.name: forward_backward_consistency
validation_metrics.definition: Track every contour point z -> z+16 -> z (forward pass then reverse pass on the same slab) and measure the Euclidean return error in level-2 voxels.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: median <= 0.5 vox (17 um) and p95 <= 1.5 vox (52 um) within the clean z-bands; points above 1.5 vox are flagged; any slab with p95 > 3 vox fails.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Self-consistency only: run the same tracker in both z directions on the same 64-slice slab held in /dev/shm; no reference surface needed.

validation_metrics.name: winding_number_conservation
validation_metrics.definition: For every tracked point, the ridge-crossing count from the umbilicus (U1 curve, or U3 local centre in the core) is re-measured independently in each slice; an unflagged change of that count along a track is a layer hop.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: 0 unflagged changes per segment in the clean bands; in the core, unflagged changes <= 1e-4 per segment-step and 100% of remaining changes carry a split/merge/break flag. Any unflagged change in a clean band fails that band.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Two independent measurements of the same quantity: the tracker's identity propagation vs a per-slice radial ridge count from the umbilicus; agreement is evidence, disagreement is a detected hop.

validation_metrics.name: reanchor_residual_and_coverage
validation_metrics.definition: Residual between the flow-predicted position and the re-anchored ridge position along n; plus coverage = fraction of ridge length per slice whose match is unambiguous (ZNCC >= 0.6, peak ratio >= 1.3).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: median residual <= 0.5 vox, p95 <= 1.2 vox; coverage >= 0.90 in the clean bands (if the predictor is worse than this it adds nothing over plain ridge tracking); in the core, coverage is reported per z with no threshold and no claim beyond it.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Both quantities are internal to the tracker and are logged per point per slice; aggregated per z-band.

validation_metrics.name: two_direction_agreement
validation_metrics.definition: In the 32-slice overlaps between sibling z-bands and over every slab, compare the top-down and bottom-up tracks: positional distance and winding number of linked segments.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: position median <= 0.5 vox, p95 <= 1.5 vox; winding numbers agree for 100% of segments linked without a flag; any winding disagreement is reported, never averaged.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Two independent passes of the same method with different initial conditions (top seeds vs bottom seeds); the overlaps give a direct consistency check.

validation_metrics.name: independent_method_agreement
validation_metrics.definition: Distance from tracked contours to (a) the audited m7 surface-probability ridge and (b) our normal-grid patch grower tifxyz surfaces where they overlap, and agreement of the winding band index.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: median distance <= 1 vox at level 2 (35 um) and p90 <= 2 vox for (a) and (b); winding band identical for 100% of points where both methods are confident; disagreements are listed with coordinates for human inspection.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: The grower uses normals and local growth, m7 is an organizer product, the tracker uses z-correspondence: three methods with different failure modes; agreement between them is the strongest evidence available without a ground-truth surface.

validation_metrics.name: radial_normal_agreement (existing sheetcheck gate)
validation_metrics.definition: |cos(n, radial from umbilicus)| of the assembled surface normals and the radius spread per cm of surface, exactly as tools/fl4/sheetcheck.py computes them.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: median |cos| >= 0.8, fraction > 0.8 >= 0.7, spread < 2.0 mm/cm; applied only outside the crushed core against the U1 axis, and inside it against the U3 local centre of the fragment bundle.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Geometric consistency with the umbilicus; a surface that cuts across windings has low |cos| and a wide radius spread.

validation_metrics.name: self_phantom_recovery
validation_metrics.definition: Take a real clean-winding level-2 slab of PHerc0268, apply a known warp (smooth bending + one shear plane inclined to z + one 2-vox crack opening along z + three bright 9-vox grains moving 0.6 vox/slice), resample it, and run the tracker; the warp is ground truth by construction and the texture is real papyrus (no parchment, no replica mechanics).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: endpoint error median <= 0.5 vox, p95 <= 1.0 vox away from the inserted features; the shear plane is detected as a break within 2 slices and no track crosses it unflagged; the displacement of tracks within 10 vox of a grain differs by <= 0.5 vox from the unperturbed run; the crack produces no unflagged split.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: The ground truth is the synthetic warp applied to real data, so the comparison is exact and the test is reproducible; it must be reported as a phantom test, never as a result on the scroll.

validation_metrics.name: drift_bound
validation_metrics.definition: For closed tracks in the clean bands, compare the z-integrated tracked displacement over 500 slices with a direct (drift-free) level-3 ZNCC block match between slice z and z+500, resampled to level 2.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: |difference| <= 2 vox at level 2 (70 um) for 95% of blocks, i.e. far below the 9-17 vox pitch; any block above 4 vox is flagged.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: A long-baseline direct match cannot accumulate per-slice bias, so it bounds the integrated drift of the tracker without a reference surface.

validation_metrics.name: strip_seam_consistency
validation_metrics.definition: In the unrolled strip (unroll_ring.py output), ZNCC of the CT texture or ink_9um map across z-band seams and across segment-link boundaries in 64x64 px windows, as in the existing vgrid seam check.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: median seam ZNCC >= 0.5 and no seam window with a lateral offset > 2 px at the peak; seams failing are listed with coordinates.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Texture continuity across independently tracked bands is a property of a correct unrolling and needs no reference.

audit.compute_estimate: Hardened SNZ tracker: level-2 contour set ~1.3e5 points per slice (assuming a mask radius of ~30-40 mm and 0.4 mm pitch, ~9-10 m of sheet per slice sampled every 70 um; the real count comes from the fl4 outer_radius_vox values). Per slice: structure tensor + ridge over 9.2 Mpx ~0.5-1 s on one core (scipy), 1-D ZNCC matching ~0.3 s vectorised, bookkeeping ~0.5 s: 1-2 s/slice ideal, 3-5 s realistic -> 3709 slices = 3-5 CPU-h per direction, 6-10 CPU-h for both; across 7 siblings in z-bands of ~530 slices with 32-slice overlap: ~1.5-3 wall-hours per direction on 4 cores each. RAM per container: one 64-slice slab 0.6 GB + float32 working slices (37 MB each) + state (<0.1 GB) < 2 GB. Level-3 macro prior: 4.3 GB volume in /dev/shm (11 GB free), block matching < 1 CPU-h. Level-1 verification crops: <= 2000 x 128^3 (2 MB each) = 4 GB of network reads, ~1 CPU-h. Outputs: int16 polylines with ids/flags ~100-150 MB compressed per z-band, ~1 GB total: the 1 GB free local disk is the binding constraint, so each band is written to /dev/shm and uploaded/pushed before the next; level-2 reads total ~34 GB from S3 per direction. Phantom test: one 64-slice slab, minutes. By contrast R1 as specified: dense flow at level 0 is 2.2e12 voxels (2.2 TB of reads) and >= 4e17 FLOP for any 3-D CNN, ~90 days per 4-core container (~13 days across all 8); even a dense classical flow at level 2 needs ~137 GB of float16 field storage (60x the free disk) and ~34 GB of input it cannot hold; neither is feasible here.
audit.what_to_reject_outright: (1) Any dense, whole-volume 3-D optical flow at levels 0-2: 2.2e12 voxels at level 0, 137 GB of field at level 2, >= 90 CPU-days for a learned net; not computable on 4 CPUs/15 GB/1 GB disk and not needed. (2) The 'fluid state' formulation itself: a single global smoothness, divergence or incompressibility prior spanning air gaps, cracks, shear planes and floating fragments is the geometric straightjacket of mode 1 and the wrong constitutive model of mode 2; papyrus is an inextensible, freely bending, fracturing shell whose layer spacing is not conserved along z. (3) Pure z-integration of flow without per-slice re-anchoring to the ridge: 0.05 vox/slice bias becomes 6.4 mm (10-20 windings) over the stack. (4) Coarse-to-fine pyramids seeded at OME levels 3-5 where sheets are sub-voxel: off-by-one-winding locks that the fine level cannot undo. (5) Any learned 'deep voxel' flow network pretrained on natural video, on En-Gedi/parchment/vellum (toxic-data rule), on lab replicas, or supervised by organizer meshes of other scrolls (memorises their collapse shapes and their hop errors); 3-D MAE pretraining on 'unreleased ESRF/Diamond raw volumes' is unverifiable and is rejected as a data plan. (6) Brightness constancy as the sole data term in a ring-artefacted, masked, grain-contaminated 116 keV volume. (7) R1 as a replacement for patch growing: z-tracking is undefined where sheets fold perpendicular to z (|n_z| > 0.7) and where coherence vanishes (ash); those regions must be declared 'no data' and left to R3/U3, never interpolated. (8) Any variant that outputs a surface without the flags and per-point confidences above, since an unflagged region in the crushed core is indistinguishable from a fabrication. (9) Unaudited community flow code (RAFT/DIS/Farneback wrappers included) until read line by line; the hardened tracker needs only numpy/scipy.

refuted_claims.claim: Step 1: 'integration sigma_i = 2.5 vox is smaller than half the smallest pitch (4.5 vox), so it never spans two sheets'; sheet pitch assumed 9-17 vox (0.3-0.6 mm) at level 2.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: A Gaussian with sigma 2.5 vox has FWHM 5.9 vox and 95 % support of 10 vox, i.e. wider than the smallest assumed pitch of 9 vox, so the isotropic tensor already averages two sheets at the proposal's own numbers. The pitch range itself is unsupported for PHerc0268: the project's own measurement on the Paris-4 scroll (logs/sib/orders/p4-core.txt) is ~0.22 mm outside the core (6.4 vox at level 2) and 0.07-0.15 mm inside (2-4 vox), and in any contact bundle pitch = sheet thickness = 3-6 vox. There the Hessian ridge at sigma 1.5 (ridge width >= 3 vox) cannot separate neighbouring sheets; the 'sheet field' is undefined precisely where the First Letters target (crushed core) lives.
refuted_claims.fix: Before fixing any sigma, measure the pitch/thickness/gap histogram of PHerc0268 at level 2 from radial profiles about the current axis (20 slices, minutes of CPU). Use an oriented anisotropic tensor (sigma across the normal <= 0.8 vox, along the tangent 3-4 vox). Where local pitch < 7 vox switch to level-1 crops (17 um; sheet 6-12 vox) or declare no-data; never claim a level-2 sheet field in contact bundles.

refuted_claims.claim: Step 3: 'search window < half pitch, so periodic-stack aliasing that causes layer hops is structurally excluded'; accept |d| <= 0.4 x local pitch within a +-6 vox window.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: A 9-sample (+-4) template inside a 13-sample (+-6) window yields only five lags, -2..+2 vox, so the measurable displacement is 2 vox/slice (sheet tilt <= 63 deg) regardless of the 0.4-pitch rule; the rule is never the binding limit and the numbers were not worked through. The re-anchor snap of +-1.5 vox equals half the pitch in a contact bundle (3 vox), so aliasing is not excluded there. And 'structural exclusion' only holds when the true displacement is small: an integer-pitch slip gives zero measured displacement with ZNCC ~ 1 (next item).
refuted_claims.fix: State the measurable range as |d| <= 2 vox/slice and tie the R3 handoff to it (|n_z| threshold derived from tan(tilt) = 2). Snap radius = min(1.5 vox, 0.3 x local pitch). Add the shear detector and tangential anchors below; do not describe aliasing as excluded.

refuted_claims.claim: Mode-1 handling: 'a |d| > 0.4 pitch is a break, not a move'; the hardened tracker handles shear planes in the crushed core.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: In a compacted bundle the most likely slip across a shear plane inclined to z is one sheet thickness = one pitch. As the shear line sweeps across a tracked point, the ridge at that (x,y) in slice z+1 belongs to the neighbouring winding but has |d| ~ 0, ZNCC ~ 1 and the same thickness: every point crossing the line is transferred to the wrong winding without any flag. A normal-only tracker that discards tangential texture cannot see this by construction, and the transfer is symmetric, so forward-backward and two-direction consistency both pass.
refuted_claims.fix: Detect the shear line per slice as a 2-D feature (ridge-phase discontinuity across a line plus coherence drop), track it in z, and cut every segment the line sweeps across (break event, no inheritance of w). Add sparse tangential anchors: 9x9 2-D ZNCC texture patches every ~2 mm along each segment, matched every 8 slices; anchor failure or inconsistent slip flags the segment. Include an integer-pitch shear in the phantom.

refuted_claims.claim: Ring artefacts are listed as a failure of R1 only; the SNZ metrics (forward-backward, winding conservation, drift bound, two-direction) are evidence of correct sheets.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Ring artefacts in the 116 keV masked volume are perfectly coherent concentric ridges, z-stationary. The Hessian ridge detector will find them, the tracker will follow them with d = 0 and ZNCC = 1, and every internal metric passes maximally on the decoy: forward-backward 0, two-direction 0, drift 0, winding count constant. The proposal omits the per-slice polar high-pass that tools/umb/st_axis.py already applies, although DECL-UMB-1 names the rotation-centre decoy explicitly.
refuted_claims.fix: Polar high-pass about the reconstruction centre on every slice before ridge detection (reuse st_axis.polar_highpass). Z-stationarity decoy flag: any segment with |d| < 0.05 vox and unchanged profile over > 100 slices is flagged unless the m7 probability and the grower agree it is papyrus. Inject synthetic rings into the phantom and require them to be rejected.

refuted_claims.claim: Mode-4 handling: grains/hairs are handled by Huber smoothing and rejection of points > 3 MAD from the segment median; 'rejected points are interpolated only if both neighbours within 3 points are accepted'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Bright debris in PHerc0268 is dense, not sparse: the project's own level-3 diagnostic (logs/umb/PHerc0268/slabs.json, 'debris_frac' = per-slab p99.5 dilated by 3 vox) flags 24-45 % of the mask area in 10 of the 12 processed slabs. A ZNCC profile whose variance is dominated by a grain locks to the grain (a 3-D object with its own tilt). With a quarter to a half of points contaminated, the MAD rule plus the 3-point interpolation limit cuts segments at a rate that fragments the sheet field into short, unlinked pieces, and the 2000-crop level-1 re-linking budget cannot repair that.
refuted_claims.fix: Measure debris density at level 2 first. Clip at the per-slab p99 and inpaint along the tangent before profile extraction; use a rank (Spearman) or sign correlation instead of raw ZNCC; use the m7 profile as the primary term in debris-flagged zones. Report the segment-length distribution and the fragmentation rate on a 128-slice pilot as a gate before any full run.

refuted_claims.claim: Step 2: seeds come from 'clean top and bottom z-bands' defined as slices where the coherent-ridge fraction c > 0.6 covers >= 80 % of the mask.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: No evidence that such a band exists. The current st_axis run on the top 15 mm of PHerc0268 (14 slabs, z 0-224 at level 3) shows admissible-voter fractions of 10-31 % of the mask and axis confidence 0.0 with median residuals 4-11 mm in 10 of 12 processed slabs: by the project's own measure the top of this scroll is not clean. A seeding rule that selects no band yields no tracker; a threshold set to make a band appear is circular.
refuted_claims.fix: Seed per 2-D tile (256^2 at level 2) wherever the tile's coherent-ridge fraction > 0.6, at many z, not only at the ends. Run a level-2 coherence survey first (every 16th slice, ~0.5 CPU-h) and define 'clean' from its empirical distribution.

refuted_claims.claim: Winding number w = ridge-crossing count along the ray from the umbilicus, stored with the point at seeding; pass = 0 unflagged changes per segment in clean bands.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: (a) A ray from the axis crosses a buckled or folded sheet more than once and crosses floating fragments, so the count is not the winding number and changes along z without any hop. (b) With ~5e8 point-steps, any ray-count noise above 2e-9 per step produces false failures: '0 unflagged changes' is unachievable and would fail every band. (c) The axis the count depends on is not validated (confidence 0.0 in most processed slabs today) and the existing level-3 ray counter returns 1 crossing per ray on the slab means, i.e. it is blind at that scale. Storing w at seeding also freezes it to an axis that will change.
refuted_claims.fix: Make w a derived attribute computed at assembly time from whichever axis is current (segment ids are axis-independent). Use the ray count only as a change detector between consecutive slices along the same ray, with a false-change rate calibrated on the phantom, and report the rate, never a zero requirement.

refuted_claims.claim: drift_bound: compare the integrated track over 500 slices with a direct level-3 ZNCC block match between slice z and z+500.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Slices 500 level-2 steps (17 mm) apart in a collapsed scroll share no texture: sheets move several pitches, debris and cracks differ. The only z-invariant content is the ring artefact pattern, so the metric either returns no accepted blocks or measures the decoy.
refuted_claims.fix: Chained level-3 block matches at 16-slice steps with loop-closure residuals, and a >= 512-slice self-phantom (a 512-slice level-2 slab is 4.7 GB in /dev/shm, feasible) as the real drift measurement.

refuted_claims.claim: forward_backward_consistency and two_direction_agreement detect layer hops.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Both are symmetric under the integer-pitch shear transfer and under ring decoys: forward A->B at the shear line is undone by backward B->A at the same line, and top-down and bottom-up passes transfer identically. They detect only asymmetric, stochastic hops.
refuted_claims.fix: Keep them as necessary conditions, drop the hop-detection claim. Hop detection needs the shear-line detector, tangential anchors and the independent grower comparison.

refuted_claims.claim: independent_method_agreement treats m7 as an independent method ('three methods with different failure modes').
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Step 3 also uses the m7 probability as a data term in the matching; agreement with m7 is then partly agreement with itself.
refuted_claims.fix: Use m7 in exactly one role. If it stays a data term, validate only against the normal-grid grower and the tangential anchors, plus an external reference-only run (below).

refuted_claims.claim: radial_normal_agreement gate as in sheetcheck.py: median |cos(n, radial)| >= 0.8, applied against the U1 axis outside the core.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: sheetcheck.py uses one z-constant centre (the seed's umb_x/umb_y), not the U1 curve. For an affinely squeezed winding the true normals deviate from radial by acos(2/sqrt((1+3 sin^2 t)(1+3 cos^2 t))): |cos| = 0.8 exactly at 45 deg azimuth for a 2:1 squeeze and 0.6 for 3:1, so correct surfaces in ovalised (not 'core') sections fail the gate; 'outside the crushed core' is not a radial zone in a crushed scroll.
refuted_claims.fix: Compare against the normal of the affine-squeeze model st_axis already fits (M(v - c)) or against the structure-tensor layering normal field; use the U1 curve with its per-slab confidence, and withhold the gate where confidence < 0.5.

refuted_claims.claim: Compute: 1-2 s/slice ideal, 3-5 s realistic, 3-5 CPU-h per direction.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Per 9.2 Mpx slice: separable Gaussians at sigma 1/1.5/2.5 (8 filter passes), 2x2 eigen-decomposition with numpy temporaries, ridge non-maximum suppression via map_coordinates, skeleton/polyline linking of 1-3e5 ridge pixels, 3.4e6 profile samples, KD-tree pair search and per-segment Huber smoothing come to 4-8 s single-core; and the z->z+1 step is sequential, only the sheet-field precompute parallelises. Expect 12-25 CPU-h for both directions. Still feasible (0.5-1 wall-h per 530-slice band on 4 cores), but the figures were not worked.
refuted_claims.fix: Time the per-slice pipeline on one real level-2 slice before scheduling; pipeline the sheet-field precompute on 3 workers ahead of the single sequential tracker process.

refuted_claims.claim: Level-2 data streamed in 64-slice slabs of 590 MB.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The level-2 zarr has 128^3 chunks and no compressor ('compressor': null, verified from /2/.zarray), so a chunk row is 128 x 3037^2 = 1.18 GB (576 chunks of 2 MB). A 64-slice slab not aligned to 128 forces each chunk row to be read twice: up to 137 GB of S3 traffic for both directions instead of 68 GB; and the total is uncompressed bytes, so S3 throughput, not CPU, may bound the wall time.
refuted_claims.fix: Use 128-slice chunk-aligned slabs (1.18 GB) with the z-halo served from the cached adjacent row (2.4 GB in /dev/shm); measure S3 throughput from a container before scheduling.

refuted_claims.claim: Level-1 verification crops: <= 2000 x 128^3 at 2 MB each = 4 GB of reads, ~1 CPU-h.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: A 128^3 crop centred on an arbitrary event spans up to 8 uncompressed chunks = 16 MB, so 2000 crops are 4-32 GB. The event count is unknown and, given the debris density, the lost-segment rate will be 1e4-1e5 per direction, not 2000; the budget then leaves most gaps unlinked.
refuted_claims.fix: Snap crops to chunk-aligned 128^3 blocks (one 2 MB chunk) and cache; measure the lost-segment rate on a 128-slice pilot before fixing a budget.

refuted_claims.claim: Outputs ~100-150 MB compressed per z-band, ~1 GB total; RAM per container < 2 GB with the 4.3 GB level-3 volume in /dev/shm.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Per-point records (x,y int16, id int32, w int16, conf+flags 2 B = 12 B) x 1.3e5 points x 3709 slices = 5.8 GB raw per direction, 11.6 GB for both; trajectories do not compress 10x. /dev/shm is RAM-backed, so the 11 GB tmpfs and 15 GB RAM are the same memory: 4.3 GB volume + 1.2 GB chunk row + 1.7 GB per-band output + 4 workers at ~0.8 GB = 10.4 GB with no headroom. The whole-scroll output has no durable home: 1 GB local disk, GitHub cannot take it, no write bucket is named; 'uploaded/pushed before the next' is undefined.
refuted_claims.fix: Each sibling holds only its level-3 band plus halo (~0.65 GB), never the whole 4.3 GB. Decimate the deliverable to tifxyz grids at 10-vox cells (~60 MB per direction) plus a sparse event table at full resolution (every cut/split/merge/break with coordinates and confidences); name the durable store before any run.

refuted_claims.claim: Step 0: 3-D structure tensor at level 3 (sigma_d 1, sigma_i 2) gives |n_z|; |n_z| > 0.7 regions are handed to R3.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: If the core pitch is ~0.1 mm as measured on Paris 4, it is 1-2 vox at level 3, below Nyquist: the tensor is noise exactly where the handoff decision is needed. A whole-volume 3-D tensor also needs six float32 components (6 x 17 GB) unless chunked, which the proposal does not say.
refuted_claims.fix: Derive tilt from the tracker's own measured per-slice displacement (tan tilt = |d|) and from a 3-D tensor on the streamed level-2 slab in 16-slice sub-slabs (6 x 0.6 GB); use level 3 only for the mask-envelope prior.

refuted_claims.claim: Step 0 macro prior: level-3 ZNCC block matching (32x32, search +-4, peak >= 0.7, peak-ratio >= 1.2) gives the bundle envelope motion.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: In regular layering the block autocorrelation is periodic with period 4-9 vox at level 3 and a +-4 search spans a full period, so the ratio test rejects exactly the well-layered blocks and keeps blocks dominated by aperiodic content: debris, cracks, the mask edge. The 'macro prior' is then a debris-motion field, median-filtered into the sheet search windows (mode 4 by construction).
refuted_claims.fix: Prior from the eroded-mask envelope (per-slice centroid and second moments) plus the previous step's median displacement of the same segment; limit the search at level 3 to +-2 and never let the prior move a level-2 window centre by more than 1 vox.

refuted_claims.claim: Tangential position 'is set by azimuth about the umbilicus at unrolling time, as unroll_ring.py already does'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: unroll_ring.py maps points to azimuth x R_ref with one z-constant centre and one R_ref: a cylindrical projection, not arc-length. In a squeezed section the local scale error equals the local radius ratio (2-3x). Because the tracker discards all tangential correspondence, a rotational slip of inner windings relative to outer ones during collapse becomes a z-dependent azimuthal shear in the strip that only the seam metric can see, and only at seams.
refuted_claims.fix: Arc-length parametrisation along the tracked polyline at assembly; measure slip with the tangential anchors and report it per segment; the seam metric stays as a check, not as the detector.

refuted_claims.claim: self_phantom_recovery with three synthetic bright 9-vox grains and a 64-slice slab is a faithful mode-4 and drift test.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Synthetic blobs lack the beam-hardening halos and streaks of real inclusions, and 64 slices cannot test drift over hundreds of slices, rings, or an integer-pitch shear.
refuted_claims.fix: Paste real debris crops from the scroll (with halos) into the phantom, use a 512-slice slab, add synthetic ring artefacts and an integer-pitch shear plane; pass bars must include rejection of the rings and detection of the shear.

verdict.surviving_core: A per-slice ridge tracker at OME level 2 (34.56 um) for the RESOLVED outer windings of PHerc0268 only, defined as regions where the measured local pitch is >= ~7 vox (0.24 mm) with visible air gaps, 2-D coherence >= 0.5 and per-slice normal displacement |d| <= 2 vox. Its retained mechanics: polar high-pass per slice (as st_axis.py), an oriented anisotropic structure tensor (narrow across the normal), Hessian ridge centrelines, prediction from the segment's own previous displacement plus a mask-envelope prior, 1-D robust (rank) profile matching along the normal with a +-2 vox measurable range, per-slice re-anchoring to the ridge within min(1.5 vox, 0.3 pitch), robust per-segment smoothing in-slice only, no smoothing across z beyond one step and none across segments, explicit cut/split/merge/break events with no interpolation across gaps, tile-based seeding wherever coherence allows, independent top-down and bottom-up passes whose disagreements are flagged and never averaged, plus two additions it cannot do without: a per-slice shear-line detector that cuts every segment the line sweeps over, and sparse tangential texture anchors to measure slip. Winding numbers are a derived attribute computed at assembly against whichever axis is current and withheld where axis confidence < 0.5. Everything with pitch < 7 vox, coherence < 0.5, |d| > 2 vox/slice or debris-dominated profiles is declared no-data and handed to R3/U3; the method makes no claim about the crushed core. Deliverable: decimated tifxyz grids (10-vox cells) plus a full-resolution sparse event table. Validation that survives: self-phantom on a >= 512-slice real slab with real debris, synthetic rings and an integer-pitch shear; forward-backward and two-direction agreement as necessary conditions only; grower comparison with m7 in a single role; seam ZNCC; the affine-model normal gate instead of the raw radial-cos gate. Compute: ~12-25 CPU-h for both directions over 7 siblings in 128-slice chunk-aligned slabs, 68 GB of uncompressed S3 reads, < 6 GB RAM per container including /dev/shm, feasible on the stated hardware.
verdict.missing_validation: (1) A measured pitch / sheet-thickness / air-gap histogram of PHerc0268 at level 2 (radial profiles about the current axis, 20 slices) replacing the assumed 9-17 vox; the tracker's domain of validity is defined from it, not assumed. (2) A level-2 coherent-ridge coverage survey per 256^2 tile and per z (every 16th slice) to show whether any 'clean' region exists and where. (3) Debris density at level 2 and the resulting point-rejection and segment-fragmentation rates on a 128-slice pilot, reported before any full run. (4) A ring-artefact decoy test: synthetic rings in the phantom must be rejected, and a z-stationarity audit of every real track. (5) An integer-pitch shear phantom: the shear line must be detected and no track may cross it unflagged; the current metrics are blind to it. (6) A tangential slip measurement (texture anchors) with a stated bound, since the strip's u-axis is otherwise unvalidated. (7) A drift test over >= 500 slices on a 512-slice real-slab phantom; the proposed z/z+500 direct match is unmeasurable. (8) The axis dependency: per-band U1 confidence >= 0.5 before any winding number is reported; today most processed slabs have confidence 0.0, so w cannot be claimed anywhere yet. (9) An external reference-only check: run the tracker on a scroll with an audited organizer segmentation (never used for training) and report the absolute hop and distance statistics, because every stated metric is self-consistency or agreement among in-house products. (10) A false-change-rate calibration for the ray-count winding metric on the phantom, replacing the unachievable zero. (11) Measured S3 read throughput from a container (68-137 GB of uncompressed reads) and a named durable store for the outputs before scheduling.

audit.strategy: Audit R2 as a claim chain: (a) is the physical signal it names ('micro density' of ordered fibre vs amorphous ink) actually present in a 116 keV, 8.64 um, 1.2 m propagation-distance uint8 masked reconstruction; (b) can an nnUNet-like 3-D net be trained and run on 4 CPU / 15 GB / 1 GB disk for a 2.19e12-voxel level-0 volume; (c) which parts of the data plan violate the owner's own toxic-data and provenance rules; (d) which of the five failure modes each component triggers on PHerc0268 specifically (crushed core, axis near reconstruction rotation centre, only one resolution). Then keep the single physically true kernel in R2 - the recto/verso fibre-orientation alternation gives a sheet-count signal that does not depend on air gaps and resolves delamination/fusion - and re-implement it with explicit, measured, CPU-cheap operators (structure tensor + 1-D radial state grammar) layered on the organizer m7 surface product, with pre-declared, ground-truth-free metrics. Repo facts used: logs/fl4/axis_PHerc0268.json (m7 L0 th0.2 product name; axis centroid drift of ~20 mm in y over the top ~32 mm), packages/orgseg-ink/README.md (fibre/crush periodicity mimics text at tile scale; growers hop windings at cracks), RULES.md D0-SETTLED item 8 (half-pitch measured per region, never hard-coded).
audit.summary_of_method_as_specified: R2 proposes an nnUNet-style 3-D segmentation network, described as 'physics-informed', that labels voxels of the 8.64 um phase-contrast CT by 'micro density' classes - ordered (fibre-aligned) papyrus vs amorphous ink vs air/ash - and then aligns sheet surfaces to those class boundaries instead of to air gaps, so that fused sheets (no gap) can still be separated and ink is mapped as a density class. The data plan attached to it is: Vesuvius open-data OME-zarr volumes and HF checkpoints for fine-tuning; 3-D MAE pretraining on 'ESRF/Diamond unreleased raw volumes'; 'synthetic carbonised papyrus replicas' as perfect ground truth; legacy EduceLab fragments/scrolls as a cross-beamline control; En-Gedi parchment as 'reference only'. For PHerc0268 it would have to run at level 0 (14833 x 12145 x 12145 = 2.19e12 voxels), since that is the only level at which any sub-sheet texture survives, and it would need training labels that do not exist for this scroll other than the organizers' own m7 surface prediction (a model output, not ground truth).

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: An nnUNet-class 3-D net has no global smoothness term, but its deep encoder (5 downsampling stages, 128^3 patch = 1.1 mm at L0) learns a shape prior from the training scrolls: 'a sheet is a thin, continuous, gently curved slab'. Trained with m7-style labels (one surface per sheet, labelled mostly where the scroll is clean), it heals discontinuities it has never seen: it bridges sheared faults, closes crush gaps, and either fuses a delaminated recto/verso pair into one sheet or splits it into two full sheets at random. A subsequent 'alignment' of surfaces to class boundaries then propagates the hallucinated continuity into the unrolled coordinate.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: In the crushed core (roughly the inner ~15 mm radius around the axis points at x~6100, y~6000-6200 at L0), a winding sheared by a fault plane is joined by the net to the neighbouring winding on the far side of the fault; the traced surface carries a +1 winding jump, so a text column from winding n is rendered next to winding n+1 and the unrolled sheet shows a seam that looks like a crack rather than an error. Separately, papyrus delaminates at the recto/verso paste joint (two ~60-100 um layers, 7-12 voxels apart at L0): a gap-trained net counts the two halves as two windings, doubling the local winding number and producing a 'phantom' blank page between two text pages.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Density-class learning transfers material statistics, not papyrus structure. En-Gedi parchment is a single homogeneous collagen layer (no two-orientation fibre lamination, thickness 200-400 um, different carbonisation); synthetic replicas have whatever density profile the fabricator chose; legacy EduceLab fragments are at different carbonisation states and beamline settings. A net pretrained or 'referenced' on these learns 'sheet = one dense band', the exact opposite of the two-layer signal R2 needs to split fused sheets, and the owner's toxic-data rule forbids parchment in any role.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Two windings pressed together in the core (sequence outward: circumferential-layer, axial-layer, circumferential-layer, axial-layer, ~300-400 um total) are labelled as one 'dense sheet' because every training exemplar of a dense band was a single sheet; the unroller renders a double-thickness slab whose 'recto' sampling depth falls on the verso of the inner sheet - the ink layer is missed entirely, and nothing in the output indicates it.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: The signal R2 names is sub-voxel at the only resolution that exists for PHerc0268. Fibre diameter 15-20 um = ~2 voxels at 8.64 um; the ink film is < 1 voxel thick; the first Fresnel fringe width at 116 keV with 1.2 m propagation is sqrt(lambda*z) = sqrt(1.07e-11 m * 1.2 m) = 3.6 um, also sub-voxel, so edge enhancement is already integrated out by the detector pixel. nnUNet additionally resamples to the training set's median spacing (e.g. 7.91 um Diamond Scroll 1, 3.24 um ESRF scans, 9.362 um JULY scrolls), so the first-stage 3x3x3 kernels see a different number of voxels per fibre than at deployment. If the net is run at L2 (34.56 um) to make compute fit, no fibre information remains at all and the method silently degenerates into an air-gap detector - the thing it claims to replace.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A net fine-tuned on PHerc0139/0814 (9.362 um JULY) and run on PHerc0268 (8.64 um, 8 % finer) sees fibre bundles ~8 % larger in voxels; its 'ordered fibre' activation shifts, and the recto/verso boundary class becomes unreliable in exactly the fused regions it was meant to resolve. The project has already measured a version of this: packages/orgseg-ink/README.md records that at 2 cm tile scale, fibre and crush periodicity scored as high as text (only 1.8 % of known-text tiles exceed the junk 99th percentile) - a texture classifier at the wrong scale confuses fibre with ink, which is precisely the 'ordered fibre vs amorphous ink' class pair R2 relies on.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Ink as a 'density class' is physically unsupported at 8.64 um: carbon ink on carbonised papyrus is carbon on carbon; the usable ink evidence (what ink_9um actually learns) is surface morphology and partial-volume texture on a rendered surface, which requires the surface first. Making unrolling depend on an ink class is circular.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: The unroller would choose between two candidate surfaces in the core by which one shows more 'ink class' - i.e. by which one the net hallucinates text on. This is the exact failure the First Letters rules warn about (34_prizes.md line 224: large-window models invent plausible letterforms); it would also contaminate the project's sealed-benchmark discipline because geometry would be selected on the ink readout.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: A density/texture classifier with no explicit outlier model assigns every dense inclusion to its nearest trained class. Mineral debris (calcite, ash crystals: bright, isotropic) becomes 'ink' or 'dense fibre'; a hair or root filament bridging an air gap (50-80 um cylinder, bright, linear) becomes 'sheet' and creates a layer bridge; ring artefacts - concentric with the reconstruction rotation axis, invariant along z - are perfect fake 'circumferential fibre layers' with zero axial variation.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: PHerc0268's scroll axis (x~6100-6190, y~5900-6230 at L0 for z >= 2224 in logs/fl4/axis_PHerc0268.json) sits within ~1-2 mm of the reconstruction rotation centre (6072, 6072); ring artefacts are therefore nearly concentric with the windings. A circumferential-texture class detector fires on every ring, adding phantom 'recto layers' between real sheets near the core, inflating the winding count by a z-invariant pattern. A single hair across a 200 um gap in the core lets a gap-plus-density tracer hop from winding n to n+1 with a continuous 'sheet' class path.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: The training library is a handful of scrolls (organizer-labelled 0139, 0814, 0800, 1203 segments) whose macro collapse shapes are few. The net's coarsest stage (128^3 patch at 5 levels = 1-4 mm context) learns 'sheets are concentric arcs with 5-50 mm radius of curvature in roughly round rolls', and 3-D MAE pretraining on a few whole volumes memorises those volumes' crush geometry rather than papyrus physics.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: The crushed core of PHerc0268 contains sub-millimetre-radius folds (buckled sheets) and flat stacked packets with no curvature. A net that has only seen round rolls under-segments tight folds (predicts one surface through a hairpin) and over-segments flat stacks (predicts phantom curvature), and no held-out scroll in the library has this collapse type, so the validation loss never shows it.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: 'Multi-density alignment' across beamlines treats reconstructed grey values as calibrated density. They are not: PHerc0268 is uint8, masked, windowed, phase-retrieved with a delta/beta filter chosen by the organizers; Diamond I12 scans (54 keV), ESRF BM18 scans (other energies/propagation distances) and EduceLab legacy volumes have different filters, different ring/beam profiles and different windowing. The same material has different grey statistics in each.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A class boundary learned as 'grey level 140-170 = ordered fibre' on an ESRF 3.24 um JULY volume maps onto PHerc0268's 8.64 um 116 keV window as a different material class; the net's output histogram on PHerc0268 would be dominated by one class across the whole core and nobody would notice without a per-scroll calibration test, which R2 does not specify.

audit.hardened_alternative:
Keep the kernel of R2 - the papyrus sheet is a bilayer whose fibre direction alternates (recto fibres circumferential, verso fibres axial), so going radially outward the sequence is [air] R(circumferential) V(axial) [air] R V ..., which gives a winding-count signal independent of air gaps, disambiguates delamination (R-only or V-only slabs) and fusion (R V R V in one slab), and depends on the outward direction from the umbilicus model (so it is consistent with the owner's ordering: umbilicus first). Drop the learned net; implement explicit, measured operators.

1. Base sheet-presence signal: the organizers' m7 surface probability (20251110183117-surface-20260413222639-surface-m7-L0-th0.2.zarr, level 0), audited by sampling (project rule: organizer products are data, verified, not trusted). Slabs = connected runs of m7 > 0 along the local normal. Air gaps remain the primary signal where they exist; the orientation signal is used only to resolve the slabs that gaps cannot.

2. Screening pass (cheap, whole volume): at level 1 (17.28 um; 7417 x 6073 x 6073 = 2.7e11 voxels, ~1.4e11 inside the mask) compute for every m7 slab its thickness along the local normal and the distance to the next slab; the local pitch is measured per region as the median inter-slab distance (RULES.md D0-SETTLED 8), never hard-coded. Flag decision tiles (256^3 at L0): slab thickness > 2x the regional mode (suspected fusion), two slabs closer than 0.5x regional pitch (suspected delamination), low planar coherence of the slab normal field (crush), or any tile inside the core radius. Expected flagged fraction ~15-20 % of the masked volume (core cross-section ~707 mm^2 of ~8500 mm^2, plus flagged outer tiles).

3. Fibre-orientation feature, computed only in flagged tiles, only at level 0 (fibres are ~2 voxels; invisible at 69 um; L1 use permitted only if metric M1 passes at L1): 3-D structure tensor with Gaussian derivative sigma_g = 1 voxel (8.6 um) and two integration scales, sigma_w = 3 voxels (26 um, fibre-bundle scale) for fibre direction and sigma_w = 8 voxels (69 um, sheet scale) for the sheet normal. Eigen-decomposition per voxel (closed form). Sheet normal = e1 of the coarse tensor; fibre direction = e3 of the fine tensor; planar coherence c_p = (l1-l2)/(l1+l2+l3), in-plane linear anisotropy c_l = (l2-l3)/(l1+l2+l3). Angle phi between fibre direction and the local axis tangent supplied by the umbilicus model (U1 spline tangent in clean regions, U3 mini-umbilicus tangent in the core). Voxel classes: R if c_l above the clean-winding 10th-percentile threshold and phi > 60 deg; V if phi < 30 deg; X (amorphous: ash, filler, no fibre texture) if c_l below threshold; M (mineral/outlier) if grey > the tile's 99.9th percentile of papyrus grey and the tensor is isotropic; H (hair/crack edge) if l1 ~ l2 >> l3 with a linear extent > 300 um. H and M voxels are excluded, never bridged across. Ring artefacts are rejected by a z-invariance test: a candidate R layer whose fine-tensor response is constant along z over > 1 mm and whose azimuthal position is constant in reconstruction-polar coordinates is an artefact, not papyrus (fibre texture modulates at fibre-bundle scale along z).

4. Radial state grammar per slab (replaces 'alignment'): along the local normal through each flagged slab (ray length +/- one local pitch), run a duration-explicit Viterbi decoding with the grammar AIR* (R V) AIR*, allowing X and M anywhere, with per-layer thickness priors (40-150 um each, measured from clean outer windings of PHerc0268 itself, no cross-scroll transfer) and emissions on (grey, c_l, phi-class) using Student-t (heavy-tailed) likelihoods so inclusions do not drag the path. Decisions: exactly one R->V transition = one winding; R V R V = two fused windings, split at the V->R transition; R-only or V-only = delaminated half, paired with the adjacent complementary half within 0.5x local pitch; otherwise the slab is marked AMBIGUOUS and reported, never forced. Where the umbilicus model's outward sign has low confidence (the core), the grammar is decoded in both polarities; disagreement = AMBIGUOUS.

5. Guard against the straightjacket: nothing global is fitted; the sheet normal is local (coarse tensor e1 cross-checked against the organizer normal grids), the outward sign is the only input from the umbilicus, and crack faces (planar structure with e1 perpendicular to the sheet normal) are never accepted as sheets, which addresses the documented grower-hops-at-cracks pitfall.

6. Interface to the rest of the pipeline: the output is a per-slab record (winding index, R/V depth, confidence, AMBIGUOUS flag) that the tracers (R3) and the ink models consume; ink detection is never an input to geometry. Every threshold (phi cut-offs, c_l percentile, thickness priors, pitch) is declared in RULES.md before the core is processed.

validation_metrics.name: M1 recto/verso orientation separability (and rolling polarity)
validation_metrics.definition: For >= 200 m7 slabs in >= 3 clean z-bands (top and bottom of PHerc0268, outer windings), split each slab into inner and outer halves along the local normal and compute the ROC AUC of the fibre angle phi (to the axis tangent) between inner-half and outer-half voxels; also the fraction of slabs whose inner half is the circumferential one (polarity vote).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: AUC >= 0.80 at level 0 (chance 0.5); polarity agreement >= 90 % across z-bands and azimuth octants. AUC >= 0.75 at level 1 is required before any L1 use of the feature. Below 0.60 at L0 the orientation feature is rejected for this scroll.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Uses only the physical prior that a sheet has two layers of orthogonal fibres; the slab halves are defined by m7 geometry, the angle by the structure tensor; no labels. The polarity (recto inward) is measured, not assumed.

validation_metrics.name: M2 texture-destruction null
validation_metrics.definition: Repeat M1 on the same tiles after (a) Gaussian blur sigma = 2 voxels (17 um: kills fibre texture, keeps 100-200 um sheets) and (b) phase randomisation of each tile; report the AUC drop.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: AUC under (a) <= 0.60 and under (b) <= 0.55. If the blurred AUC stays high the 'orientation' signal is macro shape or ring artefact, not fibre, and the feature is rejected (guards modes 3, 4, 5).
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: A within-data ablation: the real signal must live at the fibre scale by construction; the null is the same data with that scale removed.

validation_metrics.name: M3 ray-count spread (spiral self-consistency)
validation_metrics.definition: For each z in clean bands, count accepted windings along 72 rays from the umbilicus to the outer edge; spread = max - min over azimuth. For an Archimedean spiral the count along rays differs by at most 1 across azimuths.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: >= 95 % of clean z-slices have spread <= 1 (<= 2 where an outermost sheet ends, declared per slice before counting). In the core the spread is reported per z with no threshold, together with the AMBIGUOUS fraction.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: A topological invariant of a rolled sheet; needs only the axis and the slab records.

validation_metrics.name: M4 slab-grammar outcome fractions
validation_metrics.definition: Fraction of slabs decoded as exactly R V (one winding), R V R V (fused, split), R-only/V-only (delaminated, paired), and AMBIGUOUS, before and after the grammar step, per region (clean / core).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Clean bands: >= 90 % exactly R V after processing, AMBIGUOUS <= 2 %. Core: reported, not thresholded; a core AMBIGUOUS fraction > 50 % means R2's premise does not hold on this scroll's core and the unroller must say so in the FL-14 disclosure.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Internal consistency with the bilayer prior; pairing/splitting is validated by M3 (the corrected count must restore the spread <= 1 property where m7 alone violates it).

validation_metrics.name: M5 contamination injection
validation_metrics.definition: Into 500 real L0 decision tiles insert synthetic artefacts: bright spheres 30-100 um (mineral), bright cylinders 50-80 um dia x 1-3 mm spanning a gap (hair), a z-invariant concentric sinusoid at the measured ring-artefact amplitude, and +50 % Gaussian noise; measure the ray winding count through the insert and the fraction of voxel class flips within 200 um of it.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Winding count unchanged on >= 98 % of rays through the insert; class flips <= 5 % of voxels within 200 um; the ring-artefact insert must be classified H/artefact, not R, in >= 95 % of cases.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Perturbation of real data: the pre-insert decoding is the reference; the test is invariance, and synthetic data is used only as a test, never for training.

validation_metrics.name: M6 rendered-surface fibre continuity
validation_metrics.definition: Render each traced surface with vc_render_tifxyz at the decoded recto depth; compute the in-plane fibre coherence c_l and the fraction of surface area where the fibre direction is within 20 deg of the local circumferential direction; detect contiguous lines of direction discontinuity (a layer hop or a crossing to the verso of another winding).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: >= 85 % consistent area per surface; any discontinuity line > 2 mm cuts the surface there and is logged; a surface with < 70 % is rejected from reading.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Fibres on a correctly traced recto are continuous and circumferential by physics; a hop shows as a direction seam. Uses only the rendered CT texture.

validation_metrics.name: M7 independent-product agreement
validation_metrics.definition: If the organizers' 'lasagna' prediction is a winding/layer labelling, Cohen's kappa between its winding index and ours on clean bands and on the core, with a disagreement map; if the organizers run their fibers model on PHerc0268, angular agreement of fibre direction with our structure-tensor e3.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: kappa >= 0.80 on clean bands (reported only on the core); fibre direction agreement median angular error <= 15 deg. Disagreement is evidence to inspect, not an error of either side; neither product is ground truth.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Agreement between two independent estimators of the same physical quantity.

validation_metrics.name: M8 tiling/seed reproducibility
validation_metrics.definition: Re-run the full decision pass with the tile grid shifted by 50 voxels and all thresholds held; fraction of slabs with identical winding assignment and identical AMBIGUOUS status.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: >= 99 % in clean bands; reported in the core; any systematic dependence on tile placement is a bug, not a result.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Self-agreement under an irrelevant change of the computation.

audit.compute_estimate:
R2 as specified: level 0 is 2.19e12 voxels (2.2 TB uint8 raw), ~1.1e12 inside the mask. A 3-D nnUNet-class net on 4 CPU cores runs ~0.2-1 Mvox/s with sliding-window overlap; at 0.5 Mvox/s inference alone is 2.2e6 s = ~25 days per container, ~3-4 days spread over all 8 sibling containers with perfect sharding and streaming (1 GB disk, 11 GB tmpfs: nothing can be staged). Training nnUNet 3-D full-res (1000 epochs x 250 iterations x batch 2 x 128^3) takes ~2 days on one GPU; on 4 CPUs it is 50-100x slower, i.e. 100-200 days, and there are no PHerc0268 labels other than another model's output. 3-D MAE pretraining on whole volumes is out of the question by a further order of magnitude. Running the net at level 2 (3.4e10 voxels, ~9.5 h at 1 Mvox/s) is feasible but destroys the fibre signal the method depends on. Verdict: infeasible as specified.

Hardened alternative: screening pass at level 1 on m7 slabs (slab thickness and spacing along the normal; ~1.4e11 masked voxels read once, simple separable filters, ~2e7 vox/s) ~ 20 h on one container or ~2.5 h each across 8. Orientation pass at level 0 only in flagged tiles: a 256^3 tile with 16-voxel halo is 23.9 Mvox; ~15 separable 3-D Gaussian filter passes plus closed-form 3x3 eigen-decomposition is ~40 s per tile with numpy/scipy on 4 cores; memory ~1.2 GB per tile (12 float32 arrays), so 2 workers per container fit in 15 GB. With 15-20 % of the masked volume flagged (6,500-13,000 tiles) this is 3-6 days on one container, 0.5-0.75 days across 8. Download: the flagged share of a ~1 TB compressed L0 zarr is ~150-200 GB total, streamed chunk by chunk through the existing anonymous HTTPS zarr reader into tmpfs (never to the 1 GB disk); at 50-75 MB/s per container ~1 h each. The per-slab Viterbi grammar and all eight metrics are negligible (minutes). Validation on clean bands (M1-M4) needs ~200 tiles, ~2-3 h on one container, and must run before any core processing is committed.
audit.what_to_reject_outright: (1) Training, fine-tuning or MAE-pretraining any nnUNet-like 3-D network for PHerc0268 on this hardware: 100-200 CPU-days for training, ~25 CPU-days per container for level-0 inference, and no labels except another model's output (distilling m7 adds no information and inherits its errors). (2) The claim that ink is a 'micro density' class separable from fibre at 8.64 um: the ink film is sub-voxel, carbon on carbon, the Fresnel fringe (3.6 um) is sub-voxel, and the project's own calibration found fibre/crush periodicity indistinguishable from text at tile scale; any geometry step that consumes an ink class is circular and selects surfaces on hallucinated text. (3) 'Multi-density alignment' across beamlines/energies/phase-retrieval filters as if uint8 windowed grey values were calibrated density. (4) En-Gedi parchment in any role, including 'reference only' and including setting thickness or density priors - the owner's own toxic-data rule, and it teaches the opposite structure (single homogeneous layer) from the bilayer signal R2 needs. (5) 'ESRF/Diamond unreleased raw volumes' for pretraining: not in the open data, not available, and a provenance/eligibility liability. (6) 'Synthetic carbonised papyrus replicas' as training ground truth: they do not exist, and if made they would bake one fabricator's macro geometry into the model (mode 5); synthetic perturbations of real data are acceptable only as tests (M5). (7) Any run of the net at level 2 or coarser 'to fit the budget': it silently becomes an air-gap detector, the very thing R2 claims to replace. (8) Processing the crushed core before M1-M4 pass on the clean bands of PHerc0268 itself, and before the umbilicus model supplies a validated outward sign - the current 19 centroid axis points drift ~20 mm in y over the top ~32 mm of the scroll and must not be used as the radial sign for the orientation grammar.

refuted_claims.claim: Radial grammar AIR* (R V) AIR*: 'R V R V = two fused windings, split at the V->R transition'; 'R-only or V-only = delaminated half'; anything else AMBIGUOUS.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Every kollesis (sheet join: 1-2 cm overlap every ~10-25 cm of roll, i.e. roughly 5-10 % of every winding's circumference) is a genuine R V R V stack inside ONE winding (recto of the overlapping sheet lies inward over the verso of the other, whichever sheet is on top). The stated rule adds +1 winding at every join, and M3 then records the resulting spread >= 1 at those azimuths as topology rather than as the grammar's error. Fusion plus delamination (R(n) | V(n)R(n+1) | V(n+1)) produces V R slabs that the grammar does not contain; hairpin folds in the crushed core produce same-letter adjacency (R V V R, V R R V = self-contact), which the rule marks AMBIGUOUS at exactly the topology the orientation signal was introduced to resolve; intra-layer cleavage along fibre bundles (V split into V V with no gap) is indistinguishable from a fold by orientation alone.
refuted_claims.fix: Complete the language over half-layers: R|V within one sheet; V|R = sheet-sheet contact (fusion); R|R or V|V = self-contact (fold) or cleavage. Accept a split into two windings only if both decoded sheets persist > 3 cm in-plane in neighbouring tiles; a 4-layer stack that loses one sheet at a step edge on each side within < 2.5 cm is a kollesis and keeps one winding index (declare the measured kollesis spacing from clean windings first). Same-letter adjacency is a fold only if an in-plane hairpin is traced in adjacent tiles, otherwise cleavage (two halves summing to one layer thickness).

refuted_claims.claim: 3-D structure tensor with isotropic separable Gaussians: sigma_g = 1 voxel, sigma_w = 3 voxels (26 um) gives each half-layer's fibre direction; sigma_w = 8 voxels (69 um) gives the sheet normal; ~15 passes, ~40 s per 256^3 tile.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The only slab-thickness measurement available (one m7-th0.2 L1 chunk 13/15/24 in a clean outer region where the normal is ~x) gives median 4 L1 voxels (~69 um, p90 ~240 um) for the WHOLE two-layer slab, so each half-layer is ~4 L0 voxels (~35 um). An isotropic sigma_w = 3 window (effective +/-6 voxels) spans the entire slab and averages the R and V halves; the per-half e3 is a mixture and the M1 AUC is capped by the operator, not by the physics. In-plane, the bundle stripe period (50-100 um = 6-12 voxels) exceeds the window, so e3 is also unstable. The coarse window (effective +/-16 voxels) spans slab + gap + next slab (probed pitch in that chunk ~12 L1 voxels), mixing neighbouring windings into the 'sheet normal'.
refuted_claims.fix: Steer the window by the sheet normal: sigma_n ~ 1 voxel along the coarse normal, sigma_t = 6-10 voxels in-plane (anisotropic Gaussian, not separable in the global axes), or compute in-plane 2-D orientation on depth-resolved shells of each m7 slab (the operation vc_render_tifxyz already performs and M6 already uses). Fix the in-plane scale from a measured in-plane power spectrum, not from a nominal fibre diameter. Re-estimate per-tile cost after the change (a steered filter is 3-10x the separable cost; still hours per container, see compute).

refuted_claims.claim: 'The first Fresnel fringe width sqrt(lambda z) = 3.6 um is sub-voxel, so edge enhancement is already integrated out by the detector pixel' (used to argue there is no micro-density signal).
refuted_claims.why_wrong: At 116 keV the absorption of a 100 um carbon sheet is ~0.2 %; essentially all contrast in this volume IS propagation phase contrast (Fresnel number at the pixel scale p^2/(lambda z) ~ 5.8: the near-field edge-enhancement regime these scans are designed for), converted to a density-like map by a Paganin-type filter. If the fringe were integrated out there would be no image at all. The scale that actually decides which sub-sheet texture survives is the retrieval filter length L = sqrt(pi lambda z delta/beta): ~20 um at delta/beta = 10, ~63 um at 100, ~200 um at 1000 (carbon's physical delta/beta at 116 keV is ~1e3); attenuation of a feature with period P is ~1/(1+(L/P)^2). The audit never mentions this parameter, and nothing in the repo records it.
refuted_claims.fix: Read the reconstruction's delta/beta (or equivalent) from the scan metadata; measure the in-plane texture PSD on a clean rendered sheet of PHerc0268 at L0 and its ratio to the phase-randomised null; set all orientation scales from that measurement. Keep the conclusion 'ink is not a separable density class for geometry' on the carbon-on-carbon and sealed-benchmark grounds only; drop the Fresnel argument.

refuted_claims.claim: Voxel classes R if phi > 60 deg, V if phi < 30 deg, where phi is the angle between the fibre direction and the local axis tangent supplied by the umbilicus model.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: This assumes the sheet's tangent plane contains the axis direction (normal perpendicular to the axis). In buckled, folded or flat-stacked packets of the crushed core the sheet normal tilts towards z; where the normal is within ~30 deg of the axis, BOTH halves' in-plane fibres are at ~90 deg to the axis and both are labelled R; the absolute label fails silently exactly where the signal is needed. The physically invariant signal is the ~90 deg relative rotation between adjacent half-layers, which needs no axis.
refuted_claims.fix: Primary feature = in-plane angle difference between the two depth quartiles of a slab (bimodality at 90 deg), axis-free. Assign the absolute R/V name only where |n . t_axis| < 0.5 and a validated axis direction exists; elsewhere report 'alternation present / absent / single orientation' without names. The axis then supplies naming and ray counting, not detection.

refuted_claims.claim: M2 texture-destruction null: a Gaussian blur of sigma = 2 voxels (17 um) kills fibre texture and keeps 100-200 um sheets; blurred AUC must fall to <= 0.60 or the feature is rejected.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The orientation texture that survives phase retrieval is at fibre-bundle scale (50-100 um, 6-12 voxels), which a sigma = 2 blur attenuates by only ~20-50 %; a real signal would survive the null and be rejected as 'macro shape' by the gate's own rule (a built-in false negative). Conversely the layering period in the probed chunk is ~12 L0-equivalent... ~24 L0 voxels, close enough that the blur cannot separate 'fibre' from 'layering' either; the null does not isolate the scale it claims to.
refuted_claims.fix: Null (a) = in-plane isotropisation (randomise the in-plane Fourier phase only, keeping each voxel column's along-normal profile); null (b) = full phase randomisation; positive control = a synthetic bilayer with orthogonal stripes at the measured bundle period embedded in real PHerc0268 noise. Pass/fail bars set from these, declared before the core is touched.

refuted_claims.claim: Download: 'the flagged share of a ~1 TB compressed L0 zarr is ~150-200 GB, streamed chunk by chunk into tmpfs, ~1 h per container at 50-75 MB/s'; '~1.1e12 voxels inside the mask'; 'core cross-section ~707 mm^2 of ~8500 mm^2'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The CT zarr at L0 and L1 has compressor: null with 128^3 chunks of exactly 2,097,152 B; fill chunks are absent (HEAD 0/0/0 -> 404), in-mask chunks are stored uncompressed. From the L4 mask counts in logs/fl4/axis_PHerc0268.json the mask is ~32 % of the box: ~7.0e11 L0 voxels (~0.7 TB on S3), mid-scroll cross-section ~5100 mm^2 (270k L4 px x 0.019 mm^2), so the audit's 1.1e12 and 8500 mm^2 are ~1.6x high and the core share is ~14 % before any outer tile is flagged. A 288^3 tile straddles 27-64 chunks (54-134 MB); 7k-13k tiles move 0.4-1.2 TB in total without a cache, and a cache over one z-chunk-row is 18 GB (5.8 GB in-mask), too large for RAM. One sequential chunk measured here: 0.42-0.56 s, TTFB-bound (3.7-5 MB/s per stream); the only parallel figure (~70 req/s with 32 threads, tools/umb/fetch_zarr.py docstring) is unverified. /dev/shm is RAM-backed: tmpfs staging and worker RSS share the same 15 GB; '11 GB tmpfs' is not extra storage.
refuted_claims.fix: Per-tile fetch of its 27-64 chunks with a small LRU (<= 2 GB), 2 workers x <= 2 GB, total RSS + tmpfs <= 12 GB; budget 50-150 GB per container per pass => 10 min to 2 h at 20-140 MB/s. Measure the 32-thread rate on 200 in-mask chunks before committing; the conclusion (hours, feasible) survives, the audit's bytes do not.

refuted_claims.claim: Screening pass at L1: ~1.4e11 masked voxels read once at ~2e7 vox/s, ~20 h on one container; slab thickness and spacing computed from the CT.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Arithmetic: 1.4e11 / 2e7 = 7,000 s ~ 2 h, not 20 h, and the masked count at L1 is ~9e10. More importantly the CT is not needed: the m7 product at L1 is binary {0, 255} (probed chunk: unique values {0,255}, 33 % filled, 0.84 MB per 192^3 zstd chunk, ~8x compression), so slab run-lengths and gaps along a normal come from ~15-20 GB of m7 chunks, and the normal field already exists from the organizers (lasagna nx, ny at level 2 = 34.6 um; normal-grids at L0, grid-step 64). 'm7 surface probability' is also wrong: th0.2 has already binarised it; nothing softer than 0/255 is available.
refuted_claims.fix: Screening = m7-L1 run-length pass along organizer normals (audited by sampling against our coarse tensor), ~1-3 h per container including download; the CT at L1 is not read. State m7 as a binary papyrus mask in every downstream rule.

refuted_claims.claim: M7: 'if the organizers' lasagna prediction is a winding/layer labelling, Cohen's kappa between its winding index and ours'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The lasagna product is {cos (level 1), grad_mag, nx, ny (level 2)} with umbilicus_json = '' (PHerc0268.lasagna.json): an in-plane normal field at 17-35 um, not a labelling; kappa on a winding index is undefined and M7 as written can never run.
refuted_claims.fix: M7 = per-slab angular agreement between our coarse-tensor e1 projected in-plane and lasagna (nx, ny), median <= 15 deg with a sign-consistency map, plus agreement of slab thickness with the normal-grids product where both exist. This is computable today.

refuted_claims.claim: Per-layer thickness priors 40-150 um 'measured from clean outer windings'; fusion flagged at slab thickness > 2x the regional mode.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The one probed m7-th0.2 chunk gives a two-layer slab of median ~69 um, i.e. ~35 um per layer, below the stated 40 um floor: the prior as quoted would reject real layers on this scroll. m7 at th0.2 also marks only the dense part of the sheet (CT > p60 runs: median 3 L1 voxels), so m7 thickness is not the papyrus thickness; a 2x rule on it is a rule on the model output.
refuted_claims.fix: Measure the thickness distribution per region twice (m7 runs and CT along-normal profile), declare the numbers, use robust quantiles (p10-p90) as the duration prior; fusion flag at > 1.7x the regional median two-layer thickness with the kollesis exception; never quote a prior as 'measured' before the measurement exists in logs.

refuted_claims.claim: The outward sign and axis tangent come from the umbilicus model (U1 spline tangent in clean regions, U3 mini-umbilicus tangent in the core); where its confidence is low, decode in both polarities.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The project's own axis run (logs/umb/PHerc0268/slabs.json: 24 slabs covering the top ~25 mm at L3) has 0 slabs with confidence >= 0.5 and a median residual of ~10 mm; the only slab >= 0.3 is at z0 = 48 (0.45). There is at present no validated axis, no validated axis direction and no declared clean band anywhere on PHerc0268, so steps 3-4 and M3 have no admissible input, and the proposal has no fallback except the 19 centroid points it forbids. Separately, polarity is nearly irrelevant to the grammar as written (R V read backwards is V R: one transition either way), so 'both polarities' buys nothing; what the axis actually supplies is the ray for counting and the naming in the phi rule.
refuted_claims.fix: Gate all orientation work on DECL-UMB-1 bars passing for at least one z-band. Until then run only the axis-free parts (M1/M2 with the relative-angle feature) on m7 slabs in the outermost 5 mm of radius, where the sheet normal is perpendicular to z by construction of the mask boundary.

refuted_claims.claim: Ring artefacts rejected by a z-invariance test (fine-tensor response constant along z over > 1 mm at constant azimuth in reconstruction-polar coordinates).
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Most ring artefacts come from per-row flat-field errors: a bad detector pixel affects one detector row = one z-slice, so rings change slice to slice and are not z-invariant over 116 slices; only full-column defects are. The test passes the common case. The project's st_axis pipeline already applies the correct operator (per-slice polar high-pass about the image centre).
refuted_claims.fix: Per-slice polar high-pass (remove azimuthally constant components about the image centre) before any tensor, plus the DECL-UMB-1 decoy test M7 (no concentricity with the image centre over > 10 mm when the mask centroid is > 2 mm away); keep the z-invariance test only as an additional flag for column defects.

refuted_claims.claim: H (hair/crack edge) if l1 ~ l2 >> l3 with linear extent > 300 um; crack faces rejected because their e1 is perpendicular to the sheet normal; H and M voxels excluded, never bridged.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: l1 ~ l2 >> l3 is a line-like tensor (a hair); a crack FACE is plane-like (l1 >> l2 ~ l3), the same signature as a sheet, so it can only be separated from a sheet by orientation relative to the sheet normal, which is undefined in folded packets of the core, exactly where cracks are densest. A hair in contact with a sheet gives a mixed plane+line tensor that neither rule catches, re-enabling the bridge the rule was meant to block.
