refuted_claims.fix: Detect lines with a dedicated line filter (Frangi-type at 50-80 um) and subtract them before the sheet tensor; identify crack faces by their grey profile (air on both sides at the fine scale) rather than by orientation; log every excluded component with its extent.

refuted_claims.claim: 'The usable ink evidence (what ink_9um actually learns) is surface morphology and partial-volume texture on a rendered surface.'
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Asserted as fact; nothing in the repo establishes the mechanism of the ink model, and the audit cannot know what the network learned. The rule 'ink is never an input to geometry' is correct, but on the sealed-benchmark and circularity grounds alone.
refuted_claims.fix: Keep the rule, drop the mechanism claim, cite only 34_prizes.md's warning and the rowscore calibration in packages/orgseg-ink/README.md as the evidence.

refuted_claims.claim: Expected flagged fraction ~15-20 % of the masked volume; 3-6 days on one container, 0.5-0.75 days across 8.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The core is ~14 % of the ~5100 mm^2 mid-scroll cross-section, but the outer-tile share flagged by low planar coherence in a crushed scroll is unknown and could be several times the core share; the audit presents a guess as an expectation. The per-tile time, on my count (9 passes at sigma 1, 18 at sigma 3, 18 at sigma 8 over 23.9 Mvox float32, plus two closed-form 3x3 eigendecompositions) is ~25-40 s on ONE core, so 4 cores with 2 workers give ~20 s per tile wall; 7k-13k tiles = 1.6-3 days on one container, 5-9 h across 8, i.e. the audit's figure is roughly right by accident.
refuted_claims.fix: Budget for up to 50 % flagged (~21k tiles): ~5 days on one container, ~14 h across 8 at 2 workers; still feasible. Report the measured flagged fraction from the screening pass before scheduling the L0 pass.

verdict.surviving_core: What survives both lenses, stated precisely: (1) The original R2 (nnUNet-class 3-D net, cross-beamline 'multi-density' alignment, MAE pretraining on unavailable raw volumes, parchment in any role, synthetic replicas as truth, ink as a geometric density class) is rejected; its compute case is even worse than the audit says (nnUNet defaults of step-0.5 overlap and mirror TTA multiply the ~25 CPU-days per container by up to ~50x), it has no PHerc0268 labels, and it violates the owner's toxic-data and provenance rules. (2) The one physical kernel is sound: a papyrus sheet is a bilayer with orthogonal fibre bundles (recto circumferential, verso axial), so along a normal through a stack the orientation alternates by ~90 deg between adjacent half-layers; this is independent of air gaps and, read as a sequence of half-layers, distinguishes one sheet (R|V) from sheet-sheet fusion (V|R contact), self-contact/folds (R|R, V|V) and single-layer delamination (one orientation only). It survives only as the RELATIVE 90-degree alternation (axis-free); the absolute R/V naming needs a validated axis direction and holds only where the sheet normal is near-perpendicular to the axis. (3) It is detectable, if at all, only in the 8.64 um level-0 data and only at the fibre-BUNDLE scale (50-100 um period) that the unknown phase-retrieval filter leaves intact, with an operator that keeps its window inside a ~35 um half-layer along the normal while spanning >= 1 bundle period in-plane: a normal-steered anisotropic tensor or 2-D orientation on depth-resolved shells of each m7 slab. Isotropic windows cannot do it. (4) The grammar must be the complete half-layer language with kollesis, fold and cleavage rules and an in-plane persistence test; the version in the audit miscounts every sheet join. (5) The layered design is right: binary m7 (0/255) slabs as the base, organizer normals (lasagna nx/ny at L2, normal-grids at L0) as the first normal estimate, orientation only in screened tiles, a per-slab record (winding index, alternation state, confidence, AMBIGUOUS) as the interface, ink never upstream of geometry, all thresholds measured on PHerc0268's own clean windings and declared before the core is processed. (6) Compute for this hardened form is feasible on the stated hardware: screening ~1-3 h per container from m7-L1 alone; L0 orientation pass 7k-21k tiles at ~20 s wall per tile with 2 workers (~2 GB each), 0.4-1.2 TB of uncompressed 128^3 chunks fetched per tile with a <= 2 GB LRU, 50-150 GB per container per pass at a parallel rate still to be measured, outputs small enough for the 1 GB disk; total RSS + tmpfs must stay under ~12 GB because /dev/shm is RAM. (7) Metrics that survive unchanged: M3 (ray-count spread, once an axis exists), M4 (outcome fractions, with the kollesis class added), M5 (contamination injection), M6 (rendered-surface fibre continuity), M8 (tile-shift reproducibility). M1 survives only on depth quartiles with the steered operator; M2 only with the in-plane-isotropisation null; M7 only as normal-field agreement with lasagna. Nothing in the hardened alternative resolves shear-plane winding offsets or floating fragments; it reports them as AMBIGUOUS, which is the correct and only honest output for those.

audit.strategy: Audit R3 by first reconstructing the mechanism of the failure we have already observed with the closest existing implementation (VC3D vc_grow_seg_from_seed with organizer normal grids: on-layer between cracks, one-layer jump at each crack, DECL-FL-4-A8, packages/xsec), then ask whether R3's added constraint (reject extensions that violate papyrus elasticity: bending-radius and strain caps) is sensitive to that mechanism at all. It is not: a layer jump across a crack is a smooth ramp of one winding pitch (0.3-0.6 mm) over the crack width (0.3-2 mm), so the jumped surface is itself geometrically valid, exactly as the radial gate was blind to it. Elasticity acts on the surface's own shape; the error is in the surface's ordinal identity (which winding it sits on). The hardened alternative therefore replaces 'elasticity' with the only quantity that changes at a jump: the ordinal position of the sheet among its neighbours along the local layering normal (lasagna-style winding-index continuity), computed at the pyramid level where layers are separable and cracks are resolved (level 2, 34.56 um), and fed into the unchanged VC3D grower as a per-sheet masked m7 so a jump has no target to snap to. Pyramid levels are chosen from the physical scales (pitch 0.3-0.6 mm, sheet 0.1-0.2 mm, cracks 0.2-2 mm). Validation must be provably jump-sensitive: synthetic jump injection with sheared displacement, index continuity on real surfaces, neighbour clearance, fibre-phase continuity across bridged cracks, and a retrospective test against the already-grown ring1 i98 patch whose jumps the owner identified. Every metric is scored before any ink model runs; the radial gate and onsheet fraction are retired as decision metrics because both are proven blind.
audit.summary_of_method_as_specified: R3 as specified: grow surfaces bottom-up from seeds with local patch growers, and at each extension step evaluate the candidate path against a papyrus elasticity model (maximum bending curvature, maximum in-plane strain/shear, no tearing or re-joining); candidates that violate the model are rejected, so the tracer cannot slip into ash, follow a crack, or hop onto an overlapping page. The intended physics: a sheet of papyrus cannot kink sharper than its bending stiffness allows or stretch more than a few percent, so any path requiring that is not the sheet. Honest comparison with what we already run: vc_grow_seg_from_seed (villa) is already a bottom-up constrained patch grower. Its optimiser combines an edge-length term (inextensibility, step_size 20 voxels = 173 um at level 0), a straightness term (a soft quadratic curvature penalty along grid rows and columns), a surface-prediction distance term on the organizer m7 prediction (th0.2), and the NORMAL term (weight 10, DECL-FL-4-A6) that aligns the local normal with the organizer normal grids, which are themselves derived from m7. R3 is therefore the same family with a hard cap instead of a soft penalty. The measured outcome of that family on PHerc0268 (ring1 i98, seed 6154.6/7869.5/4744, 60 generations, 2 x 2 cm): median |cos| 0.928, 75% of normals above 0.8, 0.90 mm/cm radial spread, i.e. it passed every geometric bar, yet the cross-section shows one layer held between cracks and a jump to the neighbouring layer at every crack; the same seed without normal grids cuts straight across windings. The onsheet fraction did not discriminate (0.676 good, 0.676 jumped, 0.628 cross-winding). We also ran with --skip-overlap-check, which disables the one topological check the grower has. Caveat on our own finding: the jump-at-cracks behaviour is verified by owner inspection on one patch (i98) plus the radiating-fibre signature on five band-0.70 renders; its frequency across the scroll is not yet quantified, and the retrospective metric below quantifies it on the patches already grown.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Smoothness is the jump mechanism, not its cure. At a crack the m7 prediction is absent, the straightness/elasticity term extrapolates the surface linearly across the gap, the normal term cannot pick a layer (adjacent windings have parallel normals and the grids are computed from the same m7), and on the far side the distance term snaps to the nearest predicted surface. If the true sheet is displaced across the crack (shear, delamination, collapse) the nearest surface is the neighbour. The resulting ramp has slope pitch/crack-width (0.4 mm over 1 mm = 22 deg) and curvature of order 1/mm, which is the same range as genuine folds in a crushed core (radius 0.2-1 mm). A cap tight enough to reject the ramp rejects real buckles; a cap loose enough to keep real buckles passes the ramp. The constraint is non-identifiable at the one scale where it would matter.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: ring1 i98 (r about 1640 voxels, 14 mm from the axis, z 4744): each crack crossing in the cross-section is a smooth ramp onto the neighbouring winding; any curvature threshold that would reject those ramps also rejects the ovalised, heavily crushed windings the owner observed in the same band (DECL-FL-4-A7-E2), and the i96/i99/i101/i103 gate failures (2.3-3.6 mm/cm spread) would simply become early terminations with no gain in sheet identity.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Hard rejection inside a greedy grower does not prevent a jump, it relocates it. When the candidate across a crack is rejected, growth continues around the crack boundary and re-enters the far side through whatever region passes the test, typically a crushed zone where adjacent layers are fused and the transition between laminae is smooth and sub-threshold. The surface then closes on itself from the other side on a different winding, producing a self-intersection or a seam; with --skip-overlap-check (ring_run.sh) nothing detects it.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: The five band-0.70 patches (results/PHerc0268_band070_renders_montage.png) already show fibres radiating from the seed in their centre layers, the signature of a surface that is not flat on one sheet; adding a hard curvature cap converts crack crossings into detours through the fused sectors of the same band, where m7-th0.2 forms one slab and the detour is invisible to any geometric test.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: A single-sheet elasticity model cannot represent delamination (recto and verso laminae separating by less than one pitch) or hairpin folds (the sheet folding back on itself at a radius near the sheet thickness, 0.1-0.2 mm). With a 173 um vertex spacing the grower cannot resolve a 150 um fold at all and shortcuts it smoothly; at a delamination it follows the lamina with the stronger m7 response, which may be the verso while the ink is on the recto. Floating fragments are unreachable by any connected grower regardless of constraint.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Crushed core of PHerc0268 (inner 2-3 mm around the axis at z mid-height): folds at sheet-thickness radius and split laminae are expected; a grown surface there is either terminated by the cap or smoothly wrong; neither outcome is distinguishable from 'on sheet' by R3's own criterion.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: The material model is wrong for the object. Carbonised papyrus is a brittle carbon foam whose geometry was set by rolling when fresh, shrinkage and embrittlement during carbonisation, brittle fracture plus plastic collapse under burial load, and 2000 years of compaction. 'Elasticity' describes none of those stages. Any numeric limit comes from fresh papyrus literature, from parchment (En-Gedi; forbidden by the owner's toxic-data rule and mechanically different: collagen, not cellulose, different thickness and fold behaviour), or from 'synthetic carbonised replicas' that do not exist as a verified dataset and would not reproduce the fracture statistics of a 2000-year collapse. Limits derived elsewhere either reject the true geometry wholesale (fragmenting the surface into between-crack islands, which pieces.py already gives us for free) or are loosened until they constrain nothing.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: The band at band_t 0.35 (ring1) is ovalised and crushed; the A5 gate (built on a near-circular assumption) already misclassified oval windings as wandering (DECL-FL-4-A7-E2). An elasticity cap tuned on an intact-core scroll (PHerc0343, read by Nieuwlaar; PHerc1203 organizer segments) would do the same to PHerc0268's crushed band and would pass every smooth ramp.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: The curvature test lives on the wrong scale. Evaluated on the VC3D 20-voxel grid at level 0 its spatial resolution is about 350 um, so a one-pitch ramp spread over a 0.5-2 mm crack occupies 2-6 vertices and is sub-threshold for any cap that preserves 0.5 mm folds. Conversely the project's umbilicus work was done at level 3 (69 um), where the pitch is 4-9 voxels, the sheet 1.5-3 voxels and compressed air gaps under 1 voxel, so layers are not separable there. Neither the level-0 mesh grid nor level 3 is the scale at which layer identity is decidable; that scale is level 2 (34.56 um: pitch 9-17 voxels, sheet 3-6, cracks 6-60, air gaps 1-3).
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A 0.4 mm jump over a 1 mm crack on ring1 i98 is a 22 deg ramp over 6 mesh vertices: the per-vertex turning angle is about 4 deg per vertex, below the turning angle of genuine ovalised windings in the same band; at level 3 the same crack is 14 voxels wide and the neighbouring layers are 5-6 voxels apart with no resolvable gap in the compressed sector.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: The data term is m7, a learned surface probability, and in a 116 keV, 1.2 m propagation scan the crack edges carry phase-contrast fringes that m7 can read as thin layers; bright mineral debris and dense inclusions produce spurious m7 blobs; where adjacent windings touch (crush) m7-th0.2 fuses them into one slab, the distance term has a flat basin across the slab, and the surface drifts between laminae smoothly. None of these is a curvature or strain violation, so the elasticity cap passes all of them; and the onsheet-fraction test failed for exactly this reason (dense cores put papyrus everywhere).
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: ring1 i96/i99/i101/i103 (same band as i98) failed the strict gate with 2.3-3.6 mm/cm spread; in the fused sectors of that band an R3 grower drifts across the slab with no detectable kink, and at a bright inclusion at a crack edge it anchors to the fringe rather than to either sheet.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: As specified R3 is parametric, so memorisation enters only through tuning: if the elasticity thresholds (or a learned path-validity classifier) are fitted on the few scrolls with good segmentations, they encode those scrolls' collapse morphology (near-circular windings, pitch about 0.4 mm, intact cores) rather than local physics, and reject the morphology of a crushed scroll. The A5 gate thresholds (median |cos| >= 0.8, spread < 2 mm/cm) were such a tuning and failed on ovalised windings.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: Thresholds tuned on PHerc0343 w047/w048 (same 8.64 um/116 keV regime, intact enough to be read) applied to PHerc0268's crushed band at r/R 0.35 would terminate growth on the real sheet while passing smooth jumps; a learned validity net trained on PHerc1203 organizer segments would do the same with less transparency.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Validation straightjacket: every surface-only geometric metric (radial cos, spread, curvature statistics, onsheet fraction, flatness) scores a jumped surface as valid, because a jumped surface is a valid surface on a different sheet. R3's own acceptance criterion is such a metric, so an R3 pipeline validated by its own criterion would again report 'verified' surfaces that are collages of windings, repeating the FL-4 error that voided 43 reads and 9 maps.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: ring1 i98: gate PASS, cross-section FAIL. Any R3 variant scored by curvature/strain compliance would PASS the same patch.

audit.hardened_alternative:
Name: co-traced sheet stack with ordinal (winding-index) continuity, feeding the unchanged VC3D grower a per-sheet masked m7. It keeps the owner's intent (bottom-up, physics-constrained, no slipping into ash, cracks or overlapping pages) and replaces the non-identifiable elasticity cap with the quantity that actually changes at a jump: the sheet's ordinal position among its neighbours. It does not need the umbilicus for local continuity (so it does not block on U1-U3); the umbilicus is used only to assign absolute winding numbers at the end.

Inputs. Raw CT and the organizer m7 surface probability at pyramid level 2 (34.56 um; 3709 x 3037 x 3037 uint8 each, 34 GB per volume, streamed from S3 in z-slabs of 64 slices = 590 MB per slab into /dev/shm, never to disk). Organizer normal grids (level 0) subsampled to level 2 as the local layering direction field n(x). No parchment, no replicas, no unreleased volumes; nothing learned.

Stage 1, ray resampling (level 2). On a (theta, z) grid of 720 x 3709 rays (0.5 deg, every slice), cast rays along the local layering normal: for the outer windings the umbilicus-radial direction where it agrees with n(x) within 30 deg, otherwise streamlines of n(x) itself (a cheap deterministic stand-in for U2's 'project back along the orientation field'). Sample raw CT after a 1 mm Gaussian high-pass (local mean removed, as already used in FL6) and m7 with trilinear interpolation (scipy map_coordinates order 1), 1500 samples per ray.

Stage 2, 1-D layer peak detection per ray. Smooth with Gaussian sigma = 1 voxel (35 um). Peaks are local maxima of the smoothed m7 profile (raw-CT high-pass as a second channel for agreement) with prominence >= 3 x MAD of the profile and full width 2-8 voxels (70-280 um). Width < 2 voxels: debris or phase-contrast fringe, discarded. Width > 8 voxels: fused slab, flagged FUSED (not a layer). Output per ray: list of (r_k, width_k, contrast_k, flag).

Stage 3, linking and the ordinal constraint. Link peaks between neighbouring rays (theta +/- 1, z +/- 1) by gated nearest-neighbour assignment (Hungarian on the banded cost where ambiguous) with cost |dr|/gate + |dwidth|/w0, gate = 0.5 x local pitch, local pitch = median spacing of consecutive peaks in a 5 x 5 ray window (robust, no global pitch assumed). Crack rule: a sheet k that loses its peak is carried across a gap of at most 2 mm (60 rays at 0.5 deg at 14 mm radius; scaled by local radius) ONLY if both neighbours k-1 and k+1 are matched across the same gap; the bridged position preserves the fractional position between the neighbours; the status is BRIDGED. If a neighbour is also missing, or a FUSED flag appears within the gap, the label is TERMINATED (a piece boundary), never bridged. Delamination (one peak splitting into two separated by < 0.5 pitch): both laminae are kept with the inner one (recto side, facing the axis) marked primary. Hairpin fold (two peaks with opposite sign of n(x)): two local labels; merging is left to the grower's overlap check, which is re-enabled. Floating fragment (no neighbour within one pitch on either side for more than one pitch of arc): excluded from unrolling, logged for U3 with its own local frame. Output: per-sheet height maps r_k(theta, z) at level 2 (int16) with a status map {OBSERVED, BRIDGED, TERMINATED}.

Stage 4, absolute winding numbers (after the U1-U3 audit, not before). Count OBSERVED sheets inward from the outermost sheet along each ray (the outer windings are the reliable reference on a crushed scroll, the core is not); a sheet's winding number is the median count over its area; the fraction of rays where the count is indeterminate (FUSED) is reported with it. If the organizer lasagna product for PHerc0268 turns out to exist and passes a line-by-line audit, it is used as an independent index field and the agreement with ours is a reported metric; it is never used blind.

Stage 5, grow and render with VC3D unchanged. For each piece of sheet k: write a sparse level-0 zarr copy of m7 that keeps only chunks within +/- 0.5 local pitch of r_k (a band about 60 voxels thick; missing chunks read as 0), and pass it as the surface volume to vc_grow_seg_from_seed with the same parameters as ring_run.sh (step 20, 60 generations, normal grids on) but WITHOUT --skip-overlap-check. The grower's distance term then has no neighbouring winding to snap to across a crack, which is the only way a local grower can be prevented from jumping. The render mask carries the BRIDGED and TERMINATED status so bridged area is never used for a text claim. pieces.py remains the trust unit.

Why this is the honest comparison. It is the same family of method that produced the only First Letters success in this scan regime (Nieuwlaar on PHerc0343: spiral chain with an umbilicus, snap to m7, lasagna layer assignment, 66-layer render), restricted to what a crushed scroll permits: local ordinal continuity instead of a global spiral, termination instead of bridging wherever identity is undecidable.

validation_metrics.name: Synthetic jump recall and fold tolerance
validation_metrics.definition: On synthetic shell stacks (extend xsec.synth): shells with pitch 0.3-0.6 mm, thickness 0.1-0.2 mm, ovalisation up to 1.5:1, cracks 0.2-2 mm wide in one shell with sheared displacement 0-0.5 pitch across the crack, fused sectors, folds of radius 0.15-1 mm, 2-voxel debris and edge fringes. Run Stages 1-3 at level-2 voxel size. Score: fraction of cracks <= 2 mm bridged to the correct shell; fraction of true folds wrongly terminated; number of bridges across fused sectors.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Correct bridge >= 95% of cracks <= 2 mm including all sheared cases; false termination on true folds <= 5%; bridges across fused sectors = 0. A one-shell-jump injected after the fact (as in test_radial_gate_is_blind_to_a_layer_jump) must be flagged by the index metric on 100% of injected cases.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Synthetic geometry only; the truth is the generator's own shell labels. This validates the detector, not the scroll, and it is the test the radial gate failed.

validation_metrics.name: Winding-index continuity on the grown surface
validation_metrics.definition: For every vertex of the final tifxyz, cast the local layering-normal ray at level 2 and count OBSERVED sheets between the vertex and the outermost sheet (or, where the outer reference is unavailable, its ordinal position between its two tracked neighbours). Metric: fraction of vertices in the modal index class of the piece, and the number of index steps >= 0.5 along any mesh row or column inside a piece.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: >= 98% of vertices in the modal class per piece; 0 index steps inside a piece; the indeterminate (FUSED) fraction is reported and must be < 10% of the piece area or the piece is split.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: From the CT itself (m7 and raw peaks along rays through the surface); no labels. Retrospective calibration: run it on the already-grown ring1 i98 tifxyz (logs/fl4t/ring1/i98/tifxyz) and i96/i99/i101/i103; it must flag an index step at each crack the owner marked on i98 and none inside the spans the owner judged on-layer. If it does not reproduce the owner's verdict it is not used.

validation_metrics.name: Neighbour clearance
validation_metrics.definition: Distance from each surface vertex to the nearest m7 layer peak that is not its own, along the local normal, divided by the local pitch measured on that ray.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: >= 0.5 for >= 98% of vertices (the DECL-SG item-10 'adjacent m7 sheets >= half the local pitch' rule made operational); vertices below 0.3 are masked out of the render.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Ray profiles through the surface at level 2 (or level 1 for the final mesh); local pitch from the same profile, so no global pitch assumption.

validation_metrics.name: Fibre-phase continuity across bridged cracks
validation_metrics.definition: On the level-0 render centre layer, for each BRIDGED crack of width <= 1 mm: dominant fibre direction from the structure tensor (sigma 3 px); 1-D intensity profiles perpendicular to the fibres in two 1 mm windows, 0.3 mm from either crack edge; normalised cross-correlation maximised over lags of +/- 0.1 mm. On the true sheet the same fibres continue across a crack; on a neighbouring sheet the fibre positions are uncorrelated.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Correlation >= 0.3 and above the per-patch null p95 on >= 80% of bridged cracks; cracks failing are relabelled UNVERIFIED and excluded from text continuity. The null is built by pairing each near-side window with the far-side window sampled one pitch away (the neighbouring winding via the index map).
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Self-calibrated on the render: the wrong-sheet null comes from the scroll itself. Recommended but not required: confirm the statistic separates on an organizer segment of PHerc0343 (same 8.64 um/116 keV regime) where cracks are visible in the render.

validation_metrics.name: Bidirectional closure across cracks
validation_metrics.definition: For every bridged crack, grow a second patch from a seed on the far side chosen by the index map, and compare the two surfaces over their overlap: fraction of overlapping vertices whose normal-direction separation is <= 0.25 local pitch.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: >= 95% of overlapping vertices within 0.25 pitch; any overlap region with a bimodal separation histogram (two layers) fails the crack.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Our own outputs only; the two grows share no seed and no bridged data, so agreement is evidence of identity rather than of smoothness.

validation_metrics.name: Human cross-section audit (retained final gate)
validation_metrics.definition: xsec cross-sections at four heights per patch, raw CT with the surface drawn, inspected by the owner; index steps from metric 2 are drawn on the same images so the automatic and human verdicts can be compared location by location.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Owner verdict 'on one layer' at all four heights, and no disagreement between the owner's marks and metric 2 (any disagreement reopens the detector, not the verdict).
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Visual, from raw CT; this is the test that caught the i98 jumps when every number passed, and it stays until metrics 2-5 have reproduced the owner's verdict on at least the nine ring1 patches.

audit.compute_estimate: All numbers are estimates for one 4-CPU, 15 GB container using /dev/shm for scratch (no local disk writes beyond logs). Level-2 index field, full scroll: 2 volumes x 34 GB streamed from S3 in 58 z-slabs of 590 MB each; per slab: ray resampling of 64 x 720 rays x 1500 samples (69 M samples per volume, about 10-20 s with 4 worker processes on map_coordinates order 1), peak detection on 46k profiles (a few seconds, vectorised), linking (about 10-30 s in numpy). Compute about 1 min per slab, I/O 1.2 GB per slab (0.5-1 min at 20-50 MB/s through the proxy), so about 1-2 h for the whole scroll on one container, or 10-20 min wall split by z-slab across the 8 containers. Peak RSS under 3 GB (two slabs plus polar tensors plus peak lists). Outputs: peak lists about 300-600 MB compressed, per-sheet height maps 5.3 MB per sheet (int16, 720 x 3709), about 60 sheets = 320 MB; keep in /dev/shm and push a copy off-box the same session because /dev/shm is wiped on restart and only 1 GB of disk exists. Band-only first run (the ring1 band z 4000-5500 at level 0 = 375 level-2 slices, 6 slabs): under 10 min including I/O, well within one container. Per patch (2 x 2 cm): masked-m7 band at level 0 is 2315 x 2315 x ~60 voxels = 320 MB raw from roughly 600-900 m7 chunks (5-10 min of S3 reads), written as a sparse blosc zarr of 100-300 MB in /dev/shm; vc_grow_seg_from_seed 60 generations about 20 min (measured in DECL-FL-4-A7-E1); render as today; metrics 2-5 under 5 min total; synthetic suite under 5 min. Total about 45-60 min per patch, eight patches in parallel across the fleet in about 1 h. Nothing here needs a GPU, a local volume copy, or more than 4 GB of RAM at once.
audit.what_to_reject_outright: 1. The elasticity/curvature/strain cap as a layer-jump preventer: by construction it is blind to a one-pitch ramp over a crack (a jumped surface is a valid surface on another sheet), and no threshold separates ramps from the genuine folds of a crushed core. It is the same soft prior VC3D already applies, hardened, and the hardened form only relocates jumps into fused sectors. 2. Any elasticity or bending parameter taken from parchment/vellum (En-Gedi, owner's toxic-data rule), from fresh papyrus mechanics, or from 'synthetic carbonised papyrus replicas' and 'unreleased ESRF/Diamond raw volumes', which do not exist as data we hold; a plan that depends on them is not a plan. 3. Hard rejection inside a greedy grower, and --skip-overlap-check in any run whose output is to be rendered. 4. Any learned path-validity classifier trained on the few intact-core scrolls' segmentations (memorises their collapse morphology; mode 5). 5. Validation of any surface by the radial gate, the onsheet fraction, curvature statistics, or any other surface-only geometric score; all are proven blind on synthetic data and on ring1 i98, and 'gate pass' is never again to be called sheet-following. 6. Any ink map or text claim on a patch that has not passed the index-continuity, neighbour-clearance and cross-section gates, and any text-continuity claim across a BRIDGED or UNVERIFIED crack. 7. Treating R3 as a new method distinct from the existing normal-grid grower; it is not, and the honest statement is that the existing grower plus layer-identity masking is the CPU-feasible path, while the identity field is the missing component.

refuted_claims.claim: Stage 1-4 geometry: a (theta, z) grid of 720 x 3709 rays cast from the umbilicus in xy, per-sheet height maps r_k(theta, z), 'ring1 at r about 1640 voxels / 14 mm from the axis', streamed in z-slabs.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The repo's own recorded geometry (logs/umb/UMB-GEOMETRY-RESULT.md, images logs/umb/L3_xz_centre.png and L4_xy_z464.png) says PHerc0268 is a roll crushed with its former axis along the volume y axis: sheets stacked along z (3-D structure tensor at level 4: |n_z| median 0.76, 45 % of coherent voxels |n_z| > 0.8), nested hairpins at both x extremes, xy sections showing a sheet face-on. It explicitly voids every earlier xy-ray step ('wrong frame; their outputs are not reused'). Rays in xy from a z-axis are near-tangent to the sheets over most of the volume, so the along-ray peak list is not an ordinal stack and the height map r_k(theta, z) is multi-valued; and in the right frame the rays run along z, which cannot be processed per z-slab at all.
refuted_claims.fix: Build the identity field in the DECL-UMB-1-A1 frame: stream y chunk rows (128 x 3709 x 3037 = 1.44 GB uint8; tools/umb/st_axis.py's reader already supports axis=1), work in xz sections, cast rays along the local structure-tensor layering normal (mostly z), and index per branch (top or bottom of each flattened loop) from the top/bottom envelope. Before any ray is cast, map the angle between ray and local normal and declare the index undefined wherever it exceeds 30 degrees (the hairpin zones).

refuted_claims.claim: The observed failure is a one-pitch smooth ramp over the crack width (pitch/crack-width, about 22 deg, curvature about 1/mm), inferred from the i98 cross-section, and this mechanism is the premise of the whole audit.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The i98 cross-sections (logs/fl4t/ring1_i98_crosssection_check.png; xsec.draw cuts z-slices only) are xy planes, which the geometry result shows are near-tangent to the layering; the gate's median |cos(n, radial_xy)| = 0.93 means the grown surface is a near-vertical wall, which in horizontal strata is a surface cutting through many sheets along crack faces, not a ramp between two neighbours. The owner's verdict 'cuts across at the cracks' (DECL-FL-4-A8) is consistent with both readings; the ramp geometry, its slope and its curvature were never measured in a plane normal to the layering.
refuted_claims.fix: Re-cut i98 (and i96/i99/i101/i103) in xz and yz through the mesh before using them as a calibration target; add the two planes to packages/xsec/xsec/xsections.py. Keep only the frame-independent part of the diagnosis: shape constraints (curvature, strain, radial cos, onsheet fraction) cannot see which sheet a surface is on.

refuted_claims.claim: The ordinal position among neighbours along the layering normal is 'the only quantity that changes at a jump', so index continuity is jump-specific.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The along-normal count also changes at every fold crossing (a hairpin adds two crossings on some rays and none on neighbouring rays), at every delamination (one lamina becomes two), and on every ray where fragmentary outer layers are present or absent. In a flattened roll every winding is a hairpin at both x extremes, so non-jump index steps occur on every single winding, not as an exception; the count-from-outside anchor also assumes a complete outermost winding, which no Herculaneum scroll has and which was never checked here.
refuted_claims.fix: Branch-local index only (no absolute winding number from this stage); hairpin zones excluded by a normal-direction criterion and marked TERMINATED; absolute winding numbers deferred to a separate fold-traversal step; the false-termination bar tested on the flattened-roll phantom family of DECL-UMB-1-A1 (tools/umb/phantom.py), not on circular shells.

refuted_claims.claim: Level 2 (34.56 um) is the scale at which layer identity is decidable: pitch 9-17 voxels, sheet 3-6, air gaps 1-3 voxels; peaks of width 2-8 voxels are layers, > 8 is FUSED.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: In a crushed-flat roll the inter-sheet gaps are closed except at sparse open seams (L3_xz_centre.png: open seams every 1-4 mm, fine lamination at 3-6 px of 69 um between them). A 1-voxel gap (35 um) is at Nyquist and is erased by the proposal's own sigma = 1 voxel smoothing (FWHM 2.35 voxels). Two fused 100-200 um sheets are 6-12 voxels, straddling the 8-voxel cut-off, so 'one thick sheet' and 'two fused sheets' are indistinguishable; the stage returns FUSED/TERMINATED over most of the compressed stack, i.e. exactly where ink was claimed. The 'pitch 0.3-0.6 mm' does not exist in the compressed direction; the spacing there is the sheet thickness.
refuted_claims.fix: Run a separability census first (fraction of the target band where consecutive laminae are resolved at level 2). Where fused, the only physical separator is the lamina fibre-orientation alternation (recto circumferential, verso axial: a 90-degree flip at each lamina boundary), which per DECL-UMB-1 is measurable only at level 0/1 (fibres absent at 34.6/69 um); do that per patch inside the masked band at level 0 (about 2315 x 2315 x 230 = 1.2e9 voxels, 10-20 min of structure tensor on 4 cores), never full-volume.

refuted_claims.claim: The identity field is independent of the grower's data term, so masking m7 by it removes the jump target.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Every link in the chain is m7: the index field is built from m7 peaks (primary channel) along rays from the organizer normal grids (themselves derived from m7, per the product name and metadata), then used to mask m7 for a grower whose normal term uses the same grids. If m7 itself bridges a sheared crack to the neighbouring sheet (surface nets are trained to continue surfaces), the index field inherits the bridge and the masked m7 keeps the ramp. The raw-CT channel is specified 'for agreement' only, with no veto. The normal grids are also a 35 GB, three-orientation, grid-step-64 community product that would need a line-by-line audit and a 10-29 GB download that the compute estimate omits.
refuted_claims.fix: Raw-CT lamina/gap peaks are the primary channel and m7 secondary; report raw-only vs m7-only index agreement and validate on the raw-only field; n(x) from a 3-D structure tensor at level 2 computed on tiles inside each chunk row (as DECL-UMB-1 does at level 3), not from the normal grids.

refuted_claims.claim: We ran with --skip-overlap-check, which disables the one topological check the grower has; re-enabling it lets the overlap check merge hairpin labels and detect self-intersections.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: In /work/villa/volume-cartographer/apps/src/vc_grow_seg_from_seed.cpp the flag is consulted only under mode == "expansion" (line 1494) and only for overlapping.json bookkeeping against other segments in the target directory; ring_run.sh runs mode "seed", where the flag is a no-op. The grower has no self-intersection test to re-enable.
refuted_claims.fix: Add an external mesh crossing/self-intersection test on the tifxyz (the DECL-SG item-10 '0 crossings' bar) and a separate hairpin-merging step; drop the claim that omitting the flag changes anything in seed mode.

refuted_claims.claim: If the organizer lasagna product for PHerc0268 exists and passes audit it serves as an independent winding-index field.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: It exists and is catalogued (data/catalogue/eligible_products.json): PHerc0268_nx, _ny, _cos, _grad_mag OME-zarrs plus PHerc0268.lasagna.json, a level-0 in-plane direction field. No winding-index array exists anywhere in the bucket; an index would have to be integrated from the direction field, which is the U2 back-projection problem, not an independent measurement.
refuted_claims.fix: Drop the index fallback; use nx/ny at most as a cross-check of n(x), as DECL-UMB-1 M6 already does.

refuted_claims.claim: Metric 5 (bidirectional closure) is independent evidence of identity because the two grows share no seed and no bridged data.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Both grows run on the same index-derived masked m7 band, so their agreement is forced by the mask under test; it measures the mask, not the sheet. As written it also grows a second patch per bridged crack (about 21 min each, measured 1275 s on i98), which for 5-10 cracks per patch is 2-3 h per patch, not the quoted 45-60 min.
refuted_claims.fix: The far-side grow uses the unmasked m7 from a far-side seed; agreement of an unconstrained grow with the masked one is evidence; one far-side grow per patch.

refuted_claims.claim: Peak RSS under 3 GB; stream slabs into /dev/shm (11 GB free tmpfs), never to disk; per-slab 1 mm Gaussian high-pass of raw CT at level 2.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: tmpfs is RAM: on the orchestrator now free -g shows 15 GB total, 7 GB available, with 3.8 GB already resident in /dev/shm, so the real budget for a new pipeline is about 7 GB including anything it puts in /dev/shm. CT chunks are 128^3 with compressor null, so a level-2 chunk row is 1.18 GB uint8 per volume and a 64-slice slab needs the whole row. A 1 mm 3-D Gaussian at level 2 is sigma 29 voxels (233-tap separable kernels) and needs float32 input and output copies (4.7 GB each) plus a +/-116-slice halo: 10-14 GB per row, which does not fit.
refuted_claims.fix: Do the high-pass in 1-D along each sampled ray after sampling (cost nil), or 2-D per xz section; keep rows chunk-aligned; compute the structure tensor on tiles with halos inside a row; hold at most one CT row plus one m7 row in uint8 (about 2.6 GB) plus float32 tiles.

refuted_claims.claim: I/O 1.2 GB per slab at 20-50 MB/s through the proxy, about 1-2 h for the whole scroll on one container.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: No throughput measurement exists anywhere in the repo (no MB/s figure in logs, tools, STATE or LEDGER); 20-50 MB/s is asserted. Level 2 of the CT is 34.2 GB uncompressed and every byte crosses the proxy (masked zeros do not compress a null-compressor zarr); 64-slice slabs refetch each 128-slice row twice unless buffered (68 GB for the CT alone); m7's level-2 chunk size, compressor and downsampling method are unverified, so its bytes are unknown. At 5 MB/s the pass is 4-8 h; at 20-50 MB/s 25-115 min.
refuted_claims.fix: Time one chunk row through the proxy before declaring any schedule; buffer rows; split the 29 rows over the 8 containers (about 4 rows each); fetch and record the m7 level-2 .zarray first.

refuted_claims.claim: Nothing here needs a local volume copy or local disk beyond logs.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: ring_run.sh's grow parameters (reused unchanged in Stage 5) set cache_size 2e9 with cache_root under /work and write the render zarr to /work; / has 1.1 GB free on the orchestrator now, so the grow as configured cannot run here, and the proposal never says where the 2 GB VC3D cache goes.
refuted_claims.fix: Put cache_root and the render in /dev/shm and count them against the 7 GB, or run Stage 5 only on siblings with verified free disk.

refuted_claims.claim: The crack bridge limit of 2 mm is 60 rays at 0.5 deg at 14 mm radius.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: 0.5 deg at 14 mm is 0.122 mm per ray, so 2 mm is 16 rays; 60 rays is 7.3 mm. A 4x error in the one number that bounds how far a sheet may be carried without observation.
refuted_claims.fix: Specify gaps in mm and convert per actual ray spacing; in the correct frame ray spacing is a grid pitch in xz, not an angle.

refuted_claims.claim: The masked m7 keeps only chunks within +/-0.5 local pitch of r_k; about 600-900 chunks per patch.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: m7 level-0 chunks are 192^3 (catalogued .zarray), i.e. 1.66 mm = 3-5 windings, so chunk-granular keeping leaves the neighbouring windings in place; and a 2 x 2 cm sheet intersects about (2315/192)^2 x 1.5-2 = 220-290 chunks (1.6-2 GB uncompressed), not 600-900. The sparse-copy idea itself is sound: core/src/Slicing.cpp returns 0 for missing blocks ('Out-of-bounds and missing-block return 0').
refuted_claims.fix: Voxel-level masking inside rewritten 192^3 chunks, zero outside the band; recount the chunk budget at 192^3.

refuted_claims.claim: Synthetic jump recall and fold tolerance: 'extend xsec.synth' with cracks, shear, fused sectors, folds, debris, ovalisation.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: packages/xsec/xsec/synth.py contains only concentric cylinders (cylinder_patch, shell_volume); none of the listed features exists, and a cylindrical generator is the wrong geometry for this scroll.
refuted_claims.fix: Build the suite on the flattened-roll phantom family (squashed spiral, hairpins, kink, debris, rings, noise) already declared in DECL-UMB-1-A1 and add sheared cracks and fused sectors to it; score false termination on hairpins explicitly.

refuted_claims.claim: Fibre-phase continuity across bridged cracks: 1-D profiles in 1 mm windows 0.3 mm from either edge, lags +/-0.1 mm, correlation >= 0.3.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Sheet fragments in a crushed roll move as rigid pieces, so a crack with 0-0.5 pitch out-of-plane shear generally has in-plane offset well beyond 0.1 mm: the test rejects true continuations. Fibre bundles are quasi-periodic (50-200 um), so a 1-D correlation peak inside +/-0.1 mm occurs between unrelated windows; the one-pitch null covers the second problem but not the first. At 8.64 um individual fibres are at the resolution limit (project fact), so the structure tensor measures strip/bundle texture, which must be stated.
refuted_claims.fix: 2-D template match with lags to +/-0.5 mm, preconditioned on equal fibre direction (structure-tensor angle within 10 degrees) in both windows; report the lag; keep the one-pitch null.

verdict.surviving_core: What survives both lenses, restated precisely. (1) The frame-independent diagnosis: any shape-only constraint or score (elasticity/curvature/strain cap, radial cos, radial spread, onsheet fraction, flatness) is blind to which sheet a surface is on; R3's cap is the straightness term VC3D already applies, hardened, and is rejected as a jump preventer. Rejections 2, 4, 5, 6 of the proposal stand (no parchment/replica/unreleased data, no learned validity classifier trained on intact-core scrolls, no surface-only validation, no text claim across BRIDGED or UNVERIFIED cracks). (2) The replacement principle: the grower must be fed an identity constraint derived from the CT along the local layering normal, and surfaces must be scored by an identity metric, with termination instead of bridging wherever identity is undecidable and the BRIDGED/TERMINATED status carried into the render mask. (3) Its admissible form on PHerc0268: in the DECL-UMB-1-A1 frame (y chunk rows of 128 x 3709 x 3037 = 1.44 GB uint8, xz sections), rays along the structure-tensor layering normal (mostly z), raw-CT lamina/gap peaks as the primary channel with m7 secondary, 1-D along-ray high-pass, gated nearest-neighbour linking in the section with a locally measured spacing (no pitch assumed), a branch-local ordinal index counted from the top or bottom envelope, hairpin zones and fused slabs declared undefined, no absolute winding number from this stage. (4) The per-patch masked m7 for the unchanged VC3D seed-mode grower: a sparse local copy of 192^3 chunks with voxel-level zeroing outside the identity band; VC3D's reader zero-fills missing blocks, so the copy works. (5) Validation that stands: index continuity along the mesh computed from raw CT in the layering-normal direction; neighbour clearance in units of locally measured spacing with FUSED counted as fail; an unmasked far-side grow compared with the masked grow; a self-intersection test added outside the grower; and the owner's cross-section audit, now in xz and yz. (6) Compute for this surviving form, counted: index pass = 29 CT rows (34.2 GB uncompressed, bytes unavoidable) plus the m7 level-2 rows (size unverified), one CT row and one m7 row resident (about 2.6 GB uint8) plus float32 tiles, about 1.4-4e9 trilinear samples total (a few minutes of CPU per row on 4 cores), linking trivial, outputs under 1 GB; wall time is I/O-bound and unknown until one row is timed; split over the 8 containers it is about 4 rows each. Per patch: 220-290 m7 chunks (1.6-2 GB) read, a 100-300 MB sparse zarr, cache and render in /dev/shm, one 21-minute grow plus one 21-minute unmasked far-side grow, metrics under 10 min; a level-0 lamina-orientation count inside the band (1.2e9 voxels, 10-20 min) where the level-2 census says layers are fused. This fits 4 CPUs and about 7 GB of real headroom per container; the plan as written does not.
verdict.missing_validation: (a) Frame validation before any ray is cast: a per-voxel map of the angle between the proposed ray direction and the local structure-tensor normal at level 2; the index is claimed only where it is under 30 degrees, and the covered fraction of the target band is reported. (b) Separability census: fraction of the band (per chunk row) where consecutive laminae are resolved at level 2 (two peaks with a >= 1-voxel dip between them, before any smoothing); if it is below the proposal's own 90 % bar the identity field cannot come from level 2 there. (c) A timed read of one 128-slice chunk row of CT and one of m7 through the proxy, with the m7 level-2 .zarray (chunks, compressor, dtype) and the pyramid downsampling method recorded, since peak width at level 2 depends on it. (d) Re-cut i98 and the other ring1 patches in xz and yz through the mesh; the retrospective calibration target must be the owner's verdict in a plane normal to the layering, not the xy marks. (e) Independence test: index field from raw CT only versus from m7 only, agreement reported, and an explicit test of whether m7 itself bridges sheared open seams to the neighbouring lamina (trace m7 peaks across open seams in xz and compare with raw lamina continuity). (f) A mesh self-intersection/crossing test, since the grower has none in seed mode. (g) The fold false-termination and sheared-crack bridging bars run on the flattened-roll phantom with hairpins, fused sectors and sheared cracks, not on circular shells. (h) A measured disk and RAM budget per container at run time (free, df on /dev/shm and /) recorded with each run, because tmpfs and RAM are the same 15 GB and the orchestrator currently has 7 GB available and 1.1 GB of disk. (i) The 2 mm carry limit re-expressed in rays per the actual grid spacing and verified in the synthetic suite.

audit.strategy: Audit each of the six proposed data sources on three axes (does it exist and can this project download it; does its resolution/beamline/material match PHerc0268's deployment domain of 8.64 um, 116 keV, 1.2 m propagation, ESRF BM18, Paganin + unsharp, uint8 masked; which of the five failure modes it feeds), then rebuild the data plan around the only deployment-domain data that exists: the open-data bucket (PHerc0268 itself plus the other MAY-protocol volumes as same-beamline controls, the m7 surface-probability pyramid, normal grids, and the 'lasagna' product once its contents are checked). Public HF checkpoints are admitted only behind a measurable resolution-gap gate that uses existing paired 8.64 um / 2.2-2.4 um volumes (PHerc0009B, PHerc0343P, which have transform.json). The three sources that are vapour for this project (unreleased ESRF/Diamond raw volumes, physical carbonised replicas, En-Gedi bytes) are struck; parchment is struck entirely, including 'reference', because the owner's own toxic-data rule outranks the 'reference only' wording and citation of the 2016 paper needs no bytes. 'Perfect ground truth' is replaced by a seeded computational phantom family whose role is restricted to testing geometric code paths and robustness (never training a deployed model), with an explicit list of what it cannot validate. The umbilicus estimator is kept model-free (structure-tensor normal-convergence voting at pyramid level 3, piecewise-smooth axis with detected break-points, multi-centre handling) so that every claim about it is checkable on PHerc0268 itself by self-consistency, injection and cross-level tests, not by transfer from other scrolls. Every element gets a numeric bar; licence-gated items are run or recorded NOT RUN, never substituted.
audit.summary_of_method_as_specified: The owner's data plan feeds the master umbilicus model (U1 B-spline tube, U2 fibre-orientation tensor inversion, U3 inter-layer skeleton) and the master unrolling model (R1 optical-flow sheets, R2 nnUNet-like density segmentation, R3 constrained-curvature tracing) from six sources: (1) the Vesuvius open-data bucket (OME-zarr volumes, m7 surface probability, normal grids, lasagna) as the primary CT; (2) Vesuvius Hugging Face hub checkpoints (ink_9um, dinovol 3-D DINOv2, ink_3d_dino_guided, fiber models) as pretrained components; (3) the En-Gedi scroll (parchment, listed as 'reference only' while parchment/vellum is simultaneously declared toxic); (4) legacy EduceLab Scrolls 1-4 / Fragments 1-6 (Diamond Light Source I12, 2019-2023) as a cross-beamline control group; (5) unreleased ESRF/Diamond raw volumes as the corpus for 3-D masked-autoencoder pretraining; (6) synthetic carbonised papyrus replicas scanned as 'perfect ground truth' with known geometry. The implied validation is transfer: a model pretrained on (5), fine-tuned on (1)+(4), checked against (6), with (3) as a sanity reference, then deployed on PHerc0268 (level 0 = 14833 x 12145 x 12145 uint8, 2.2 TB; level 3 = 4.3 GB at 69 um; level 4 = 0.54 GB at 138 um) on 4 CPUs / 15 GB RAM / 1 GB disk / 11 GB volatile tmpfs with no GPU.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Every ground-truth source in the plan has smooth geometry: intact legacy rolls, the Paris 4 spiral fit (130 clean windings), and any replica or phantom built as a parametric spiral plus low-order deformation. A global B-spline tube (U1) tuned and validated on them is rewarded for smoothness and for 'bridging from the clean top and bottom'. On a crushed core the true origin of the windings is not one smooth curve: it jumps at shear planes and splits where the core folded on itself, so the bridged axis lands where no sheet converges. The failure is invisible to any metric computed on the training/validation library because that library contains no such jumps.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: The existing 19 'axis_points' (tools/fl4/fl4.py, level-4 mask centroid at z fractions 0.05-0.95) were fed as-is into seeding at radial fractions 0.15-0.35 of the mask radius. A B-spline through them smooths any lateral jump of the core across the crushed middle band; rays from the smoothed axis then cross sheets at grazing angles, seeds land one to three windings off, and winding numbers assigned by ray-crossing count are wrong by 1-3 in the core. That is exactly the cross-winding 'collage' the xsec README documented on PHerc0268 (a surface that passed every numeric gate, radial |cos| 0.928, yet jumped layers at each crack). No validation of the 19 points exists; a global smooth fit would hide rather than expose the jump.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: En-Gedi is parchment (collagen; isotropic density, no fibre anisotropy, no laminated air gaps), with radio-dense metal-bearing ink that is bright in CT, scanned uncarbonised... as a charred lump on a lab micro-CT at roughly 18 um (Seales et al. 2016). Any threshold, prior, texture statistic or learned weight that touches it learns 'sheet = uniform slab, ink = bright, gap = air'. Physical carbonised replicas (if they existed) are modern papyrus charred in a furnace for hours: different shrinkage, brittleness and crush pattern from pyroclastic burial plus two millennia of compaction, and none would reproduce an ash-infilled core. Legacy intact rolls have different rolling/collapse mechanics. The 'reference only' status does not neutralise this: references set expectations and thresholds.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: A sheet-vs-gap prior from En-Gedi or replicas expects air between windings. PHerc0268's core has ash-filled gaps at papyrus-like density: the project measured 'fraction of surface points on predicted papyrus' = 0.676 for a correct surface and 0.676 for a layer-jumped one (packages/xsec/README.md), i.e. m7 puts papyrus everywhere in the core. A density-transition prior sees one thick slab where there are five windings; a layer-counting axis estimator sees zero layers and falls back to the hull centroid; a bright-ink prior from En-Gedi fires on mineral inclusions.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Three scale mismatches. (a) Every public HF checkpoint is 2.2-2.4 um (dinovol ps8/ps6, ink_3d_dino_guided, fiber_dinoguided, the 20260417190342 ink maps); PHerc0268 is 8.64 um, a 3.6x gap. dinovol's 8^3 token spans 19 um at 2.4 um but 69 um at 8.64 um (half a sheet instead of a tenth); its 128^3 global crop holds about two windings at 2.4 um and about seven at 8.64 um, so the pretrained features were learned at the wrong semantic scale. (b) Legacy DLS volumes are 7.91 um at 53-88 keV with different propagation and phase retrieval: similar voxel pitch, different contrast physics. (c) Inside our own pipeline: level 4 (138 um) aliases the winding pitch (0.3-0.6 mm = 2.2-4.3 voxels), so any orientation field computed at level 4 to save memory is noise; and at 8.64 um individual fibres are at the resolution limit, so U2's dense 'fibre-orientation tensor field' is not measurable at all on this volume. Only the sheet-normal (layering) field at levels 2-3 is.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: U2 run on PHerc0268 level 0 would return sheet-edge orientation plus noise and call it fibre orientation; projecting those 'fibre normals' backwards gives a convergence point dominated by the strongest edges (the outer mask boundary and the brightest crushed slab), not the winding origin. The organizers' fiber model outputs exist only at 2.4 um on other scrolls (Paris4, 1451, 0332, 1299, 0139); none exist on PHerc0268. A dinovol feature map applied at 8.64 um without the gate in metric 8 would be used with no evidence it means the same thing.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Phantoms and replicas supply clean air gaps and uniform density transitions, so an estimator validated on them is allowed to depend on sheet/gap contrast. PHerc0268's real volume adds: ash-filled gaps, mineral inclusions (bright compact blobs with sharp edges that dominate any gradient-based vote locally), ring artefacts centred on the sample-stage rotation axis (which is NOT the scroll axis), the organizer mask boundary (a hard zero edge in 'masked.zarr'), Paganin smoothing with an unsharp-mask halo (4.0/1.2) at every boundary, and uint8 quantisation. The most seductive wrong answer for any radial-convergence or Hough-type umbilicus estimator is the ring-artefact centre: it is perfectly consistent across all z.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: (a) A normal-convergence vote at level 3 picks up the concentric ring artefacts and returns the reconstruction centre as a razor-sharp, z-invariant 'umbilicus' that disagrees with the mask centroid by millimetres; without metric 6 nothing distinguishes it from a real axis. (b) The fl4 centroid uses nonzero voxels of the masked volume: if the organizer mask is a cylinder around the sample rather than the scroll outline, the 19 axis_points are the field-of-view centre, not the scroll; the stored n_mask_l4 counts already in the seeds JSON reveal this (near-constant across z = cylinder mask) and have never been checked. (c) A 10-voxel bright inclusion at level 3 outweighs a 0.3-mm-pitch layering signal in a 4-voxel structure-tensor window.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Any learned component in the plan (nnUNet-like R2, MAE/DINO features, or a phantom-trained axis regressor) sees a tiny library of macro shapes: legacy Scrolls 1-4, Paris 4, the MAY-protocol set (0009B and 0343P fragments, 1451, 0800, 1447) and phantoms whose collapse is OUR invention. It learns those shapes. Worse: iterating the phantom generator until the method passes installs our own deformation prior as ground truth (validation by construction), and no metric computed on that library can detect it. PHerc0268's crush is one of a kind.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: An axis network trained on near-circular cross-sections (every intact roll and every smooth phantom) outputs the convex-hull centroid. PHerc0268's core is folded with sheets on one side flattened against the other, so the true winding origin sits millimetres off the hull centroid; the network is confidently wrong, its training-set error is tiny, and the error only surfaces downstream as unrolled text that is a collage. The same applies to a phantom family tuned to 'look like 0268 at level 4': it encodes what we already believe about the collapse and can only confirm it.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Outside the five, but decisive: accessibility. Three of the six sources do not exist as downloadable data for this project. 'Unreleased ESRF/Diamond raw volumes' are by definition not public, no beamline agreement exists, raw projections would need GPU reconstruction, and the 3-D MAE pretraining they were meant to feed cannot run on 4 CPUs (dinovol's pretraining was a multi-GPU run over ten 2.4 um scrolls). 'Synthetic carbonised papyrus replica' CT scans exist in no public bucket or HF dataset and the project has no lab or beamline to make them. En-Gedi is not in the open-data bucket, its public availability is unverified here, and it is forbidden by the owner's own rule anyway. The plan's pretraining stage and its 'perfect ground truth' stage therefore silently have no input.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: As written, the umbilicus model for PHerc0268 would wait on a pretraining corpus and a ground-truth set that will never arrive, while the only data that can validate anything on 0268 (the volume itself, 4.3 GB at level 3, streamable chunk-by-chunk; 0.54 GB at level 4) sits unused. The 1 GB free disk and the restart-wiped 11 GB tmpfs also forbid local copies of any second volume, so every 'control group' must be streamed at level 3/4 and every phantom regenerated from a seed, not stored.

hidden_failure_modes.mechanism: Outside the five: licence and provenance contamination. The legacy EduceLab data (DLS volumes at data.aws.ash2txt.org / dl.ash2txt.org, title-search meshes) is under the EduceLab Data License with citation, non-commercial and publication-reservation terms; the project accepted it for five meshes for internal use only (RULES.md OWNER-LICENSE-EDUCELAB-1; logs/pp/CITATION_RULES.md forbids including them or derivatives). Community umbilicus/mesh files for legacy scrolls are untrusted inputs and any community parser is code that must be audited line by line.
hidden_failure_modes.concrete_pherc0268_scenario: If a legacy-trained or legacy-validated component sits anywhere in the PHerc0268 submission chain, the First Letters package must disclose and cite it and must not contain derived geometry; a fresh licence acceptance scoped to the specific legacy volume is needed before any download, and the organizer umbilicus file for a legacy scroll must be parsed by our own code, not the community tool that produced it.

audit.hardened_alternative:
DATA PLAN v2 (what enters, in what role, with what gate).
A. Deployment-domain data, the only data any deployed component may be fitted on: PHerc0268 volume 20251110183117 (MAY protocol: 8.64 um, 116 keV, 1.2 m, ESRF BM18), streamed chunk-wise from S3. Level 4 (928 x 760 x 760, 0.54 GB) held in /dev/shm and regenerated after any restart; level 3 (1855 x 1519 x 1519, 4.3 GB) processed in z-slabs of 64 slices (148 MB uint8 each), never cached whole; level 2 (34 GB) only as a few 64-slice slabs for verification; level 0 only as sparse 64^3 cubes. Organizer products on the same pyramid: m7 surface probability, normal grids, and 'lasagna' once its contents are confirmed (if it encodes radial direction or layer ordering it becomes a fourth independent estimator and a validation target, audited before use, never trusted alone).
B. Same-protocol controls (no training, robustness only): level-3/4 streams of two or three other MAY-protocol volumes (PHerc1451 20250521151225, PHerc0800, PHerc1447) and one or two JULY-protocol volumes (0841, 0139 at 9.362 um / 113 keV). They show the estimator is not tuned to 0268 or to phantoms.
C. Public HF checkpoints (scrollprize/ink_9um base, dinovol_v2_ps8_with_paris4_352500, fiber_dinoguided, ink_3d_dino_guided): MIT, public, already sha-verified for ink_9um. None drives the umbilicus. Any use at 8.64 um must first pass the resolution-gap gate (metric 8) on PHerc0009B and PHerc0343P, which carry both an 8.64 um and a 2.2-2.4 um volume with transform.json. Checkpoints trained only at 2.4 um that fail the gate are not used on 0268 at all, and never upsampled 0268 data to fake 2.4 um (that triples the voxel count with no new information).
D. Computational phantom family (replaces 'perfect ground truth replicas'): deterministic, seeded, generated on the fly at level-4 scale (760^3, 0.44 GB), level-3 scale (512^3 sub-volumes) and small level-0 cubes (256^3, 2.2 mm). Generator: parametric spiral sheet, pitch 0.3-0.6 mm, thickness 100-200 um, gap fraction 0-100 % filled with ash-density material; deformations applied as a displacement field that is piecewise smooth with explicit discontinuities: global elliptical squash (axis ratio 0.3-1.0), collapsed-core piecewise-affine crush, delamination (sheet split into two half-thickness sheets with a wedge), sharp buckles (fold angles to 150 degrees, radius of curvature down to 1 sheet thickness), shear bands (displacement jumps of 0.5-3 mm across a plane), floating detached arcs, two-centre phantoms (two winding origins 3-10 mm apart over a z-range, for U3); contaminants: bright spheres and filaments 2-10 voxels at the 99.9th-percentile intensity; artefacts: concentric ring artefacts centred OFF the scroll axis by 2-8 mm, Gaussian PSF (sigma 0.7 voxel at level 3) plus an unsharp halo, uint8 quantisation, a hard zero mask (both tight-outline and cylinder variants). Ground-truth axis per z = the spiral origin mapped through the displacement field; ground-truth break-points = the shear planes; ground-truth winding number per voxel = the spiral parameter. Role: unit and regression tests of the geometry code (axis conventions zyx vs xyz, pyramid scaling and the +8 half-voxel offsets in fl4.py, break-point detection, multi-centre association) and robustness sweeps. Explicit non-roles: the phantom never trains a deployed model, never tunes a threshold used on 0268 unless that threshold is then re-verified by a 0268 self-consistency metric, and the generator's parameters are frozen and hashed before the estimator is run on 0268 (METRIC-HASH style) so the phantom cannot be iterated into agreement. What it cannot validate, stated in the record: realism of 8.64 um phase-contrast texture of carbonised papyrus, true ink/papyrus contrast, the real collapse mechanics of 0268, real scanner artefacts, and the real sheet count/pitch; therefore phantom pass rates are evidence about code and robustness only, never about performance on 0268.
E. Legacy EduceLab DLS data: optional, numeric-only cross-beamline control of the macro-scale estimator (metric 9) on one 7.91 um legacy scroll that has an organizer-published umbilicus file (Scroll 1 / PHerc.Paris.3 is the candidate; verify by listing). Requires a fresh licence acceptance scoped to that one volume, our own parser for the umbilicus file, no bytes into any model, no derivative in any submission. If the licence scope is not granted, the metric is recorded NOT RUN; B already covers cross-scroll robustness in-domain.
F. Struck: En-Gedi bytes in any role (citation of Seales et al. 2016 is allowed, data is not); unreleased ESRF/Diamond raw volumes; 3-D MAE pretraining (no data, no GPU; dinovol already occupies that niche at 2.4 um and goes through gate C); physical replicas as ground truth; any parchment or vellum; any pooling of MAY, JULY, 2.4 um and DLS volumes as one domain for a fine-scale model without per-protocol stratification.

UMBILICUS ESTIMATOR built on this data (model-free, so that the data plan above suffices to validate it).
Level 4 (138 um): initialisation only. Mask centroid per slice (existing fl4 code) kept as estimator E1 after the mask-tightness check (metric 6b); convex hull and outer radius per azimuth. No orientation field at level 4 (pitch aliases at 2.2-4.3 voxels).
Level 3 (69 um; pitch 4.3-8.7 voxels; sheet 1.4-2.9 voxels): per slice, 2-D structure tensor with derivative Gaussian sigma_d = 1.0 voxel and integration sigma_i = 4 voxels (about one pitch), computed only inside the mask eroded by 3 voxels (removes the mask-edge gradient). Coherence c = (l1-l2)/(l1+l2); pixels with c > 0.5 cast a line vote along their eigenvector normal (the sheet normal) into an accumulator at level-3 resolution, weight c, limited to a length of 0.6 R (so votes from the outer windings do not cross the whole slice). Accumulator smoothed with Gaussian sigma 2 voxels; the peak is estimator E2 with confidence q = peak / second-peak after non-maximum suppression at 1 mm. Estimator E3: the same vote cast by the m7 surface normals (from the normal grids or the gradient of m7 at level 3) restricted to m7 > 0.5; E4 = lasagna-derived direction, if confirmed. Artefact guard: the ring-artefact centre is estimated once per 100 slices by the same vote restricted to the zeroed periphery and low-coherence background, and any estimator peak within 2 level-3 voxels of it over more than 50 % of z with q < 1.5 is discarded as artefact-locked (metric 6a). Per-slice fusion: geometric median (Weiszfeld) of the available estimators, weighted by q and by their pairwise agreement; per-slice uncertainty u(z) = the pairwise spread.
Along z: no single global spline. Fit the axis with a Huber-loss smoothing spline (knots every 2 mm = 29 level-3 slices) and run a change-point detector (PELT, L2 cost on the residuals, penalty frozen from the phantom sweep) to find shear planes; each detected break starts a new spline segment with a free offset, so the axis is piecewise smooth and the break list is a reported output. Bridging across a low-confidence band (q < 1.3 or u > 1 mm over more than 20 slices) is done by extrapolating the two adjacent segments towards each other; the band is marked INTERPOLATED and carries an uncertainty equal to the max leave-band-out residual (metric 4); seeds and winding numbers inside an INTERPOLATED band are never used for text claims.
Multi-centre (U3 without inter-layer skeletonisation, which has nothing to skeletonise in an ash-filled core): when the accumulator shows k >= 2 peaks with second/first > 0.6 over > 20 consecutive slices, the band is declared multi-core; up to three centres are tracked across slices by nearest-neighbour association (max step 0.5 mm per slice), each becomes a local origin for the downstream unrolling, and the band's global winding numbers are suspended.
Verification at level 2 and level 0: on 10 level-2 slabs the vote is repeated (sigma_i = 8) for metric 2; on a few hundred 64^3 level-0 cubes near the core the 3-D structure tensor's smallest-eigenvalue direction (sheet normal) is compared with the radial direction from the fused axis, as a check that the axis explains the fine-scale layering, never as an estimator (the fibre field itself is below the resolution limit at 8.64 um).

validation_metrics.name: PHANTOM-AXIS-ERR (code and robustness, not 0268 performance)
validation_metrics.definition: On the frozen, seeded phantom family (known axis, known shear planes, known winding numbers), the per-z Euclidean distance between the estimated and true axis, reported as median and 95th percentile in mm, per phantom class (crush 0.3-1.0, delamination, buckles, shear jumps, floating fragments, ash fill 0-100 %, contaminants, off-centre ring artefacts, cylinder vs tight mask, two-centre). Also break-point recall/precision and winding-number accuracy along rays.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Median <= 0.14 mm (2 level-3 voxels) and p95 <= 0.30 mm (below half the smallest pitch) in every class; every true shear plane detected within +-5 slices with <= 1 false break per 500 slices; two-centre phantoms: both centres recovered within 0.3 mm over >= 90 % of their z-range; winding number correct for >= 98 % of voxels outside INTERPOLATED bands. Any class failing blocks use of that code path on 0268.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Ground truth exists by construction; the phantom generator parameters and seed list are hashed before any 0268 run so the family cannot be adjusted after the fact. Pass here means the implementation is correct and robust, and is recorded as such; it is never cited as evidence about PHerc0268.

validation_metrics.name: CROSS-LEVEL-CONSISTENCY
validation_metrics.definition: Axis estimated independently at level 3 (full) and at level 2 (10 slabs of 64 slices spread over z), initialised from level 4; distance per slice after scaling to a common frame.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Median <= 1 level-3 voxel (69 um), p95 <= 3 voxels (0.21 mm) over the level-2 slabs; failure means the estimator is resolution-dependent (failure mode 3) and is not used.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Self-consistency on PHerc0268 itself: two scales of the same volume must agree on the same physical point; no labels needed.

validation_metrics.name: ESTIMATOR-AGREEMENT
validation_metrics.definition: Per-slice pairwise distances between the independent estimators E1 (mask centroid), E2 (structure-tensor normal-convergence vote), E3 (m7 normal convergence) and E4 (lasagna, if confirmed), and the resulting per-slice spread u(z).
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: In the clean top and bottom bands: median pairwise distance <= 0.3 mm. In the crushed band: u(z) is reported as the uncertainty envelope; a band with u > 1 mm is marked multi-core or unresolved, never silently bridged; the fused axis is 'usable' only where u <= 0.5 mm.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Agreement of estimators that rely on different signals (mask geometry, CT layering orientation, organizer surface model) on the same slice of PHerc0268; disagreement is itself the measurement.

validation_metrics.name: LEAVE-BAND-OUT
validation_metrics.definition: Hold out each 10 % z-band in turn, refit the piecewise axis (with break detection) from the remaining 90 %, and measure the residual between the predicted axis in the held-out band and the directly estimated axis there.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Median residual <= 0.3 mm in clean bands; for a band to be bridged (INTERPOLATED) its predicted-vs-direct residual must be below half the local pitch (<= 0.15-0.3 mm), otherwise the band is handled by local centres only. The residual observed is stored as that band's bridging uncertainty.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Predictive self-consistency on PHerc0268: it tests exactly the owner's 'bridge from clean top and bottom' operation against what the data in the middle say.

validation_metrics.name: RAY-ISOTROPY and OPTIMUM SHARPNESS
validation_metrics.definition: From the estimated axis, per clean slice, cast 36 rays and count m7 sheet crossings per mm along each; coefficient of variation across azimuth. Separately, the median |cos| between m7 surface normals and the radial direction, evaluated at the estimate and at the estimate displaced by +-0.5, +-1, +-2 mm in x and y.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: CV of crossings per mm <= 0.25 in clean bands; |cos| peaks at the estimate with a margin >= 0.05 over the 1 mm displacements (a flat optimum means the axis is unconstrained there and the slice is marked low-confidence). Note: this metric validates the axis, not sheet continuity; the xsec work showed radial |cos| is blind to layer jumps.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: A wrong axis makes winding density asymmetric in azimuth and lowers radial alignment; both are computed from m7 and the normal grids on PHerc0268 alone.

validation_metrics.name: ARTEFACT-CENTRE and MASK checks
validation_metrics.definition: (a) Ring-artefact centre estimated once per 100 slices from the periphery/background vote; distance from the fused axis per slice, and the fraction of z where they coincide within 2 level-3 voxels. (b) Coefficient of variation across z of the nonzero-mask voxel count (n_mask_l4, already stored in the fl4 seeds JSON) and of the mask's per-slice bounding box.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: (a) If the axis coincides with the artefact centre over > 50 % of z while ESTIMATOR-AGREEMENT is poor (median > 0.5 mm), the estimate is rejected as artefact-locked. (b) CV(n_mask_l4) > 0.05 and a per-slice bounding box that varies with z confirm a tight outline mask and admit E1; otherwise E1 is excluded and the 19 historical axis_points are declared VOID as an axis.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Both are properties of the PHerc0268 volume itself (reconstruction geometry and organizer mask), read from the existing level-4 data and the fl4 JSON; no labels.

validation_metrics.name: CONTAMINANT-INJECTION on real slices
validation_metrics.definition: Into real PHerc0268 level-3 slices add 50 bright blobs (3-10 voxels, intensity at the slice's 99.9th percentile) and 5 bright filaments per slice at random positions, re-run the per-slice estimators, and measure the axis shift versus the uninjected run.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Median shift <= 1 level-3 voxel (69 um), p95 <= 2 voxels, for every estimator that remains in the fusion; an estimator exceeding this is down-weighted or removed.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Real texture plus synthetic anomalies; the uninjected estimate is the reference, so only stability is measured, which is what failure mode 4 is about. Bridges the phantom-to-real gap for artefact robustness without needing realistic phantom texture.

validation_metrics.name: CHECKPOINT-RESOLUTION-GAP gate (before any HF checkpoint touches 0268)
validation_metrics.definition: On PHerc0009B (8.64 um 20250521125136 vs 2.401 um 20250820154339/20260319104112) and PHerc0343P (8.64 um 20250521134555 vs 2.215 um 20260304131111), both with transform.json, run the checkpoint at its native resolution and on the 8.64 um volume over the same physical regions (4 regions of about 2 mm cube); after registration compare outputs: Pearson r of continuous maps (cosine-to-prototype, first PC of patch features) or Dice of binarised maps.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: r >= 0.7 or Dice >= 0.6 on >= 3 of 4 regions per scroll; otherwise the checkpoint is not used at 8.64 um in any role, and no upsampling workaround is tried.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: The checkpoint's own native-resolution output is the reference; the test asks only whether it means the same thing at 8.64 um. Uses organizer registration files already in the bucket; no manual labels.

validation_metrics.name: SAME-PROTOCOL SCROLL CONTROLS
validation_metrics.definition: Run the full estimator at level 3 on 2-3 other MAY-protocol volumes (PHerc1451, PHerc0800, PHerc1447) and 1-2 JULY volumes (PHerc0841, PHerc0139); apply CROSS-LEVEL-CONSISTENCY, ESTIMATOR-AGREEMENT and RAY-ISOTROPY on their clean bands.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: All three metrics pass on every control volume's clean bands with the same frozen parameters used on 0268; a parameter that must change per scroll is evidence of tuning (failure mode 5) and is recorded as such.
validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: Same self-consistency metrics on other real scrolls at the same beamline and voxel size; streamed at level 3/4, nothing stored.

validation_metrics.name: CROSS-BEAMLINE CONTROL (optional, licence-gated)
validation_metrics.definition: On one legacy DLS 7.91 um scroll with an organizer-published umbilicus file (candidate: Scroll 1 / PHerc.Paris.3; verify by listing), run the macro-scale estimator at the equivalent 63-70 um level and compare per-slice to the organizer axis, parsed by our own code.
validation_metrics.pass_threshold: Median <= 2 voxels (about 0.16 mm), p95 <= 4 voxels. If the licence scope is not granted, the metric is recorded NOT RUN; it is never replaced by a community-derived substitute and no legacy bytes enter any model.
