validation_metrics.how_computed_without_ground_truth: The organizer file is treated as data (a reference axis), not as training input; it tests beamline invariance of a model-free estimator at a scale where beamline differences wash out.

audit.compute_estimate: Streaming: level 4 of PHerc0268 (0.54 GB) once per container life into /dev/shm; level 3 (4.3 GB) streamed as 64-slice slabs, about 5-20 min of S3 transfer, never persisted (1 GB disk). Per-slice 2-D structure tensor + line vote at level 3 (1519^2): about 0.5-1 s per slice with numpy/scipy on 4 cores, 1855 slices = 15-30 min; m7 and normal-grid votes similar, so the three estimators plus fusion and change-point detection take under 1.5 h. Level-2 verification on 10 slabs of 64 slices (3037^2): about 10 min. Phantom family: 30 seeded phantoms at 760^3 generated and evaluated in 1-2 min each (about 1 h), plus 20 at 512^3 level-3 scale and 10 at 256^3 level-0 scale (about 20 min). Contaminant injection on real slices: 30 min. Same-protocol controls: 3-5 volumes at level 3, 30-60 min each including transfer, run on sibling containers in parallel. Checkpoint resolution-gap gate: dinovol ps8 (216 M parameters) forward on a 128^3 crop on 4 CPUs about 10-30 s; 4 regions x 2 scrolls x 2 resolutions x a few crops = under 1 h; ink_9um tiles are faster. Leave-band-out: 10 refits of a spline on 1855 points, seconds. Peak RAM under 3 GB (one 148 MB slab plus float32 tensors of 6 x 1519^2 x 4 B = 55 MB per slice; level 4 resident 0.54 GB). Persistent outputs: JSON axis files with break list and per-slice uncertainty (under 1 MB) and PNG diagnostics. Total for the umbilicus and its full validation: about 4-6 CPU-hours on the orchestrator, or 1-2 wall-hours with the seven siblings. Not feasible and struck: 3-D MAE pretraining (even a 10 M-parameter toy at 64^3 would need days on 4 CPUs and is far below the public dinovol), nnUNet-style 3-D training, any dense level-0 tensor field (2.2 TB input).
audit.what_to_reject_outright: 1. En-Gedi in any computational role, including 'reference only': parchment (collagen, no fibre anisotropy, no laminated gaps), radio-dense metal-bearing ink, lab micro-CT at about 18 um, not carbonised; the owner's toxic-data rule outranks the reference wording; the 2016 paper may be cited, its bytes may not be used, and its public availability is unverified here anyway. 2. 'Unreleased ESRF/Diamond raw volumes' as a pretraining corpus: not accessible to this project by definition, raw projections would need GPU reconstruction, and the 3-D MAE pretraining they would feed cannot run on 4 CPUs; the public dinovol checkpoints already fill that niche at 2.4 um and must pass the resolution-gap gate before any use. 3. Physical 'synthetic carbonised papyrus replicas' as perfect ground truth: no public scans exist, the project cannot make or scan them, and even a physical replica is not ground truth for geometry unless scanned before and after collapse; furnace-charred modern papyrus does not reproduce an ash-infilled 2000-year-old crush. 4. Legacy EduceLab DLS data as training data for any PHerc0268 model: different beamline, energies (53-88 keV), contrast physics and collapse state, under a licence the project accepted for internal use of five meshes only; admitted solely as an optional, licence-gated, numeric-only cross-beamline control of the model-free macro estimator with our own parser. 5. Any HF checkpoint applied at 8.64 um without the resolution-gap gate, and any upsampling of PHerc0268 to fake 2.4 um. 6. Any learned axis estimator (regressor, nnUNet-like, MAE-feature) trained on the small scroll library or on phantoms: it memorises macro shapes and cannot be validated on 0268. 7. Phantom results cited as evidence of performance on PHerc0268, and any adjustment of the phantom generator after the estimator has run on 0268. 8. A single global B-spline tube with silent bridging across the crushed band: the axis must be piecewise smooth with reported break-points, uncertainty per slice, and INTERPOLATED bands excluded from text claims. 9. Pooling MAY, JULY, 2.4 um and DLS volumes as one training domain for any fine-scale model without per-protocol stratification. 10. The existing 19 level-4 centroid axis_points as an axis until the mask-tightness check and the estimator-agreement metric have been run on them.

refuted_claims.claim: The estimator is built on per-xy-slice 2-D structure tensors, a per-z mask centroid (E1), a line-vote accumulator per xy slice, a Huber spline plus PELT along z, leave-10%-z-band-out, and 'bridging from the clean top and bottom' in z. The axis is assumed to run roughly along the volume z axis.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The repo's own frame inspection (logs/umb/UMB-GEOMETRY-RESULT.md, images logs/umb/L4_xy_z464.png, L3_xz_centre.png, L3_yz_full.png) shows PHerc0268 is a roll crushed flat with its former roll axis along the volume y axis: xy sections show one sheet face-on (strip cross-hatch and in-sheet cracks over a round 82 x 68 mm outline), xz sections show strata stacked along z closing in hairpins at the x extremes, and the level-4 3-D structure tensor gives |n_z| median 0.76 with 45 % of coherent voxels above 0.8. The stored fl4 axis JSON confirms it independently: n_mask_l4 per z-slice runs 32k -> 270k -> 32k as a chord-area profile of an object lying across z, and the centroid y drifts 45 mm over z. A 2-D structure tensor in an xy slice measures in-sheet texture, not layering, so the vote has no winding signal; the project's own xy-frame run of the same idea (logs/umb/PHerc0268_xy_discarded/st_axis.log, 27 slabs) returned confidence 0.0 on every slab with median normal-line residuals of 6-14 mm and conditioning 0.03-0.2. Every z-indexed element (E1 per z, spline/PELT/leave-band-out along z, 'top and bottom' bands) is in the wrong frame; the y-extremes are the roll's slanted end faces, not clean windings.
refuted_claims.fix: Add a frame step before any 2-D slicing: at level 4, 3-D structure tensor over coherent voxels, roll-axis direction a = eigenvector of the smallest eigenvalue of sum(c n n^T); bar: smallest/middle eigenvalue <= 0.5 and a within 15 degrees of a volume axis (else re-slice along a). For 0268 the sections are xz planes indexed by y (1519 level-3 sections); every along-axis operation (spline, change points, leave-band-out, 'clean' bands, bridging envelopes) is indexed by y. The 19 axis_points are VOID because of the frame, not because of mask tightness (tools/umb/st_axis.py --axis y already does the re-slicing).

refuted_claims.claim: E2: coherent pixels cast line votes along the sheet normal into a 2-D accumulator; the peak is the axis, q = peak/second-peak after non-maximum suppression at 1 mm; k >= 2 peaks with second/first > 0.6 over > 20 slices declares the band multi-core and tracks up to three centres.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: In a flattened stack the flat-face normals are parallel (along z), so their vote lines never concur: they lay a ridge across the whole section, the 'peak' is wherever the densest flat packet happens to be, and q is meaningless on a ridge. The only voters that carry origin information are the hairpins at the x extremes, whose normal lines converge on two foci (the ends of a slit), not one point; the proposal's rule would classify every section of a single flattened roll as 'multi-core' with two or three centres and suspend winding numbers everywhere. The first four xz slabs of the live y-frame run (logs/umb/PHerc0268/slabs.json) already show the ill-conditioning the point model suffers: conditioning 0.02, admissible fraction 0.13-0.14, residual 6.5-14 mm (end-face slabs, so not yet conclusive for the interior).
refuted_claims.fix: Per xz section fit a slit (two foci F1, F2, half-length c, orientation phi) as the primary model, with the point model as the c < 0.5 mm special case (as DECL-UMB-1-A1 already states): hairpin voters (|n_x| > 0.7 in the slit frame) vote for the foci by robust line concurrency; flat-face voters determine phi and the stacking direction only. 'Multi-slit' is declared only when hairpin residual clusters > 1 mm from both foci exceed 10 % of voters, never from the number of accumulator peaks. The radial coordinate for unrolling is distance to the slit segment, not to a point.

refuted_claims.claim: Artefact guard: the ring-artefact centre is estimated per 100 slices from the periphery/background vote and an axis within 2 voxels of it over > 50 % of z is rejected (metric 6a); the existing polar high-pass about the image centre removes rings.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Ring artefacts are circles about the rotation axis (parallel to z) in xy planes. In the xz sections that the correct frame requires they are not rings at all: a detector-column defect produces z-invariant vertical stripes at x = x_rot +- sqrt(r^2 - (y - y_rot)^2). A structure tensor with sigma_i 4-5 sees each stripe as a coherent edge with normal along +-x, i.e. exactly the signature of a hairpin voter, so stripes vote for spurious foci on the x axis; the 'ring centre' concept and a polar high-pass about the xz image centre (which the live run still applies: slabs.json carries image_centre [759, 927] and polar_fallbacks) address an artefact that does not exist in that plane. The debris exclusion (p99.5) does not catch stripes because they are low contrast.
refuted_claims.fix: In xz sections remove the z-stationary component per column: subtract from each column its median over z inside the mask (genuine hairpin/layer signal alternates along z and survives). Decoy test: the stripe map (columns whose z-median deviation exceeds 3 MAD) is turned into votes on its own; any focus within 1 mm of a stripe-only focus is rejected. Phantom stripes must be vertical x-stripes in xz, not off-centre rings.

refuted_claims.claim: Mask erosion of 3 level-3 voxels after sigma_d = 1 and sigma_i = 4 'removes the mask-edge gradient'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The organizer mask is a hard 0 -> ~150 grey-level edge; layering contrast at level 3 is of order 20-40 grey levels. With Gaussian integration sigma_i = 4 the edge's squared-gradient contribution at distance d is ~150^2 exp(-d^2/32) and equals the layering's ~30^2 at d ~ 10 voxels; at 3 voxels the edge outweighs the layering by ~20x, so the outermost 0.7 mm of every section votes with the mask outline's normal (which in a flattened stack is along +-x at the sides, again mimicking hairpins). The current code uses erode 14 (1.0 mm) for this reason.
refuted_claims.fix: Erode by at least 2.5 sigma_i (>= 10-12 voxels at sigma_i 4-5, i.e. 0.7-0.8 mm), and verify on a phantom with the tight-outline mask that the fraction of admissible voters within 1 mm of the mask edge is < 1 %.

refuted_claims.claim: E1 (mask centroid), E2 (structure-tensor vote), E3 (m7 normal convergence) and E4 (lasagna direction) are independent estimators whose per-slice agreement (Weiszfeld median, spread u(z)) is a measurement.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: E2, E3 and E4 are all functions of the same CT gradient field: E3 is the gradient of an nnUNet surface map computed from the CT, and the lasagna (bucket-verified: PHerc0268.lasagna.json version 2, groups cos at level 1 and grad_mag/nx/ny at level 2, umbilicus_json empty) is an in-plane xy normal field with gradient magnitude, computed with no umbilicus under a z-axis assumption. It has no nz channel: for 0268, whose normals are mostly along z, nx/ny are the normalised remainder of a nearly vertical vector and the xz in-plane direction (nx, +-nz) cannot even be recovered up to sign without a decode audit of the uint8 encoding. m7 is additionally useless in the core (packages/xsec/README.md: 0.676 'papyrus' fraction for a correct and a layer-jumped surface alike). Agreement among E2/E3/E4 therefore reproduces a shared artefact (a stripe, a crack, the mask edge) with high 'confidence'. E1 measures the hull centre of a flattened stack, which is not the slit. The proposal also exempts m7 and lasagna from its own resolution-gap gate (rule C) without stating why.
refuted_claims.fix: Treat m7 and lasagna as reported cross-checks (DECL-UMB-1 M6 style: angle statistics, 'not computable' when nz cannot be decoded), never as fusion members; the only independent noise estimate is split-half (odd/even sections) of the same estimator; the only independent decoy references are the mask centroid, the image centre and the stripe foci. Decode the lasagna encoding from the organizers' code under line-by-line audit before any use.

refuted_claims.claim: RAY-ISOTROPY: from the axis cast 36 rays per clean slice, count m7 crossings per mm, CV <= 0.25 passes; |cos| between m7 normals and the radial direction must peak at the estimate.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: For a flattened roll a correct slit gives strongly anisotropic crossing densities by construction: vertical rays cross ~2N sheets across the 90 mm stack while rays along the slit cross only hairpins beyond the slit ends; the CV of a correct answer exceeds 0.25, so the metric fails the truth and favours a wrong round-roll answer. The radial |cos| test is already documented as blind to layer jumps (xsec README) and, in a stack, is maximised by any point on the stacking axis.
refuted_claims.fix: Use the flattened-geometry balance already declared as M5b: vertical rays up and down from 5 points along the slit, |N_up - N_down| <= 1 on >= 80 % of points and max-min of (N_up + N_down) <= 2 (each closed loop crosses a vertical line through the slit exactly twice); count crossings on the CT at level 1-2 along the local stacking direction, not on m7.

refuted_claims.claim: Metric 6b: CV(n_mask_l4) > 0.05 with a z-varying bounding box 'confirms a tight outline mask and admits E1'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: From the stored JSON (logs/fl4/axis_PHerc0268.json) CV(n_mask_l4) = 0.45, so the metric passes, but the variation is the chord-area profile of a roll lying across z (and includes an outlier point at z = 14096 whose centroid, x 10762 / y 1374, sits in a volume corner). The metric cannot distinguish 'tight mask' from 'wrong frame' and would admit an estimator that the frame test voids.
refuted_claims.fix: Replace by the frame test above plus, in the correct sections, a mask-vs-hull check (mask area / convex-hull area per xz section, and the fraction of mask-edge voxels adjacent to nonzero CT). E1 survives only as a decoy reference.

refuted_claims.claim: No orientation field at level 4 because the pitch (0.3-0.6 mm = 2.2-4.3 voxels) aliases; U2 is 'not measurable at all' on this volume; U3 has 'nothing to skeletonise in an ash-filled core'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: 2.2-4.3 voxels per period is above Nyquist, and on 0268 the structure that is actually visible at levels 3-4 is packet-scale layering (1-3 mm bands) plus wide open cracks, not single windings: the project's level-4 3-D structure tensor (1.8 M coherent voxels) is what produced the frame result. Individual winding gaps are mostly below 70 um or ash-filled and are the thing that is invisible at level 3, which means the level-3 vote measures the stacking direction, not the pitch, and winding numbers cannot come from level 3 at all. The face-on cross-hatch (papyrus strip boundaries and fibre-aligned cracks, 1-3 cm apart) is a measurable orientation signal at level 3 that gives the roll-axis direction (recto strips run around the roll, verso strips along it); a dense fibre field is not measurable, but U2's idea survives at strip scale as a frame cross-check. The images show prominent air cracks, so there is something to skeletonise; it is just the wrong thing (delamination cracks cutting across layers, where the xsec work saw layer jumps), so a crack skeleton yields crack webs, not mini-umbilici.
refuted_claims.fix: Level 4 is the frame and coarse stacking-field scale (keep it); level 3 gives the slit per section; the pitch and sheet counts are measured at level 1 (17 um; period 17-35 voxels) along vertical rays from the slit on sparse cubes, and 'winding number' is reported as a local sheet count from the slit along the stacking direction with its own confidence, never as a level-3 ray-crossing count. Record the strip-direction field as a frame cross-check with a numeric bar (angle to the fitted roll axis <= 15 degrees).

refuted_claims.claim: Compute: 0.5-1 s per level-3 slice, three estimators plus fusion under 1.5 h; level-2 verification on 10 slabs of 64 slices in 10 min; 30 phantoms at 760^3 generated and evaluated in 1-2 min each; same-protocol controls 30-60 min each.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Measured on this hardware: the discarded xy run took ~26 s per 16-slice slab including fetch (1.6 s/slice, with the point model); the live xz run produced its first 4 slabs in ~14 min (~3.5 min per slab in --no_models mode, 1855 x 1519 sections, first chunk-row fetch included). A full pass is 95 y-slabs, i.e. 0.7-5.5 h per estimator per container, not 15-30 min. Level 2 xz sections are 3709 x 3037 (4x the pixels) and a chunk-aligned y-row is 128 x 3709 x 3037 = 1.44 GB; 640 sections cost 1-9 h and ~14 GB of transfer, not 10 min. A 760^3 phantom is 439 M voxels: the generator needs several float32 temporaries of 1.76 GB each (mgrid alone 5.3 GB) and the estimator then runs on 760 sections at the measured per-section cost, so 30 of them are 10-80 CPU-hours, not 1 h; and a phantom at level-4 scale cannot carry 1.4-2.9-voxel sheets, so it tests only plumbing. Level 3 is uncompressed (zarray: compressor null, 128^3 chunks, 4.28 GB) so every re-pass re-streams 4.3 GB unless cached.
refuted_claims.fix: Budget one level-3 pass at 1-6 CPU-h per container and split the 95 y-slabs across the 8 containers by y-range (<= 45 min wall); cache level 3 (4.3 GB) plus level 4 (0.54 GB) in /dev/shm per container life (RAM 4.8 GB + <= 3 GB working set fits in 15 GB) so injection, split-half and smoothing-sensitivity passes do not re-stream; level-2 check on 4 y-rows of 32 sections; phantoms <= 400^3 at level-3 scale and 128-256^3 at level-0/1 scale, <= 10 per frame per sweep, on siblings.

refuted_claims.claim: CHECKPOINT-RESOLUTION-GAP gate: PHerc0009B and PHerc0343P 'both with transform.json'; 4 regions of about 2 mm cube per scroll with 'a few crops'; dinovol 128^3 crops hold about two windings at 2.4 um and seven at 8.64 um; the whole gate runs in under 1 h.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: A 128^3 crop is 0.31 mm at 2.4 um (0.5-1 winding, not two) and 1.1 mm at 8.64 um (2-4 windings, not seven); tiling a 2 mm cube at 2.4 um takes ~275 crops per region, so 'a few crops' and '2 mm regions' are inconsistent and the full-tiling cost is 2200 forward passes x 20-80 s = 12-50 CPU-h, not under 1 h. The transform.json claim for 0009B/0343P is not recorded anywhere in the repo (RULES.md 307-308 records transforms only for 0841, as a 7-landmark affine, and notes 0009B/0343P have no m7 on their 8.64 um volumes), so it is unverified. The gate is also irrelevant to the umbilicus, which no checkpoint drives.
refuted_claims.fix: Defer the gate to the unrolling/ink stage; verify by bucket listing that a transform exists for each pair before scheduling; define the gate as sparse (<= 8 crops per region at matched physical positions, comparing only the ~90 ps8 tokens of the 8.64 um crop that overlap the 2.4 um crop), and state the corrected winding counts.

refuted_claims.claim: Cross-beamline control: 'Scroll 1 / PHerc.Paris.3' on a legacy DLS 7.91 um volume with an organizer-published umbilicus; and (project fact) no organizer umbilicus exists anywhere in the open-data bucket.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Scroll 1 is PHerc. Paris 4 (RULES.md 1165, 2365); Paris 3 is Scroll 2. The repo's own bucket record (logs/p4/recon.json) lists an organizer umbilicus for PHercParis4 on the ESRF 2.4 um volume 20260411134726 (146 control points, z 2252-72960, in 2.4 um voxels) under the EduceLab Data License, which contradicts the 'none anywhere' fact for the bucket as a whole (it remains true for PHerc0268). The umbilicus is defined on the 2.4 um ESRF volume, so a DLS 7.91 um run would need an extra 2.4 um <-> 7.91 um transform and would not be a clean cross-beamline test.
refuted_claims.fix: Run the licence-gated control on Paris 4's 2.4 um volume at level 5 (~77 um, close to 0268 level 3) against that umbilicus divided by 32, parsed by our own code; it is an intact-roll, same-beamline, organizer-referenced control of the point/upright code path only. Record NOT RUN if the licence scope is not granted.

refuted_claims.claim: Same-protocol controls (1451, 0800, 1447, 0841, 0139) passing the self-consistency metrics with frozen parameters 'show the estimator is not tuned to 0268'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Those rolls, to the extent they are upright cylinders about z, exercise the point/upright code path; 0268 exercises the flattened slit path. Passing on upright rolls says nothing about the hairpin/two-focus fit, the stripe guard in xz, or the slit-based winding coordinate. Each control also needs its own frame test first; the proposal assumes their frame.
refuted_claims.fix: Keep the controls for the upright path; for the flattened path the only real-data evidence is 0268 itself (split-half, leave-band-out along y, injection), plus the flattened phantom; say so in the record. Check whether PHerc0490A (already processed by fl4) is a second crushed example before claiming any cross-scroll evidence for the slit path.

refuted_claims.claim: En-Gedi was 'scanned uncarbonised'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The En-Gedi scroll is a charred lump (burned c. 600 CE) scanned at ~18 um on a lab micro-CT; the proposal's own sentence contradicts itself. The strike stands for the stated material reasons (collagen, no lamination, bright metal ink, lab micro-CT), not because it is uncharred.
refuted_claims.fix: Correct the record; keep the strike.

refuted_claims.claim: The phantom generator is frozen and hashed before the estimator runs on 0268, so the phantom cannot be iterated into agreement.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The y-frame run on 0268 started at 18:50 UTC today (logs/umb/PHerc0268/slabs.json, 4 slabs by 19:04) at the same minute DECL-UMB-1-A1 was written, which only declares that the flattened phantom 'is re-run in the new frame'; no METRIC-HASH freeze of the flattened phantom (hairpins, x-stripes, tilt, swirls, two-focus truth) is on record before the run. The rule is already violated in practice unless a freeze record exists.
refuted_claims.fix: Freeze and hash the flattened-roll phantom family (phantom.py --flat --axis y plus stripes and tilt) before any slabs.json from the y-run is read or scored; if the run's records have already been read, the phantom sweep is recorded as post-hoc and cannot count as the M9 bar.

verdict.surviving_core: Data plan: (A) the only data any deployed component is fitted on is PHerc0268 itself (masked 8.64 um CT 20251110183117), streamed from S3 and cached per container life in /dev/shm as level 4 (0.54 GB) plus level 3 (4.28 GB, uncompressed 128^3 chunks); organizer products on the same pyramid (m7 level 3: 1855 x 1519 x 1519, 192^3 zstd chunks; lasagna = cos at level 1 and grad_mag/nx/ny at level 2, computed with no umbilicus under a z-axis assumption, no nz channel) enter only as reported cross-checks after a decode audit, never as fusion members. (B) Same-protocol MAY/JULY rolls stream at levels 3-4 as controls of the upright code path only, each after its own frame test. (C) HF checkpoints play no role in the umbilicus; the resolution-gap gate is deferred to the unrolling stage, made sparse, and preceded by verifying that transforms exist. (D) A seeded, hashed computational phantom family in both frames at level-3 scale (<= 400^3) and small level-0/1 cubes, with hairpins, tilt, swirls, shear jumps, delamination, ash fill, debris, tight and cylinder masks, and in the xz frame z-invariant x-stripes instead of rings; it tests code and robustness only, with its non-roles stated. (E) Licence-gated intact-roll control on PHerc. Paris 4 (Scroll 1) at level 5 of its 2.4 um volume against the organizer umbilicus (146 control points), own parser, or NOT RUN. (F) All strikes stand: no En-Gedi bytes, no parchment or vellum, no unreleased raw volumes, no 3-D MAE or nnUNet training, no physical replicas as ground truth, no pooling across protocols, no learned axis regressor, no single silent global spline. Estimator: step 0 is a frame test at level 4 (roll-axis direction from the smallest eigenvector of the coherence-weighted normal outer-product sum, with an eigenvalue-ratio bar and a strip-direction cross-check); for 0268 the sections are xz planes indexed by y. Per section at level 3: column-wise z-median removal (stripes), mask erosion >= 10-12 voxels, debris exclusion, 2-D structure tensor (sigma_d ~1.2, sigma_i 4-5), coherence threshold calibrated on a phase-randomised null of the same slab, split-half odd/even. Per section the primary model is a slit: hairpin voters (normals near +-x in the slit frame) fix two foci by robust line concurrency, flat-face voters fix the slit orientation and stacking direction, the point model is the c < 0.5 mm special case, and multi-slit bands are declared from hairpin residual clusters, not from accumulator peaks. Along y: confidence-weighted Huber-penalised piecewise-smooth foci curves with explicit change points, leave-band-out along y, declared bridging envelopes, and a reported break list. Outputs per section: F1, F2, c, phi, confidence, split-half distance, decoy distances (image centre, mask centroid, stripe foci). The unrolling coordinate is distance to the slit segment along the local stacking direction, with sheet counts measured at level 1 along vertical rays (M5b balance), reported with per-band confidence and never as global absolute winding numbers inside flagged bands. Compute, corrected: one level-3 pass is 95 y-slabs at a measured 0.5-3.5 min per 16-section slab (0.7-5.5 CPU-h per container), split across 8 containers by y-range for under 45 min wall; working set <= 3 GB plus 4.8 GB of /dev/shm cache; level-2 check on 4 y-rows of 32 sections (1-3 h); phantoms <= 10 per frame per sweep on siblings; outputs are JSON and PNG under 1 MB each.
verdict.missing_validation: (1) A frame test with a numeric bar is absent entirely: level-4 3-D structure tensor over coherent voxels, roll-axis direction = smallest eigenvector of sum(c n n^T), bar smallest/middle eigenvalue <= 0.5 and angle to the chosen slicing axis <= 15 degrees, cross-checked by the face-on strip/crack direction field (angle to the fitted axis <= 15 degrees); the same test must be run on every control scroll and on a phantom written in the wrong frame, which must fail it. (2) A null test: a phase-randomised slab and an xy section of 0268 must yield confidence 0 and no focus; the proposal's q ratio has no null calibration. (3) A two-focus recovery test on the flattened phantom (phantom.py --flat --axis y with hairpins, tilt up to 15 degrees, swirls, z-invariant x-stripes, tight and cylinder masks): foci within 0.3 mm over >= 90 % of y, slit length within 20 %, and no spurious 'multi-slit' on single-roll sections; frozen and hashed before any y-run record is read. (4) A stripe decoy test on real sections: foci computed from the stripe map alone must lie > 1 mm from the accepted foci. (5) An edge-leak test: fraction of admissible voters within 1 mm of the mask edge < 1 % at the chosen erosion. (6) Split-half (odd/even y-sections) as the per-section noise floor for every number reported, and leave-band-out along y rather than z. (7) A fine-scale check of the slit coordinate: at level 1 along vertical rays from 5 slit points, sheet-crossing balance (M5b) and a measured pitch distribution; without it 'winding number per voxel' has no validation on 0268 and must not be claimed. (8) A decode audit of the lasagna uint8 encoding and of m7's pyramid pooling before either is cited as a cross-check, with 'not computable' as the recorded outcome if nz cannot be recovered with sign. (9) Verification by bucket listing that a 2.4 um <-> 8.64 um transform exists for PHerc0009B and PHerc0343P before the checkpoint gate is scheduled, and a corrected sparse definition of that gate. (10) Licence-scope confirmation for the Paris 4 umbilicus control, recorded NOT RUN otherwise. (11) A timing record per slab (already emitted by st_axis.py) so compute claims are measured, not asserted: the first four xz slabs took ~3.5 min each, which the proposal's 0.5-1 s per slice does not survive.
